Instagram Help Guide

Instagram’s official help, gathered into one screen-reader-friendly document

2026-07-29

Instagram Help Guide

This guide gathers Instagram’s official help: setting up and using your account, posting photos, reels and stories, messaging, following and blocking, privacy and reporting, teen accounts and parental supervision, professional accounts and advertising, Meta AI on Instagram, the policies, and fixing problems. It was taken from Instagram’s own help centre on 28 July 2026.

Instagram runs as an app on iPhone and Android and in a web browser at instagram.com. There is no Windows program and no Alexa skill.

This is one of the largest volumes in the collection, and the reason is Instagram: its help centre runs to more than a thousand articles, many of them a few lines long, covering features that come and go. Everything gathered is here rather than a selection, because a guide that quietly drops articles is worse than a long one.

The sections below are mine, not Instagram’s. Instagram numbers its articles and shows the same category list on every page, so nothing survives being taken out of the site; the grouping here is by subject and that choice is my own. Where an article could sit in two places, the first matching rule won — so accessibility articles are gathered first and together, since they are the ones most likely to be wanted.

Two things about the source. Instagram publishes some articles that are only a heading and a sentence pointing elsewhere; those with almost nothing in them are left out, and the count is stated in the log rather than hidden. And each article ends with a feedback prompt and a list of related links, which have been cut — they are furniture, not help.

Headings run three deep: this title, then a section, then an article, with each article’s own subheadings nested beneath. Every article is listed in the table of contents below.

Add a caption to your post
  1. Click Create on the left, then click Post.
  2. Choose a photo or video from your computer’s library.
  3. Click Next in the top right. You can also add filters (for a photo) or edit a cover photo and trim (for a video).
  4. Click Next again, and then click Write a caption…
  5. Click Share.

  1. Click Options in the top right of your post.

Turn off translations

Turn off translations for all

Turn off translations for one

I have a different question

You can disable translations and read the caption on the Captions sticker in its original language.

Turn off translations for a single reel
  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Find the reel you want to turn off translations for.
  3. Tap Options.
  4. Tap Translations.
  5. Toggle off Translate text on reels.
Turn off translations for all reels
  1. Open in the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.

How do I secure my account?

I have a different question

If your Threads profile was disabled, you’ll see a message telling you when you try to log in. Accounts that don’t follow our Community Standards may be disabled.

In certain regions, we may disable profiles for people in a specific age range in accordance with local laws and regulations. Your account will no longer be visible to others once it’s disabled.

Troubleshoot a disabled account

If you think your profile was disabled by mistake, you may be able to ask us to review the decision by opening the app, entering your username and password and following the on-screen instructions.

If you don’t see a disabled message, you may be experiencing a login issue. If your profile was deleted by you or someone with your password, there’s no way to restore it. You can create a new profile with the same email address you used before, but you may not be able to get the same username.

If someone gained access to your profile or you’re unable to log in to your profile, visit this page on your desktop or mobile browser to secure your account.

About Meta Verified for creators

What are Meta Verified benefits?

How do I subscribe to Meta Verified?

What are the eligibility requirements?

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Instagram and Facebook.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

Meta Verified for creators is a paid subscription that provides tools to help you build more confidence with new audiences and protect your brand. This subscription comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

Automatic renewal

Meta Verified subscriptions are billed on a recurring basis and renew automatically, unless canceled. You will be charged on the same date as your original purchase, until you cancel.

Learn more about payments for Meta Verified creator subscriptions.

Subscription plans & benefits

We offer several subscription plans for creators. Plans, benefits, and availability may vary by region, by app, and by account. To see the specific features available to your account, please start the subscription process.

[TABLE]

Learn more about Meta Verified subscription benefits.

Note: Meta Verified creator subscriptions are only available for eligible subscribers. Subscription plans and benefits listed may not be available to all regions or creators.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta Verified.

Eligibility

To purchase a Meta Verified subscription, you need to meet the eligibility requirements.

The following accounts are eligible for Meta Verified:

  • Instagram professional creator account
  • Instagram personal account
  • Facebook professional creator account
  • Facebook personal account

You can verify up to two eligible profiles that are added to the same Accounts Center:

  • One Instagram account and one Facebook account
Verification process

When you subscribe to Meta Verified, you’ll follow a verification process and submit an application for review.

You’ll choose a subscription plan, select the profile(s) you want to verify, set up your recurring subscription payment, and confirm your identity.

Step 1. Choose your profile

You’ll choose the profile(s) you want to verify and set up your recurring subscription payment.

You can verify up to two eligible profiles that are added to the same Accounts Center.

When you bundle your subscription and verify two profiles instead of one (example: one Instagram account and one Facebook account), you may receive a discounted price. Both profiles may need to have similar names and pictures.

Note: Advanced Protection needs to be enabled on the profile(s) you’re verifying. This security feature can’t be disabled once your subscription is active.

Step 2. Confirm your identity

You’ll confirm your identity.

To confirm your identity, you’ll need to upload photos of a government-issued photo ID.

Note: If eligible, you may be verified using your activity across Meta products, such as name tenure and profile completeness including name and picture.

Step 3. Get reviewed

You’ll submit your information for review.

Once you complete the application process and submit your information, it’ll go into review. After review, you’ll get a notification with an update on your verification status. This process can take up to 3 business days.

Learn how to troubleshoot issues when subscribing to Meta Verified.

After you’re verified

If your application is approved, your subscription will become active and your selected profile(s) will be verified. You’ll get access to the Meta Verified benefits associated with your subscription plan.

Learn how to manage and make changes to your subscription:

  • View subscription details
  • Update subscription payment method
  • View subscription payment history
  • Change subscription plan
  • Contact Meta Verified support
  • Cancel subscription
Important information
  • Subscribers must agree to the Meta Verified Terms of Service and follow our Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.
  • If you provide false or misleading information during the verification process, Meta may prevent your profile from being verified, remove your verified status, or take additional action on the account.
  • After successfully subscribing to Meta Verified, certain activity may result in Meta’s revocation of your subscription due to integrity concerns and potential fraud risk.

Visit the Meta Verified for creators Help Center.

When you block someone, they won’t be able to see anything you post on Threads. People aren’t notified when you block them.

There are multiple ways to block or unblock someone on Threads.

Block or unblock a profile

Click an option below to learn more.

Through feed:

Through their profile:

You can also unblock someone by clicking Unblock below the number of followers on their profile.

What happens when you block someone on Threads

When you block someone:

  • Their likes will be removed from your posts. Unblocking someone won’t restore their previous likes.
  • They won’t be able to see your replies or any content you repost.
  • Their replies to your posts can’t be seen by others.
  • They won’t be able to mention your username or tag you, even if you change your username.
  • They won’t be able to message you.
  • If you’re in a group chat with someone you’ve blocked, you’ll get a dialog asking whether you want to stay in the group or leave. If you choose to stay in the group, you and the blocked person will be able to see each other’s messages in the group.
  • They won’t be able to find your profile or content on Threads.

Branded content is content for which the creator has been compensated, either with money or something else of value, by a brand or business partner. This may include when products and services have been gifted for free. Learn more about branded content on Instagram

All branded content must be disclosed using the paid partnership label. You can review what content is considered branded content and when you need to use the paid partnership label.

As an Instagram creator, you can request access to the paid partnership label to allow you to share branded content. You can disclose your partnerships with brands in Feed, Stories, Live, Reels and Instagram videos. Note: Adding the paid partnership label is only available on the Instagram app.

Before you begin

To be eligible for branded content tools on Instagram, you must:

  • Comply with our Branded Content Policies
  • Meet our eligibility requirements for Instagram branded content.
  • Remain compliant with our Community Standards and Content Monetization Policies.

These requirements help Instagram maintain the integrity of branded content partnerships.

How to access the paid partnership label on Instagram

To enable branded content tools, including the paid partnership label:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Business tools and controls or Creator tools and controls.
  4. Tap Branded content.
  5. Tap Set up branded content tools.
  6. If you are eligible for branded content tools, tap Enable.
Get started with branded content on Instagram

After setting up branded content, you can:

  • Learn how to use the paid partnership label to tag organic branded content on Instagram. Note: You must do this every time you post branded content.
  • Join Instagram’s creator marketplace to help brands discover you for branded content partnerships.
  • Add your interests so brands can understand the type of content you like to create.

Remember, it is up to you to discuss the terms of branded content with brand partners. You can message the brand with questions about the project, or to discuss payments, the content to create, or the date to post.

Boost your brand’s impact now by learning how to sharpen your branded content game! Read more.

You can also request help with monetization, including branded content tools, on the Instagram app.

How Avatar AutoGen Works

How AutoGen works

What information is used?

How long is data kept?

I have a different question

The Avatar autogenerate feature (“AutoGen”) enables us (Meta Platforms, Inc., “we”, “us” or “our”) to quickly recommend avatars to you that more closely match your facial appearance using a video recording of yourself (“Selfie”) that you submit. This Avatar AutoGen Privacy Article applies to our processing of your information in connection with generating recommended avatars via AutoGen.

Information we use and retain to provide the AutoGen feature

In order to recommend avatars inspired by your appearance, our software analyzes your Selfie to estimate the location of parts of your face, like your eyes, nose and mouth, and specific points on the contours of those parts of your face (collectively, “estimated facial points”). Our software also analyzes your Selfie to detect the approximate size, shape and color pigment of certain features (collectively, “predicted facial attributes”). We then use the estimated facial points and predicted facial attributes together to suggest avatars that look more like you (“recommended avatars”). If you choose to, you can use the avatar editor to customize the recommended avatars, such as by adjusting the recommended hairstyle, before selecting your final avatar. None of your Selfie, estimated facial points, predicted facial attributes, and recommended avatars will be used for any purpose other than to generate your recommended or final avatars and none of this information is used to identify you.

After you select your final avatar, we will delete your estimated facial points within 14 days, and use your recommended avatars, predicted facial attributes and any customizations you make to understand how well Autogen worked for you and how we can further improve it. Your recommended avatars and predicted facial attributes will be disassociated from your account immediately and deleted within 90 days.

We will store your final avatar so that you can use it for interactive digital experiences across our services. Once your final avatar has been created, you can delete it at any time by clicking the trashcan icon in your Avatar Editor settings. Your final avatar will also be deleted if you delete your account. Once you delete your final avatar (or account), we no longer store this data.

Other information we use

Consistent with our Privacy Policy, we also collect other information in connection with your use of the avatar editing tools (e.g., whether you used one of our recommended hairstyles or used our editing tools to choose another hairstyle for your final avatar). We use this other information–which does not include your Selfie, estimated facial points, predicted facial attributes, recommended avatars, or final avatar–to troubleshoot, diagnose and fix problems that you may have in using the avatar editing tools, as described in our Privacy Policy. This other information will be deleted when we no longer need it to provide or improve the avatar editing tools.

We do not share this information

We do not share any of the information described in this article, including your Selfie, estimated facial points, predicted facial attributes, recommended avatars, or final avatar, with third parties.

How Instant Avatar AutoGen Open Beta Works

How Instant Avatar works

What data is used?

Delete my Instant Avatar

I can’t use Instant Avatar

I have a different question

This Instant Avatar AutoGen Open Beta Article explains how the Instant Avatar autogenerate feature (“Instant Avatar AutoGen”), where available, works and how Meta processes Instant Avatar Autogen data. The Instant Avatar AutoGen feature enables Meta Platforms, Inc. (“we”, “us” or “our”) to quickly recommend avatars to you that more closely match your appearance using one of your existing public profile photos.

Information we use to provide the Instant Avatar AutoGen feature

In order to recommend avatars inspired by your appearance, we select one or more of your public profile photos based on photo quality factors designed to identify a good photo for the Instant Avatar AutoGen service, such as whether the photos is a close-up, shows a front-facing subjects, or depicts only one person. The selected public profile photo (“Profile Photo”) will be used to generate your recommended avatar.

In order to recommend avatars inspired by your appearance, our software analyzes your Profile Photo to estimate the location of parts of your face, like your eyes, nose and mouth, and specific points on the contours of those parts of your face (collectively, “estimated facial points”). Our software also analyzes your Profile Photo to detect the shape and color pigment of certain areas of your face (collectively, “predicted facial attributes”). Depending upon your head pose, our software may also adjust the position of your face to produce a forward facing image (“frontalization”). None of this information is used to identify you.

We then use the estimated facial points, predicted facial attributes, and frontalization together to suggest an avatar that looks more like you (“recommended avatar”).

You are able to choose from a selection of standard body shape options for your avatar. To select which standard body shape options to present to you, we consider certain selections you may have made in your profile information, such as gender. Regardless of the options presented to you, you may choose to manually select any available body shape option for your avatar before finalizing.

You may be able to choose from a selection of clothing options for your avatar. We may consider certain selections you have made in your profile information, such as gender, the shape and style of clothing visible in your Profile Photo, and the predictions made on your Profile Photo to generate your recommended avatar in order to suggest clothing, accessory, and makeup options for your avatar. For example, if your Profile Photo is used to suggest a certain hairstyle for your recommended avatar, you may see suggestions for certain kinds of headwear. Suggested clothing options may be selected from clothing assets available in the avatars store (such clothing assets may be subject to additional terms and conditions though no payment is required for clothing assets we recommend to you in Instant Avatar AutoGen). If you choose to, you can then use the avatar editor to further customize your recommended avatar before finalizing your avatar.

After you select your final avatar, we will delete your estimated facial points within 14 days, but we use your recommended avatars, predicted facial attributes and any customizations you make to understand how well Instant Avatar Autogen worked for you and how we can further improve it. Your recommended avatars and predicted facial attributes will be disassociated from your account immediately and deleted within 90 days.

We will store your final avatar so that you can use it for interactive digital experiences across our services. You can edit your final avatar at any time using the avatar editor located via your “Edit Profile” option on your Instagram Profile. You can also delete your final avatar at any time by clicking the trashcan icon in your avatar editor settings. Your final avatar will also be deleted if you delete your account. Once you delete your final avatar (or account), we no longer store this data.

For more information about how we process your data, see Meta Privacy Policy.

How to keep your Threads profile secure

How do I use security features?

How do I report scammers?

How do I turn on two-factor authentication?

How do I create a strong password?

I have a different question

You can use the following tools to help keep your profile secure when you use Threads.

Use security features
  • Turn on two-factor authentication for more account security.
  • If you’ve created a Threads profile with an Instagram account, turn on login requests to receive alerts whenever someone tries to access your account.
  • Revoke access to any suspicious third-party apps.
  • Create a strong password with a combination of at least six numbers, letters, and special characters to avoid repetition. Change your password regularly.
Never share your information
  • Never share your password.
  • Log out of your profile when using a computer you share with other people.
Report scammers and suspicious activity
  • Watch out for common scams, similar to those that can also appear on apps like Instagram.
  • Report threads that don’t follow our Community Standards.
  • Report Threads profiles that impersonate you.
  • Report suspicious emails to phish@meta.com.
  • Don’t click any suspicious links or attachments in threads.

Note: Meta will never send you direct messages about your account in our apps. Official messages about account security will only be sent to your email address.

Yoti, a third party age verification service uses a variety of options for people to verify their age on Instagram, allowing us to provide age-appropriate experiences. Yoti is verified by the Age Check Certification Scheme and is the leading age verification provider for several industries around the world including social media, gaming and age restricted e-commerce.

With Yoti, there are a few different ways you can choose to verify your age:

  • Upload an ID

Types of ID that Yoti uses to verify your age

The ID you choose must include a photo of your face and your birth date.

  • Passport
  • Drivers license

How to use your ID to verify your age

If you choose to use your ID to confirm your age, you will need to allow Instagram to have access to your camera.

To capture your photo, you should lay your ID on a flat surface, avoid glare or shadows, and center your ID. Once your ID is scanned, you can submit the photo of it for review, or you can retake the photo.

Depending on the laws in your region, you may also be required to get parental approval if we determine you’re under a certain age.

My account was hacked

Recover my account

Someone using my account

Check what was accessed

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you think your account has been hacked or taken over, there are several actions you may be able to take via the website or the app to secure your account. If someone gains access to your account or you’re unable to log in, visit this page on your desktop or mobile browser to secure your account.

You can also try the recovery steps below. Some of these recovery steps may not be available to you depending on the type of account you’re trying to recover, but we recommend trying them all.

Check your email account for a message from Instagram

If you received an email from security@mail.instagram.com letting you know that your email address was changed, you may be able to undo this change by selecting secure my account in that message. If additional information was also changed (example: your password), and you’re unable to change back your email address, request a login link or security code from Instagram

Request a login link from Instagram

To help us confirm that you own the account, you can request that we send a login link to your email address or phone number.

To request a login link:

  1. On the login screen, tap Forgot password?
  2. Enter the username, email address, or phone number associated with your account, then click Send login link. Note: If you don’t have access to the username, email address, or phone number associated with your account, visit this page and follow the on-screen instructions.
  3. Complete the captcha to confirm that you are a real human, then click Next.
  4. Click the login link in your email or a text message (SMS) and follow the on-screen instructions.
Request a security code or support from Instagram

If you’re unable to recover your account with the login link we sent to you, you may be able to request support from us on a mobile device.

To request support from Instagram:

Be sure to enter a secure email address that only you can access. Once you’ve submitted your request, you should receive an email from Instagram with next steps.

Learn more about what you can do if you don’t know your username.

Verify your identity

If you submitted a support request for an account without photos of you, you should receive an auto-response email from the Support Team at Meta. We’ll ask you to help us verify your identity by providing the email address or phone number you signed up with and the type of device you used at the time of sign up (example: iPhone, Android, iPad, other).

If you request support for an account with photos of you, you’ll be asked to take a video selfie of you turning your head in different directions to help us check that you’re a real person and confirm your identity.

Once you submit the video selfie to help us verify your identity, you’ll receive an email from Instagram at the secure email address you provided. We use this video to ensure you are a real person and that you are who you say you are.

Keep in mind that the video you submit will never be visible on Instagram and will be deleted within 30 days.

If we weren’t able to confirm your identity from the video you submitted, you can submit a new video and we’ll review it again.

If you’re still able to log into your Instagram account

If you think your account has been hacked or an attempt to hack your account has been made and you’re still able to log in, there are things you can do to help keep your account secure:

  • Change your password or send yourself a password reset email.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication for additional security.
  • Confirm your phone number and email address in account settings are correct.
  • Check Accounts Center and remove any linked accounts you don’t recognize.
  • Revoke access to any suspicious third-party apps.
  • Learn more about what you can do if your Instagram account is a professional account and you’re able to log in, but a hacker is still taking actions on your account.

If you’re still having trouble accessing your account, we’d like to hear more about your experience so we can continue to improve our support options.

Use our security tips and tricks to double up on security.

What are data logs?

How long do data logs take?

I have a different question

When you Download your information from Instagram, you have options on how much information you want to download.

The two options are Available information and Specific types of information.

  • Available information are files that include information and activity for the accounts and profiles you selected but won’t include data logs.
  • Specific types of information includes all of the files in Available information as well as data logs. This selection also allows you to select only certain types of information for download, such as photos, messages or data logs.
Data logs

Data logs are additional details we collect and store that can be associated with you. This data can be unique but it can also be additional details about information already provided in your profile and account downloads. It can include things like:

  • Your logged interactions, including things you’ve viewed or clicked on
  • Information that supports the use of Facebook, such as device information third party apps or websites you have logged into using your Instagram login.

If you’d like to download data logs, select Specific types of information when you are downloading your informationfrom your main profile.

Data logs will be a separate download from your profile information because they take longer to prepare. You will get a notification when they are ready to download. It may take up to 15 days to get data logs. They won’t delay the other information you request, which is typically ready in a few hours.

You cannot subscribe to Meta Verified directly on Threads.

To get a verified badge on Threads, you first need to subscribe to Meta Verified on Instagram. After you subscribe, make sure your Threads account is added to the same Accounts Center as your verified Instagram account. Accounts Center is where you can manage your connected Meta accounts, like Instagram and Threads.

If you have an active Meta Verified subscription on Instagram, and your Threads account is connected in the same Accounts Center, your verified badge will automatically appear on Threads.

Note: Threads in Accounts Center is slowly rolling out and isn’t available everywhere.

Only the verified badge will show on Threads. Other Meta Verified benefits, such as enhanced support and impersonation protection, are not available Threads.

Editing your Threads profile

If you are subscribed to Meta Verified on Instagram and your Threads account is connected in the same Accounts Center, there are some limitations to editing your Threads profile.

Profile picture

You can’t change your profile picture directly on Threads. Your picture is automatically carried over from your verified Instagram account and will match your Instagram profile.

If you want to change your profile picture, you need to change it on Instagram. Any changes you make to your Instagram profile picture will also update your picture on Threads.

Profile name and username

You can update your profile name and username for Threads directly in Accounts Center. However, your Threads profile name and username need to match your verified Instagram account. If they don’t match, you will lose your verified badge on Threads.

Reasons you may lose your verified badge on Threads

There are several situations where your verified badge on Threads may be removed:

  • Deleting your verified Instagram account: Your Meta Verified subscription will be canceled and your verified badge will be removed from Threads.
  • Moving accounts out of an Accounts Center: If you move either your verified Instagram account or Threads account out of the same Accounts Center, you will lose your verified badge.
  • Updating your Threads profile information: If you change your profile name or username on Threads so it no longer matches your verified Instagram account, you will lose your verified badge. Your Threads profile info needs to match your verified Instagram account for you to keep the badge.
  • Subscription issues: If your Meta Verified subscription is revoked or canceled, your badge will be removed from Threads. Learn more about revoked Meta Verified subscriptions.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

You can permanently delete your Instagram profile from your phone or computer.

Export your information

Before deleting your profile, you may want to log in and export a copy of your information (like your photos and posts) from Instagram. After your profile has been deleted, you will not have access to Instagram’s Export your information tool.

When you delete your profile, your profile, photos, videos, comments, likes and followers will be permanently removed. If you’d just like to take a break, you can temporarily deactivate your profile instead.

Permanently delete your account from Accounts Center

If you see Manage accounts at the bottom of Accounts Center:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Accounts Center, then click Profiles and personal details.
  3. Click Manage next to the account type you want to delete.
  4. Click Deactivation or deletion.
  5. Click the account you’d like to permanently delete.
  6. Click Delete account, then click Continue.

If you see Accounts at the bottom of Accounts Center:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Accounts Center at the top left of your screen.
  3. Click Personal details, under Account Settings.
  4. Click Account ownership and control.
  5. Click Deactivation or deletion.
  6. Choose the account or profile you want to delete.
  7. Select Delete account.
  8. Click Continue then follow the instructions to confirm.
Sign up again to get back on Instagram

After your profile is deleted, you can sign up again with the same username or add that username to another profile as long as it hasn’t been taken by a new person on Instagram.

After 30 days of your profile deletion request, your profile and all your information will be permanently deleted, and you won’t be able to retrieve your information. During those 30 days the content remains subject to Instagram’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy and is not accessible to other people using Instagram.

Note: The number of days that you can cancel an account deletion varies by region.

Deletion can take up to 90 days

It may take up to 90 days to complete the deletion process after it begins. Copies of your content may remain after the 90 days in backup storage that we use to recover in the event of a disaster, software error, or other data loss event. We may also keep your information for things like legal issues, terms violations, or harm prevention efforts. Learn more about this in our Privacy Policy.

If your profile is removed for violating Community Standards, you may not be able to sign up again with the same username.

Why Instagram can’t delete a profile for you

For security reasons, we can’t delete a profile for you. You’ll need to be able to log into your profile to request deletion. If you can’t remember your password or username, see some tips for logging in.

Refund eligibility

Request a refund

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Instagram and Facebook.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

Refunds for Meta Verified subscriptions are only available if you meet the eligibility criteria.

Refund eligibility

Refunds are available if:

  • You did not complete the verification process within 3 days of starting it.
  • Meta could not verify your identity during the review process.

Refunds are not available if:

  • You cancel your subscription after completing verification and being approved.
  • You cancel your subscription during your current billing cycle.
  • You cancel your subscription and choose to immediately cancel your benefits.
  • Your account violates the Meta Verified Terms of Service, Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, or Community Standards.
  • You provide false or misleading information during verification.
  • Your subscription is revoked because your account is no longer eligible for Meta Verified.
  • Your subscription is revoked due to integrity concerns or potential fraud.

Meta does not offer any credits or partial refunds for canceled Meta Verified subscriptions.

Note: Refund eligibility may vary by region due to local laws.

Refund process

Your refund process depends on where you purchased your Meta Verified subscription:

  • If you purchased directly through Instagram or Facebook on a computer, your refund is processed automatically by Meta.
  • If you purchased through Apple, Apple’s policies only allow you to request a refund through the Apple App Store.
  • If you purchased through Google, Google’s policies only allow you to request a refund through the Google Play Store.

Refunds are returned to the original payment method used to purchase your subscription. Refunds may take several business days to appear. In some cases, it can take up to 60 days, depending on your bank or payment provider.

Troubleshooting tips

If you haven’t received a refund, it may be due to one of the following reasons:

  • Refund in progress. Refunds may take several business days, and in some cases up to 60 days, depending on your bank or payment provider. This is especially common for Apple App Store purchases.
  • Refund eligibility. You may not be eligible for a refund. Review the eligibility criteria in this article.
  • Payment method. Make sure you’re checking the correct account or card that was used for the original payment.
  • Purchase platform. If you purchased through Apple or Google, you need to request your refund through the Apple App Store or Google Play Store.
  • Pending or failed payment. If your payment is still pending or has failed, your refund may not be processed until the payment is completed or canceled.

Note: Meta does not offer any credits or partial refunds for canceled Meta Verified subscriptions.

If you have an Instagram account, you can report a profile or content on Instagram that doesn’t follow our Community Standards.

Currently, you can report a post for any of the following reasons:

  • I just don’t like it
  • Bullying or unwanted contact
  • Suicide, self-injury or eating disorders
  • Violence, hate or exploitation
  • Selling or promoting restricted items
  • Nudity or sexual activity
  • Scam, fraud or spam
  • False information
  • Intellectual property

You can also report a profile for posting content it shouldn’t be, pretending to be someone else, or for being a child under the age of 13. Learn how to report a comment or how to report a message.

Keep in mind that your report is anonymous, except if you’re reporting an intellectual property infringement. The account you reported won’t see who reported them.

Report a post through Feed
  1. Click Options in the top right of the post.
  2. Select Report and follow the on-screen instructions.
Report someone through their profile
  1. Click their username from their Feed or story post, or click Explore and search their username to go to their profile.
  2. Click Options next to their username.
  3. Select Report, then select the type of account you want to report and follow the on-screen instructions.

If you don’t have an Instagram account, you can report abuse, spam or anything else that doesn’t follow our Community Standards.

After you report something on Instagram, you may be able to check the status of your report. Even if we don’t remove the content or profile you reported, we understand that you likely want to see less of this type of content on Instagram. We may use your report to make content similar to what you reported appear lower in your feed or in the recommendations we make for you, like Suggested Posts and Explore.

Learn more about what you can do if you don’t agree with Instagram’s decision about content you reported.

Requirements to apply for a verified badge on Instagram

Apply for verified badge

What are verification requirements?

My account was rejected

I have a different question

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity, while others are subscribed to Meta Verified.

  • Verified badges mean an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid subscription that comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

If you already have an existing verified badge based on prior requirements, you can still subscribe to Meta Verified.

There are two ways to get the verified badge

  1. Subscribe to Meta Verified. Learn more about the eligibility criteria.
  2. Apply for the verified badge if you are a public figure, celebrity or brand and meet the account and eligibility requirements outlined below.

For accounts not subscribed to Meta Verified, we look at a number of factors when evaluating Instagram accounts to determine if they meet our verification criteria.

In addition to following Instagram’s Terms of Use and Community Standards, your account also needs to be:

  • Authentic: Represent a real person, registered business or entity.
  • Unique: Represent the unique presence of the person or business. Only one account per person or business may be verified, with exceptions for language-specific accounts. We don’t verify general interest accounts (example: @puppymemes).
  • Complete: Your account must be public and have a bio, profile photo and be active when you apply.
  • Notable: Your account must represent a well-known, highly searched for person, brand or entity. We review accounts that are featured in multiple news sources, and we don’t consider paid or sponsored media content as sources for review.

Learn more about how to apply for a verified badge if you meet the above account and eligibility requirements.

Note

  • Make sure your username is what you’d like it to be before you apply for a verified badge. Once verified, you may not change the username on your account.
  • If you receive a verified badge using false or misleading information during the verification process, we will remove your verified badge and may take additional action to disable your account.

If your account is verified by Instagram for notability, you may want to enable additional security tools like two-factor authentication. Learn about other security tips on Instagram.

Revoked Meta Verified creator subscriptions

My subscription was revoked

Why was my subscription canceled?

My payment failed

I lost my benefits

I have a different question

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Instagram and Facebook.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

When your Meta Verified subscription gets revoked, you immediately lose all subscription benefits. This is different from canceling your subscription, where you typically have access to benefits until the end of your current billing cycle.

There are several reasons why Meta Verified subscriptions may get revoked or unexpectedly canceled.

Common reasons for revocation

Payment issues

Your subscription will be canceled if your payment method fails and there is no backup payment method on file. We recommend adding a backup payment method so that if your default payment fails for any reason, your backup payment will be charged to keep your subscription active.

Learn how to update your payment method for Meta Verified.

Verification failure

If your verification doesn’t pass the review process after submitting your first payment, your subscription will be canceled and you’ll be eligible for a refund.

Learn about refunds for Meta Verified creator subscriptions.

Profile updates

If you update your verified profile information and your changes aren’t approved because they violate our policies, your subscription may be revoked.

Policy violations

If your verified account violates our policies, your subscription will be revoked. Subscribers must agree to the Meta Verified Terms of Service and follow our Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.

Account deletion

If you delete your verified account, your subscription will be canceled.

Account removed from bundle

If you remove one of your verified accounts from an existing subscription bundle, your subscription will be revoked after 7 days or at the end of your current billing cycle – whichever comes first. If you re-subscribe that account to the same bundle within this period, your subscription will stay active.

Change in account type

If you switch your Instagram account type from business to personal, your subscription will be revoked after 7 days or at the end of your current billing cycle – whichever comes first. If you switch back to a business account within this period, your subscription will stay active. Make sure you’re still connected to the same business you originally purchased the subscription for.

Change in eligibility

If you no longer meet the eligibility requirements (example: moving to a location where Meta Verified is not available), your subscription will be canceled.

Learn more about Meta Verified eligibility requirements for creators.

App store changes

If you make changes to your subscription directly through the Apple App Store or Google Play Store (example: changing your plan), your subscription may be revoked.

Learn how to manage your Meta Verified subscription.

What happens if your subscription is revoked

If your subscription gets revoked, we will attempt to notify you via email and in-app notification.

You’ll immediately lose access to all Meta Verified subscription benefits (this includes support and any open cases with the support team). Revocation is different from canceling your subscription, where you typically have access to benefits until the end of your current billing cycle.

If you want to re-apply for Meta Verified, we recommend making sure your account meets the eligibility requirements and follows our policies. You may need to make updates to your account or payments before signing up again.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta Verified.

What happens if I sync?

Unsync my profile information

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

After your accounts are added to the same Accounts Center, you can choose to sync your name, profile picture, username and/or avatar across your Facebook, Instagram and/or Meta Horizon profiles. Syncing your profile information allows you to make updates across your profiles simultaneously. You can also create new profiles using information from your other existing profiles.

You don’t have to sync your profile information with another account to sign up for Facebook or Instagram. You can choose whether to sync your profile picture, username and/or avatar across your profiles, but in order to sync profile information you need to sync your name.

If you choose to sync your profile information, you can decide to unsync it later.

What it means to sync your profile information:
  • If you sync profile information across your Facebook, Instagram or Meta Horizon profiles, changes you make to your profile information (such as your name, username, profile picture and avatar) will appear across all of your profiles with synced info. For example, when you change your avatar on Facebook or Instagram, it will change for both profiles.
  • If you remove an account from an Accounts Center, your profile info for profiles in that account will no longer sync.
  • You can’t sync information from one profile to another between profiles on the same app (for example, you can’t sync two Instagram profiles, two Facebook profiles, or two Meta Horizon profiles).
Sync your name, username, profile picture and/or avatar across your profiles
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. On the left, click Accounts Center.
  3. Below Profiles, click Facebook or Instagram profile you want to sync, then click your profile’s name again at the bottom.
  4. Click Toggle next to Sync profile info to turn name and profile picture syncing off or on.
  5. If you have more than 2 profiles, first choose which profile you want to sync with.
  6. Click Manage your sync settings to choose to sync your name or your name and profile picture. To use a different profile picture:
    1. Click Profile picture, then click Edit profile picture.
    2. Click the circle next to the account that you’d like to use for your profile picture.
    3. Click Confirm.
  7. Click Sync profile info.
Sync your name
  • Before you can sync your profile picture, username or avatar, you need to sync your name. This means that:
    • When you sync your name, your name will become the same across all of the profiles you’ve chosen to sync.
    • People will be able to see and search for you with this name on the apps (Facebook, Instagram and/or Meta Horizon) where you’ve chosen to sync profile information.
    • People may also see suggestions (like to add you as a friend or to follow you) associated with this name on the apps (Facebook, Instagram and/or Meta Horizon) where you’ve chosen to sync profile information.
Sync your profile picture
  • If you choose to sync your profile picture, your picture will become the same across all of the profiles you’ve chosen to sync.
  • Note that your previous Instagram profile pictures are not saved. If you choose to sync your profile picture (and use a Facebook profile picture for your Facebook and Instagram accounts) if you turn off profile syncing, your previous Instagram profile picture will not appear.
Sync your username
  • If you choose to sync your username, your username will become the same across all of the profiles you’ve chosen to sync. This means:
    • People will be able to see and search for you with this username on the apps (Facebook, Instagram and/or Meta Horizon) where you’ve chosen to sync profile information.
    • People may also see suggestions (like to add you as a friend or to follow you) associated with this username on the apps (Facebook, Instagram and/or Meta Horizon) where you’ve chosen to sync profile information.
  • To sync your usernames, the username you choose must be available on each app.
Sync your avatar

When you sync your avatar, you can choose to use either your Facebook or Instagram avatar across your profiles. The default avatar will be the avatar from the app you’re currently using.

  • You haven’t exceeded the number of times you can update your profile info (listed in this article).
  • You don’t already have pending profile updates that are in review. (This process can take up to 3 days.)

If you have trouble updating your verified profile info, please contact Meta Verified Support.

Learn how to contact Meta Verified Support.

Visit the Meta Verified for creators Help Center.

Verified badges on Instagram

What is a verified badge?

How do I get verified?

Why was my badge removed?

I have a different question

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity, while others are subscribed to Meta Verified.

  • Verified badges mean an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid subscription that comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

If you already have an existing verified badge based on prior requirements, you can still subscribe to Meta Verified.

The verified badge means an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.

An Instagram account with a verified badge next to its name now means that Instagram has confirmed that it is the authentic presence for that person or brand. Previously, the verified badge also required the person or brand to be notable and unique. You may still see users with a verified badge that represents our previous eligibility requirements.

The verified badge is a tool to help people find the real accounts of people and brands. If an account has the verified badge, we’ve confirmed that it represents who it says it does. A verified badge is not a symbol to show importance, authority or subject matter expertise. We don’t use the verified badge to endorse or recognize public figures or brands.

Once verified, public figures, celebrities and brands that meet certain account and eligibility requirements may not change their username on their account. Verification cannot be transferred to a different account. Instagram accounts that impersonate public figures or other people go against our Community Standards and aren’t allowed on Instagram.

Note: While many public figures verify their account on Instagram, not all public figures have verified badges . As we test and learn, there will be no immediate changes to accounts on Instagram or Facebook that are already verified based on prior requirements.

If you already have a notable profile and an existing verified badge, you can still apply for a Meta Verified subscription. Learn more about Meta Verified subscriptions.

What happens when you apply for a verified badge on Instagram

My verified badge was removed

I was denied a verified badge

What happens to my account?

How do I get Meta Verified?

I have a different question

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity, while others are subscribed to Meta Verified.

  • Verified badges mean an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid subscription that comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

If you already have an existing verified badge based on prior requirements, you can still subscribe to Meta Verified.

Once we review your request, you’ll receive a notification in Activity up to 30 days after applying letting you know if your account has been verified or not. You can tap Notifications in the top right to see notifications in Activity.

If your request is denied, you can submit a new request again in 30 days. Note that applying for a verified badge multiple times before receiving a decision will cancel your application.

Keep in mind that Instagram can remove verified badges at any time, and may take away your badge or disable your account if you:

  • Advertise, transfer or sell your verified badge.
  • Use your profile picture, bio or name section to promote other services or activities that violate our Community Standards or Terms of Use.
  • Attempt to verify your account through a third party.
  • Switch your account from public to private too many times.

If your account doesn’t have a verified badge, there are other ways to let people know you’re authentic. For example, you can link to your Instagram account from your official website, Facebook Page, YouTube or Twitter account. You can also subscribe to Meta Verified to get a verified badge.

Note:

  • If you provide false or misleading information during the verification process, we will remove your verified badge and may take additional action to disable your account.
  • Facebook or Instagram may reach out to you for verification. Learn more about how to make sure this outreach is authentic.

Verifying your account on Instagram will not verify your account on Facebook. Visit the Facebook Help Center to learn how to verify your Facebook account.

What happens when you report a post or profile on Instagram

What happens after I report?

Check report status

I disagree with a decision

I have a different question

When you report a piece of content (example: post, comment, story) to us, we will take action to hide or remove that content from Instagram if we find that it goes against our Community Guidelines. Our Community Guidelines define what is and isn’t allowed on Instagram, and they apply all over the world. They’re designed to encourage expression and create a safe environment on Instagram.

Even if we don’t remove the content or profile you reported, we understand that you likely want to see less of this type of content on Instagram. We may use your report to make content similar to what you reported appear lower in your feed or in the recommendations we make for you, like Suggested Posts and Explore.

Learn more about how to check the status of your report and what you can do if you don’t agree with Instagram’s decision about content you reported.

Certain profile information on Instagram, for public and private accounts, is always public. This information can be associated with you and is public to everyone, on or off Instagram, even if they don’t have an Instagram account.

Profile information that anyone can see in your Instagram profile includes your:

  • Name
  • Username
  • Profile picture
  • Bio
  • Links
  • Number of followers and following
  • Avatar
  • Threads username
  • Channels you create

Keep in mind that this information can’t be hidden and remains public regardless of whether your personal account is made private or public.

If you don’t want people to see this info, we suggest editing your profile.

What is a trademark violation?

What is not a violation?

Trademark violations may involve using a company or business name, logo or other trademark-protected materials in a manner that may mislead or confuse others with regard to its brand or business affiliation.

What is not a violation?

Using another’s trademark in a way that has nothing to do with the product or service for which the trademark was granted is not a violation of Threads and Instagram’s terms and conditions. Note that Instagram and Threads usernames are provided on a first-come, first-served basis and may not be reserved.

What to do if your Threads profile posts unauthorized content

How do I secure my account?

How do I change my password?

How do I turn on two-factor authentication?

How do I remove linked accounts?

I have a different question

If your Threads profile is leaving comments or sharing things that you haven’t posted, your password may be compromised. Additionally, if inauthentic activity is detected on your account, you may see an error message that says, “Try again later” when using Threads.

If you can log in to your Threads profile, there are several things you can do to secure your account:

  • Change your password or send yourself a password reset email. Be sure to pick a strong and unique password. Use a combination of at least six numbers, letters and special characters (like !$@%), and try to avoid repetition. Note: Whenever you change your password, any devices logged into your account will automatically be logged out and you’ll need to sign in again.
  • Revoke access on Threads to any suspicious third-party apps. You should never share your login information with an app you don’t trust. If you give these apps your login information, whether with an access token or by giving them your username and password, they can gain complete access to your account.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication for additional account security.
  • Confirm your phone number and email address in account settings are correct.
  • Check Accounts Center and remove any linked accounts you don’t recognize.

If you think your account has been hacked or taken over, there are other actions you may be able to take to secure your account. If someone gains access to your account or you’re unable to log in, visit this page on your desktop or mobile browser to secure your account.

Beware of scams

Be careful before giving third party apps or websites access to your Instagram account or Threads profile. In particular, you shouldn’t use apps that offer likes and followers in exchange for your Instagram login details. These websites and apps are likely attempts to use your account in an inappropriate way.

About privacy and security with shared access on Instagram

Manage shared access

Download shared access activity

Block shared access

I have a different question

Shared access is only available to eligible Instagram accounts. This feature is not available to teens.

Shared access allows you to invite people you trust to access your Instagram account. Shared access also provides an additional layer of security and flexibility for people who currently manage other accounts, or would like to collaborate with others on their account without having to share their password.

Your privacy and security with shared access

If you’ve shared access to your account with someone else:

  • People you’ve shared access with are acting on your shared account with your consent, but not as you. We encourage you to establish rules or expectations with them outside of Instagram on how to act on your behalf.
  • You’ll be able to see and download any activity on your account that’s taken by someone you’ve shared access with. Learn how to view your shared access account activity. You can also access and download a copy of your account activity, including shared access account activity.
  • The ads you see on the account you’ve shared access to may be influenced by actions other people take on the shared account.
  • If you block someone you’ve shared access with or they block you, they’ll automatically lose access to the shared account.

If you’ve been given access to someone else’s shared account:

  • You’re acting on behalf of the person who’s given you access to their account, but not as them. We encourage you to establish rules or expectations with them outside of Instagram on how to act on their behalf. Do not take actions on the shared account without the consent of the person that shared access with you.
  • You’ll be able to see and download any activity you’ve taken on the shared account but you won’t have access to the content itself such as the pictures, videos or reels. Learn how to download a copy of your account activity.
  • Any action you take on the shared account can be seen by the person who shared access with you.
  • Ads you see while using the shared account may not be relevant to you.
  • If you block the person that’s shared access with you, you’ll automatically lose access to their shared account.
How your shared access appears to other people on Instagram

When someone takes action on your shared account, they’ll appear as you. People can go to the About this account section of your account and see that your account is shared.

The accounts you see as available to log into may appear because:

Add or remove Instagram login information on your mobile device
  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.

Remove an account from the login screen on your mobile device
  1. Go to the login screen on the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Options on the top right of the screen.
  3. Tap Remove profiles from this device.
  4. Tap Remove next to the account you’d like to remove.

What happens if I remove an account?

I can’t remove an account

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you previously set up a single login for multiple Instagram accounts, you can continue to use this feature across your Instagram accounts by setting up your Accounts Center. You can remove any of these accounts at any time.

To remove an account you’ve linked to a single login from Instagram app for Android and iPhone:

Instagram app for Android:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Accounts Center.
  4. Tap Logging in with accounts.
  5. Tap Choose which accounts can log into other accounts and tap the account you want to remove.
  6. Below Which accounts can [account’s name] log in to, tap Uncheck next to the account you want to remove and follow the on-screen instructions.

Instagram app for iPhone:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Accounts Center.
  4. Tap Logging in with accounts.
  5. Tap Choose which accounts can log into other accounts and tap the account you want to remove.
  6. Below Which accounts can [account’s name] log in to, tap Uncheck next to the account you want to remove and follow the on-screen instructions.

If you did not previously set up a single login for multiple Instagram accounts, you won’t see the options above.

Instagram app for iPad:

When you change the password on the single login you use for multiple Instagram accounts, the new password will still log you into all of your linked accounts.

Keep in mind that you can’t add new Instagram accounts to a single login, but you can remove any previously added accounts at any time. If you remove an account from your single login, you can’t add it back.

If any of your Instagram accounts use two-factor authentication, you’ll be asked to enter your special login code or confirm your login attempt when logging into any of these accounts.

If you’ve previously set up a single Instagram login for multiple Instagram accounts, you’ll no longer be able to add any additional Instagram accounts to that single login. This means:

  • Any additional accounts you haven’t already added to your single Instagram login will require separate login information.
  • If you remove an account from your single Instagram login or change the password on an individual account associated with that single login, you won’t be able to add it back. You can log into that account with its individual password.

Learn more about what to do if you’re having trouble logging into your account.

Note: Each of your accounts on a single login will also keep their individual passwords, which you can still use to log into each individual account.

Log in using your Instagram login information
  1. Open the Instagram app or go to instagram.com.
  2. Log in using by entering one of the following:
    • Email: You can log in with any email that’s listed on your Facebook account.

    • Username: You can also log in with your username, if you created one.

Log into Instagram using your Instagram login information

You can log into your Instagram account using your Facebook login info, as long as your Facebook and Instagram accounts are added to the same Accounts Center, and allowed to log in to each other.

For example, from your Instagram login screen, you can enter the phone number or email and your password associated with your Facebook account to log in to your Instagram account.

Note: If you have two-factor authentication enabled on your Facebook or Instagram account, you won’t be able to use your Instagram login information to log into Facebook on an unrecognized device.

Saved accounts on your login screen

You may see multiple accounts you have across Meta apps (for example, Facebook), that you can use to log in. The accounts you see as available to log into may appear for one or more of the following reasons:

  1. The account was recently logged into on the same device.
  2. You have multiple accounts added to the same Accounts Center, and allowed to log in to each other.
  3. You use an Android phone and you’re logged into a Google account that is associated with any Facebook or Instagram accounts you have.

Logging in with a saved account allows you to log in easily with one tap, instead of entering your email or mobile phone number and password. In some cases, you may still need to enter your password. You can remove saved accounts that appear on the login screen at any time.

Remove an account from the login screen on your phone

  2. Tap Settings on the top right of the screen.

Two-factor authentication protects your account by requiring a code if there’s a login attempt from a device we don’t recognize.

If any of your Instagram accounts use two-factor authentication, you’ll be asked to enter your special login code or confirm your login attempt when logging into any of these accounts.

Turn on two-factor authentication
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click See more in Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  3. Click Two-factor authentication, then select an account.
  4. Choose the security method you want to add and follow the on-screen instructions.
Turn off two-factor authentication
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click See more in Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  3. Click Two-factor authentication, then select an account.
  4. Choose the security method you want to turn off and follow the on-screen instructions.

When you set up two-factor authentication on Instagram, you’ll be asked to choose one of three security methods:

  • Authentication app: (recommended): Download an authentication app, such as Duo Mobile or Google Authenticator to get login codes. This security method is recommended, because you can add multiple devices connected to an account so they can all get login codes. Note: Two-factor authentication through an authentication app can only be turned on using the Instagram app for Android and iPhone.
  • Text message: We’ll send a login code to your mobile number.
  • WhatsApp: Turn on the text message security method first. Then, you can turn on the WhatsApp security method to get login codes from WhatsApp.

You’ll need to have at least one of these set up in order to use two-factor authentication.

Note: After you’ve turned on two-factor authentication, you’ll be able to see login requests and remove trusted devices. If you lose access to your phone or email address and are unable to get login codes, you can use a backup code to log in. Learn more about login codes.

Keep in mind that:

  • If you haven’t marked the device you’re using as a trusted device, you can do so when you log in from that device using two-factor authentication. This way you won’t have to enter a security code when you log in again. Trusted devices are any device that you’ve already signed in to using two-factor authentication and have marked as trusted by tapping Trust this device.
  • You shouldn’t tap Trust this device if you’re using a public or shared device that other people you may not know can access.
  • To set up text message (SMS) two-factor authentication, you can either use a mobile number that’s already been added to your account or add a new number.

Use our security tips and tricks to double up on security.

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you set up two-factor authentication for an Instagram account using a third-party authentication app, you can connect multiple devices to two-factor authentication on that account.

When you add multiple devices to two-factor authentication on a single Instagram account, you’ll get a 6-digit login code from the authentication app on that device.

Keep in mind that one device will need to set up two-factor authentication through an authentication app first before other devices can be added. Any additional devices will also need to download an authentication app before connecting to two-factor authentication.

Set up two-factor authentication on additional devices
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Accounts Center.
  3. Click Password and security then select Two-factor authentication.
  4. Click your Instagram account.
  5. Click Authentication app, then click Copy key or use the QR code to link your account to the authentication app.
  6. After your Instagram account is linked to your authentication app, copy the 6-digit code your authentication app creates.
  7. Go back to Instagram on your computer, click Next and paste the 6-digit code to complete the process on that device.

Keep in mind that you can add up to five connected devices to two-factor authentication for a single Instagram account and you can remove a connected device at any time.

Your Instagram key can also be used if you use multiple authentication apps on the same device. To do this, follow the steps above on the same device.

Remove a connected device from two-factor authentication
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Accounts Center.
  3. Click Password and security, then select Two-factor authentication.
  4. Click your Instagram account, then select the method you are using to get login codes (example: text message, WhatsApp, or authentication app).
  5. Click Turn off.

Removing a connected device from two-factor authentication does not log it out from your account.

When you set up two-factor authentication on Instagram you’ll receive an alert whenever someone tries logging in to your account from a device or web browser we don’t recognize. These alerts may appear as push notifications, in Activity, or as in-app notifications, and will tell you which device tried logging in and where it’s located. You can approve or deny the request immediately.

Turn login requests on or off

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Security, then tap Two-factor authentication.
  4. Tap Additional methods, then tap Toggle next to Login requests to turn notifications on or off.

Note that in order to receive login request notifications, you may need to turn on push notifications from Instagram.

Approve or deny a login request

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap the notification to view the location and type of device the request is coming from.
  2. Tap Approve if you recognize the device to allow access to your account. Tap Deny if you don’t recognize the device.
  3. If you deny the request, follow the on-screen instructions to reset your password. Note: When you deny a login request from a device you don’t recognize, we ask you to reset your password so that anyone trying to get into your account with your current password will no longer have access.

Note that you can view a list of devices that have recently logged into your Instagram account at any time. If you don’t recognize a recent login, you can log out of that location or device and let us know that the login wasn’t you.

View your account’s recent login activity

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Security, then tap Login activity.
  4. If you recognize the login, tap This Was Me, then tap Confirm. If you don’t recognize the location or device listed, tap This Wasn’t Me and follow the on-screen instructions to reset your password and secure your account. Note: You may not see these options if there hasn’t been a login to your account from a device or web browser we don’t recognize. Instead, follow the below step to log out of any devices listed.
  5. To log out of devices you’re currently logged into, tap Options to the right of the login, then tap Log out.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

When you turn on two-factor authentication, you’re asked to choose either text message (SMS) codes or a third-party authentication app as your primary security method. About Edits

Start a video project

Edit my video

Delete my Edits content

I have a different question

Edits is an app from Instagram that allows you to turn your ideas into engaging videos. With Edits’ powerful editing tools, you can create your own video projects that can include text, music, effects, and more.

Start a video project

You can record a video project with Edits and keep it as a draft or download it to your device.

You can also view reels on Edits that were shared on Instagram to see what is trending and reuse audio from those reels to start your own video projects.

When you’re ready, you can automatically download your video to your device and choose to share it on Instagram or Facebook as a reel. Learn more about how to download and share your video.

Edit your content

Edits offers the tools to create unique content for your audience. You can use these tools to add and manage multiple layers (examples: music, text) of your video content.

Learn how to edit your video on Edits.

How information from your Instagram account is used on Edits

You may log into Edits using your Instagram account. We use your Instagram information in accordance with Meta’s Privacy Policy to do things like import your saved reels on Instagram and collect and share real-time insights in Edits on reels you share to Instagram.

Data from your Instagram account is used for Edits and can include:

  • Content you interact with on Instagram
  • Your Instagram login information
  • Your Instagram account ID
  • Your Instagram name and username
  • Your Instagram profile information like your profile picture
  • Your Instagram followers
  • Accounts you follow on Instagram
  • Your age on Instagram
  • Your Instagram location information
  • Your Instagram account status relating to intellectual property violations and instances of going against the Community Standards.

Note: Information relating to your use of Edits will be processed in accordance with Meta’s Privacy Policy. The Instagram Terms of Use apply to your use of Edits.

Delete your information

You can delete video content you created on Edits at any time.

If you want to delete other information relating to your use of Edits, such as what actions you took on Edits, you will have to delete your Instagram account since Edits is part of Instagram.

If you temporarily deactivate your Instagram account, this will also temporarily deactivate Edits for you.

Access and export your information

You can view and export information about your use of Edits on Instagram.

Music not available in my region

My account is a business account

I have a different question

Musical expression is encouraged across Meta technologies.

Our agreements with rights holders

Meta is obligated to uphold our agreements with the rights holders of the music that’s available in our licensed music library. These agreements are designed to protect artists, songwriters, and their works.

The music available in our library is intended for personal, non-commercial use.

Restricted access to the music library

To make sure that the music in our licensed library is not used for commercial purposes, certain business accounts and certain types of posts do not have access to the library. Licensed music may also not be available in certain countries or regions.

If your account does not have access to the licensed music library, then you may be able to use Meta’s Sound Collection.

About Meta’s Sound Collection

Sound Collection provides access to over 14,000 songs and sounds which are entirely royalty free and safe to use in Reels and Instagram Stories. The content in Sound Collection can be used for commercial purposes like ads. You can find this music library by swiping up and selecting Music sticker in Stories, or by tapping Audio in the Reels camera.

If you’re not seeing the music sticker in Reels, make sure your app is updated to the latest version by visiting the App Store or Google Play Store. Keep in mind that the music sticker isn’t available to everyone.

When you record a reel, you’ll see a tool menu on the left. You can tap:

  • Length to choose the length of your clip. When you return to your clip, you see a countdown before your clip starts recording.
  • Dual camera to record a reel using the front and back camera on your device at the same time.
  • Align clips to see the end of your last clip. You can use the transparent photo to align your next clip before recording. This will only appear after you record your first clip.

Note that you can also record a reel with your own audio. Learn more about using audio in your reel and who can see your reels.

About Frames stickers

When you add the Frames sticker to your story, your friends and followers will see a blurry image, like a polaroid picture that was just taken. Your viewers can shake their phones, or tap “shake to reveal,” to develop the photo in the frame.

You can caption the picture with text or emojis. The date and time the picture was taken will automatically be added.
