Apply effects to your Instagram photo

Apply effects to photo

Adjust photo perspective

Make photo brighter

Add color to photo

I have a different question

You can edit photos you take or upload from your phone’s library. Once you’ve taken or uploaded a photo, tap Next, then tap Edit at the bottom of the screen. Learn more about the effects you can create:

  • Tap Adjust to change the photo’s vertical or horizontal perspective.
  • Tap Brightness to make your photo brighter or darker.
  • Tap Contrast to make the bright areas of your photo brighter and the dark areas darker.
  • Tap Structure to bring out the detail and texture in your photo.
  • Tap Warmth to shift the colors of your photo toward warmer orange tones or cooler blue tones.
  • Tap Saturation to increase or decrease the color intensity of the image (example: adjust up to make the red redder).
  • Tap Color to add a color (yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, cyan or green) to either the shadows or highlights of your photo. Tap the color you want to use twice to adjust the strength of the color.
  • Tap Fade to give your photo an aged look.
  • Tap Highlights to adjust the focus on the bright areas of the image.
  • Tap Shadows to adjust focus on the dark areas of the image.
  • Tap Vignette to darken the edges of the photo. Adding a vignette can direct the attention away from the edges towards the center of the photo.
  • Tap Sharpen to add crispness to your photo and make the photo appear clearer.
  • Tap Tilt Shift to give the appearance of a shallow depth of field, or placing the focus on a subject in the background while blurring out the foreground and vice versa.
  • Tap at the top to balance exposure and increase brightness.

In preview mode, a gray dot will appear below each of the effects you’ve applied to your photo. For example, a gray dot below Brightness means you’ve adjusted the brightness of your photo.

In most regions, an Apple service fee of 30% of your total ad payment, before any taxes and local fees, may apply when you add available funds to your ad account in the Instagram iOS app. This fee is retained by Apple, not Instagram or Meta. Learn how to avoid the Apple service fee when boosting on Instagram.

If you’re based in or intend to target audiences in the US and want to create an ad campaign that relates to credit, employment, housing, social issues or political ads, you must choose the category that best describes your ads from the Special Ad Category dropdown menu.

You can boost a post on Instagram to turn it into an ad to help your brand reach new audiences and drive engagement. Boosted posts appear in Explore, Home Feed, Explore feed, profile feed and Stories. Instagram feed posts that include product tags can also be boosted.

Before you begin
  • Convert your profile to a professional account.
  • If you haven’t boosted on Instagram before, you’ll be prompted to choose an ad account to connect to. You can choose an existing Facebook ad account, or keep your Facebook and Instagram accounts separate.
  • For people residing in the EU, the EEA and Switzerland, your ability to advertise and monetize with ads is limited if your account is in an Accounts Center with a subscription to use Meta Products without ads or a less-personalized ad experience. Learn more about these limitations on your ability to advertise or monetize.
Boost an Instagram post

Note: When you boost a reel on the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to pay with available funds. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee when boosting your content, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

To boost an Instagram feed post on the Instagram app:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap the post you’d like to boost.
  3. Below the post’s image, tap Boost.
  4. Fill in the details of your ad by setting the Goal (what do you want people to do when they see your ad), Audience (who you want to see your ad), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next once you’ve completed these details.
  5. Tap Preview ad to review the placements that your ad will run and control Advantage+ creative. Note: If your ad runs in the Feed placement, your ad will appear in profile feed. Learn more about ads in Instagram profile feed.
  6. To complete your ad, tap Boost post.

To boost an Instagram feed post on instagram.com:

  1. Click Profile, or select your profile picture to go to your profile.
  2. Select the post you’d like to boost, then click Boost.
  3. Fill in the details of your ad by selecting a Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run).
  4. To complete your ad, select Boost post.

Once you select Boost post, your ad will be submitted for review to make sure it meets our ad policies. You’ll receive a notification after you submit an ad for review, when it’s being reviewed, when it’s approved or disapproved and when the ad ends. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

You can boost Instagram reels to turn them into ads to help your brand reach new audiences and drive engagement. Boosted reels appear in the Reels tab, Explore, Feed and Stories.

You can also learn how to boost an Instagram post or boost an Instagram Story.

Before you begin

If you haven’t boosted on Instagram before, you’ll be prompted to choose an ad account to connect to. You can choose an existing Facebook ad account, or keep your Facebook and Instagram accounts separate.

Before you boost an Instagram reel, check its eligibility before posting. To be eligible for boosting:

  • Reels must be 90 seconds or less and have a full-screen (9:16) vertical format.
  • Reels can’t use licensed music. Instead, we recommend using royalty-free music, like what’s available in our Sound Collection, or original audio.
  • Your ad shouldn’t use Instagram Reels published before October 15th, 2021.
  • Your reels media can’t contain face or camera effects, GIFs, product tags, interactive stickers or camera filters from a third party.
  • Reels that have already been shared to Facebook can’t be boosted.
Boost an Instagram Reel

Note: When you boost a reel on the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to pay with available funds. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee when boosting your content, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

To boost an Instagram reel from the Instagram app:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap the reel you’d like to boost.
  3. Below the reel, tap Boost.
  4. Fill in the details of your ad by selecting a Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next once you’ve completed these details.
  5. To complete your ad, tap Boost reel under Review your ad.

To boost an Instagram reel from instagram.com:

  1. Click Profile, or select your profile picture to go to your profile.
  2. Select the reel you’d like to boost, then select Boost.
  3. Fill in the details of your ad by selecting a Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run).
  4. To complete your ad, select Boost reel.

Once you select Boost post, your ad will be submitted for review to make sure it meets our ad policies. You’ll receive a notification after you submit an ad for review, when it’s being reviewed, when it’s approved or disapproved and when the ad ends. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

In most regions, an Apple service fee of 30% of your total ad payment, before any taxes and local fees, may apply when you add available funds to your ad account in the Instagram iOS app. This fee is retained by Apple, not Instagram or Meta. You can boost Instagram stories to turn them into ads to help your brand reach new audiences. You can only boost stories that are:

  • Active (currently visible on your profile)
  • Featured in your highlights
  • Reposted from your Instagram archive

Note: When creating an ad using an existing post with Ads Manager, you can only select Instagram stories that are active.

For partnership ads, archived stories can be boosted if the advertiser is tagged and has partnership permissions with the creator. The branded content tag can be applied after the story is archived, within 24 hours.

You can also learn how to boost an Instagram post or boost an Instagram reel.

Eligible formats for boosted Instagram stories
  • For most ads: You can use one of the following interactive elements: location sticker, hashtag sticker, tappable text, countdown sticker, and @mention sticker for the account you’re boosting from. You can mention up to 5 people in your boosted story.
  • For partnership ads: You can use up to five of the following interactive elements: location sticker, hashtag sticker, countdown sticker, tappable text and @mention sticker for the creator or the business partner’s profile. Learn more about eligible formats for partnership ads.
Before you begin

If you haven’t boosted on Instagram before, you’ll be prompted to choose an ad account to connect to. You can choose an existing Facebook ad account, or keep your Facebook and Instagram accounts separate.

Before you boost an Instagram story, check its eligibility before posting. To be eligible for boosting, the story must:

  • Not contain polls, quizzes, music, link stickers, or other complex creative tools.
  • Only use effects made by Instagram.
  • Avoid using emojis, GIFs, or copyrighted music.
  • Only use a single story card. Carousel (multi-card) stories are not supported.
  • You can add a link in your organic story, but only if you add a link as an action button during ad creation, and only if your story does not already have a sticker or interactive element.
    • To optimize for action buttons, follow ad specification guidance for stories and leave approximately 14% of the top and 20% of the bottom of your creative free from text, logos, or other key elements to prevent the action button from covering them.
    • You can also adjust the default position of the action button for ads in the 9:16 ratio in the ad creative section in Meta Ads Manager.
  • For partnership ads:
    • You may use up to five interactive elements: location sticker, hashtag sticker, countdown sticker, tappable text, and @mention sticker (for creator or business partner).
    • The advertiser must have account-level permissions and be tagged using the paid partnership label, an @mention, a people tag, a product tag, or a Collab.

Note: When you boost a reel on the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to pay with available funds. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee when boosting your content, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

To boost an active Instagram story on the Instagram app:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap your profile picture to access your story.

  4. Fill in the details of your ad by selecting a Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next (iOS) or (Android) once you’ve completed these details.
  5. To complete your ad, tap Boost post.

To boost an active Instagram story on instagram.com:

  1. Click Profile, or select your profile picture to go to your profile.
  2. Click your profile picture to access your story.
  3. At the bottom of your story’s image or video, click More, then select Boost.
  4. Fill in the details of your ad by selecting a Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run).
  5. To complete your ad, select Boost post.

Once you select Boost post, your ad will be submitted for review to make sure it meets our ad policies. You’ll receive a notification after you submit an ad for review, when it’s being reviewed, when it’s approved or disapproved and when the ad ends. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

Boosted stories will run for the duration you set, even after the original story expires from your profile.

Data used to suggest content from your camera roll

Turn on camera roll suggestions

What data is used?

I can’t see suggested reels

What are suggested reels?

I have a different question

Permissions, access, and data

If you give Instagram permission to access metadata about the photos and videos on your device’s camera, we can use this data to group the media in your camera roll and suggest content you can share as stories, posts or reels.

Some of the metadata that the Instagram app uses to suggest reels includes:

  • How recently your photo or video was taken
  • Where your photo or video was taken
  • Photos or videos you favorited
  • The presence of people or animals
How the app prepares reels

To see and share reels that Instagram prepares for you, you must allow the Instagram app to access metadata about the photos and videos on your device’s camera to suggest content. Learn how to allow the app to access this metadata for us to make these suggestions.

The app uses photos and videos from your device’s camera roll to create reels and suggest them to you. Suggested reels are only shared to Instagram if you choose to share them. You can view, edit, and save your suggested reels without sharing them.

Edit my AI’s personality

My AI won’t publish

I have a different question

Custom AIs on Instagram aren’t yet available for everyone.

When you create an custom AI on Instagram, the personality details of that AI change how it interacts with people. You can decide how the AI starts conversations, give it instructions on how to respond and include example questions that help people start a conversation with it. By adding more detail to your AI, you’ll refine how it should act.

Your AI starts with generated personality details, but you can edit these at any time.

You can access the Meta AI Studio Handbook for more details on the personality options.

To edit your AI
  1. Go to aistudio.instagram.com using a computer.
  2. Click Your AIs.
  3. Click next to the AI you want to edit.
  4. Edit your AI. To switch between Knowledge and Introduction and capabilities, click on the name.
  5. You can change AI’s audience in the top right. Setting your AI’s audience doesn’t affect your account privacy. You can set the audience to:
    • Everyone - Everyone on Instagram can see your AI. You can also share your AI on your Instagram profile and to Messenger and WhatsApp by clicking Discoverability, then toggling where you want your AI to be seen.
    • Close Friends - Only your close friends on Instagram can see your AI. You can show your AI on your Instagram profile to your close friends by toggling Show in Instagram profile.
    • Only Me - Only you will be able to see and interact with your AI.
  6. Tap Create.
  7. Once you’re happy with your changes, click Publish.

Your AI will need to be reviewed after your edits before people can chat with it. You’ll be notified when it’s available. Learn more about acceptable AIs.

You won’t see the chats that other people have with your AI, but you can see insights on how many chats your AI has had and other data about it.

Note

  • Similar to other chats, interactions with AI are subject to our Community Standards and Terms of Service.

  • An AI’s response may be inaccurate or inappropriate and should not be used to make important decisions.

  • Meta uses your interactions with AIs to improve AI at Meta. If the AIs cannot answer your query, Meta shares the messages you send to AI and general information, like your region, with select partners so you can get better results. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service to learn more.

  • Meta AI uses your location information to give you more relevant responses. Your location information is based on things like the settings you’ve chosen on your device, or your activity across our products. Learn more about how to manage your location in the Privacy Center.

  • Other information from your profile such as your age and gender, and interests based on your activity across our products, such as the types of content, including ads, you view or interact with and how you interact with it, will be used to help personalize your interactions with AI. Learn more about how Meta uses this information in the Privacy Center. You can also see how information is used across your accounts in the same Accounts Center and export your information. Learn how to Export a copy of your information.

  • Depending on your prompt, the content generated may go against our Community Standards or Terms of Service of Meta’s platforms. Sharing AI-generated content on our platforms that go against these standards will be treated the same as sharing other content that go against our standards. If you share generated content that goes against our standards, your content may be removed and your account may be restricted or disabled. Learn more about the Community Standards and Terms of Service on:

    • Facebook, Messenger and Instagram
    • WhatsApp

  • Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products can be used to personalize content and ads.

  • People who create an AI in Meta AI Studio do not have access to the chats other people have with that AI, unless they’re a creator using an AI based on themselves to respond to their personal messages. Learn more about AI auto replies.

  • Custom AIs are not licensed professionals or experts trained to help people. Chats with custom AIs can’t replace professional advice. You shouldn’t rely on AI chats for medical, psychological, financial, legal or any other type of professional advice. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service for appropriate ways to use AIs for self-help or other purposes.

Learn more about how Meta uses information for generative AI models.

After you start a thread or reply to a thread, you can choose to edit the text of your post. Note: you can only edit a post within 15 minutes of posting.

Edit your post

Threads.com from a computer

  1. Click Profile on the left to go to your profile.
  2. Click Threads at the top to view threads you’ve posted or click Replies at the top to find your replies to threads.
  3. Click on a thread or a reply you’ve recently posted.
  4. Click Options in the top right of your post.
  5. Click Edit, then update the text of your post.
  6. When you’re ready, click Post.

Threads app for Android and iPhone

Keep in mind
  • You can’t edit a post 15 minutes after it was posted.
  • Only the text of a post can be edited. No additional attachments can be added, nor can current attachments be removed.
  • If anyone interacts with your post (examples: like, reply, repost, or quote) before you finish editing, your edited post will include Edited in the top right to indicate that it’s been edited.
  • For posts with approvals on for replies, replies can’t be edited.
  • If you’ve turned on sharing to the fediverse, we will delay sharing your posts to other fediverse servers for 15 minutes to allow for editing of your posts on Threads.

If you’re past the time limit to edit a post, you have the option to delete a post.

I can’t share my reel

Sharing to Facebook not working

My Facebook is not listed

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re having trouble sharing an Instagram reel to Facebook, try these steps to resolve the issue. Before you begin:

  • Make sure that both your Instagram and Facebook apps are updated to the latest version.
  • Make sure you have a stable internet connection.
Check that sharing is enabled

Make sure your Instagram account is set up to share your reels to Facebook by verifying your sharing settings in Accounts Center.

  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Sharing across profiles.
  5. Below Share from, select your account.
  6. Make sure that the toggle next to Your Instagram reels is turned on.
Check your Facebook connection

Make sure that your Facebook account has been added to your Accounts Center.

  1. Go to your Instagram settings.
  2. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Accounts at the bottom.
  3. Make sure your Facebook account is listed.
Turn sharing off, then back on

Toggling the sharing feature off and then on again can help refresh the sharing connection.

  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Sharing across profiles.
  5. Below Share from, select your account.
  6. Turn off the toggle next to Your Instagram reels, then turn it back on again.
Check for account restrictions

Check if your account has any restrictions or limitations on it.

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below More info and support, tap Account Status.
Restart the Instagram and Facebook apps

This can help to clear any minor software issues that might be preventing sharing. Close both the Instagram and Facebook apps completely, then reopen the apps and try sharing your reel again.

Log out and log back in

This can help refresh your account sessions on both apps.

Report the issue if troubleshooting steps don’t work

If you’ve tried all of the troubleshooting steps and still can’t share your reel, then you can report the issue to Instagram.

  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Below More info and support, tap Help.
  5. Tap Report a problem.

How does video selfie age verification work on Instagram?

How does video selfie work?

What happens to my video selfie?

Why can’t I verify my age?

I have a different question

This feature is only available in some countries.

If you are under 16 and trying to change your age on Instagram to over 16, you will be asked to give us additional information to help verify your age.

There are a few different ways you can verify your age:

  • Take a video selfie
  • Upload your ID
How your age is verified

If you choose to take a video selfie, we partner with vendors who use technology to estimate your age. After you’ve taken a video selfie, we’ll share an image from that selfie with the vendor. Our vendors’ technology only estimates age. It can’t identify specific people.

Once your age has been estimated and shared with us, we will delete the image within 30 days. We don’t share any other information about you with the vendor.

How to take the selfie

If you choose to take a video selfie to verify your age, you’ll see instructions on your screen for how to take the selfie. If you haven’t used the camera on Instagram before, we’ll ask you for permission to use the camera so you can take the selfie.

When you take the selfie, make sure your whole face is visible and that you have enough light for the camera. Avoid wearing anything that blocks your face, like a mask or hat. You’ll be asked to move your face in different directions, such as to the right and left and up and down.

Once your age has been estimated and shared with us, we will delete the image within 30 days. Once you have submitted your selfie, you can keep using Instagram or exit the app.

It can take up to 20 minutes to verify your age. You will get a notification with the outcome of the verification.

How to delete Edits

Delete my Edits data

What happens if I delete?

Can I get my account back?

How long does deletion take?

I have a different question

You can delete video content you created on Edits at any time, but if you want to delete other information relating to your use of Edits, such as what actions you took on Edits, you will have to delete your Instagram account since Edits is part of Instagram.

Before deleting your Instagram account, you may want to download a copy of your information.

Delete your Edits information
  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Profiles and personal details.
  5. Tap Manage next to the desired account, then tap Deactivation or deletion.
  6. Tap the account you’d like to permanently delete.
  7. Tap Delete account, then tap Continue.

Your Instagram account and content will be permanently deleted 30 days after your request is submitted, and you’ll no longer be able to retrieve your information. During the 30-day period, the content on Edits remains subject to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

You can cancel your Instagram account deletion request before the 30-day deadline by logging back into your Instagram account. After canceling your Instagram profile deletion request, your content will be visible again on Edits.

Keep in mind
  • If your Instagram account is removed for violating Community Standards, you may not be able to sign up again with the same Instagram account.
  • It may take up to 90 days to complete the deletion process after it begins. Copies of your information may remain after the 90 days in backup storage that we use to recover in the event of a disaster, software error, or other data loss event. We may also keep your information for things like legal issues, terms violations, or harm prevention efforts. Learn more about how long we keep your information in Meta’s Privacy Policy.

How to make sure content you post to Instagram or Threads doesn’t violate copyright law

How to avoid copyright violation?

What content can I post?

Can I use content I bought?

What is fair use?

I have a different question

Under Instagram’s Terms of Use and Meta’s Community Standards you can only post content to Instagram or Threads that doesn’t violate someone else’s intellectual property rights. The best way to help make sure that what you post to Instagram or Threads doesn’t violate copyright law is to only post content that you’ve created yourself.

Posting content that facilitates copyright infringement through unauthorized devices or services is also not allowed on Instagram or Threads.

It’s possible to infringe someone else’s copyright when you post their content on Instagram or Threads, or facilitate copyright infringement, even if you:

  • Bought or downloaded the content (example: a song from iTunes)
  • Recorded the content onto your own recording device (examples: a song playing in the background during a party, concert, sporting event, wedding, etc.)
  • Gave credit to the copyright owner
  • Included a disclaimer that you didn’t intend to infringe copyright
  • Didn’t intend to profit from it
  • Modified the work or added your own original material to it
  • Found the content available on the internet
  • Saw that others posted the same content as well
  • Think that the use is a fair use
  • Are using an unauthorized streaming device or service (examples: a “jailbroken” or “loaded” app or service)

Before you post content on Instagram or Threads, you may want to ask:

  • Did I create all of the content myself?
  • Do I have permission to use all of the content included in my post?
  • Does my use of the content fall within an exception to copyright infringement?
  • Is the content protected by copyright (for example, is it a short phrase, a concept or idea, or a work that has fallen into the public domain)?

It’s generally a good idea to get written permission from the author of the work before posting content on Instagram or Threads. You might be able to use someone else’s content on Instagram or Threads if you’ve gotten permission from them, such as through obtaining a license. You also may be able to use someone else’s content if it’s in the public domain, is covered by fair use, or there is another exception to copyright.

Learn more about copyright and what copyright laws protect.

How to make sure the content you post to Instagram or Threads don’t violate trademark law

My content violates trademark law

How to avoid trademark violation

What is trademark infringement?

I have a different question

Under Instagram’s Terms of Use and Meta’s Community Standards you can only post content to Instagram or Threads if it doesn’t violate the intellectual property rights of another party, including trademarks. Please note that as an Instagram or Threads user, you are responsible for the content you post. If your content violates Threads or Instagram’s policies or is reported to Instagram or Threads as infringing the intellectual property rights of another party, Instagram or Threads may remove that content.

Before you post content, you might want to ask:

  • Have I used someone else’s trademark to sell or promote goods or services in a way that may confuse people?
  • Does my use of a trademark only refer to someone else’s goods or services, or make some other type of non-infringing use of the trademark (example: using a trademarked word in its ordinary dictionary meaning, or using the trademark in a way that is not related to the sale or promotion of products or services)?

If you have questions about trademark law or whether your content infringes another party’s trademark rights, you may want to contact an attorney.

How to use music in your videos on Instagram or Threads

My video was muted

Why was my video blocked?

Dispute a music claim

Music guidelines for Live

I have a different question

We want to encourage musical expression on Instagram and Threads, while making sure we uphold our agreements with music rights holders. These agreements protect artists, songwriters and other music rights holders by setting limitations around the amount of recorded music that can be included in Live broadcasts or videos.

Please keep the following general guidelines in mind when using music in your live videos:

  • There are no limits on using music in Stories, or traditional musical performances (example: filming a live artist or band performing their own music).
  • The more full-length recorded tracks in your video, the more likely the video may be limited (example: muted or blocked).
  • Shorter clips of music are recommended.
  • There should always be a visual component to your video; recorded audio should not be the primary purpose of the video.

If we detect that your live video broadcast includes music in a way that doesn’t adhere to our music licensing agreements, you may receive a notification from us while filming. This notification is intended to alert you so you can make changes to your stream and avoid interruptions. If your video is muted or blocked, we’ll make clear what actions you can take to stop the interruption. These actions may include an option to dispute a rights holder’s claim if you believe it was made in error.

Learn more about our Music Guidelines in our Terms of Use or how to replace muted audio in Reels or in Posts.

Image resolution of photos you share on Instagram

What is the best resolution?

What aspect ratios are supported?

My photo resolution is low

How to upload high quality photos?

I have a different question

When you share a photo on Instagram, regardless of whether you’re using Instagram for iPhone or Android, we make sure to upload it at the best quality resolution possible (up to a width of 1080 pixels).

When you share a photo that has a width between 320 and 1080 pixels, we keep that photo at its original resolution as long as the photo’s aspect ratio is between 1.91:1 and 3:4 (a width of 1080 pixels with a height between 566 and 1440 pixels). If the aspect ratio of your photo isn’t supported, it will be cropped to fit a supported ratio. If you share a photo at a lower resolution, we enlarge it to a width of 320 pixels. If you share a photo at a higher resolution, we size it down to a width of 1080 pixels.

If you want to make sure that your photo is shared with a width of 1080 pixels:

  • Download the most recent version of the Instagram app.
  • Upload a photo with a width of at least 1080 pixels with an aspect ratio between 1.91:1 and 3:4.
  • Make sure you’re using a phone with a high-quality camera as different phones have cameras of varying qualities.

Instagram or Threads removed content as a result of your trademark report. What information is sent to the person who posted that content

What information is sent?

What is a report number?

What is a rights owner?

I have a different question

When we receive trademark infringement reports and remove the reported content, we provide the reported user with the following information:

  • Report number
  • Rights owner’s name
  • Email address provided by the reporting party
  • Description of the rights owner’s trademark(s)
  • Description of the removed content

In rare cases (such as when we are contacted by fax, mail or email), we provide the report number and a description of the removed content. Instagram and Threads may provide additional information if it’s requested by the person who posted the reported content.

For any content that was removed based on U.S. trademark rights, we will include instructions for how to appeal if the affected user believes the content should not have been removed.

Manage scheduled messages from businesses

Stop scheduled messages

Mute business messages

Report a business message

I have a different question

This feature isn’t available to everyone.

When you chat with a business on Instagram, the business might offer you the choice to opt-in to receive messages about certain topics regularly. These topics could include promotions, new products or classes, and other updates.

Tap Get messages to receive messages about these topics based on the schedule shown (for example, Get weekly messages). The business chooses the schedule of messages.

To opt-out, mute or report these messages from a business:

  1. Tap Messages in the top right of your Feed.
  2. Tap on the chat with the business.
  3. Find the gray text acknowledging that you’ve chosen to receive these specific daily, weekly or monthly messages from the business.
  4. Tap Manage.
  5. To stop receiving this specific category of messages regularly, tap Stop these messages. To silence the entire chat, tap Mute messages.
  6. To report an issue, such as scamming, tap Report and follow the on-screen instructions.

Meta doesn’t control the content or topic of the messages that businesses send. You may continue to receive other messages about the same or different topics in addition to the messages you choose to receive, including ones that could be promotional in nature.

The recurring schedule of messages is based on the timezone of the business. This means that in some cases, you may receive an additional message per day, week or month, depending on which frequency you’ve opted into.

Tapping Stop these messages only ends the scheduling of messages on that topic. A business can continue to contact you about the same topics at other times.

If you’d like to stop all communications with a business, learn how to block an account on Instagram.

How long can reels be?

I have a different question

Reels isn’t currently available to everyone. Some accounts may be able to see reels, but won’t be able to record them.

You can record and edit videos up to 20 minutes with Instagram Reels. You can add effects and music to your reel or use your own original audio.

Record your reel
  1. Click Create on the left.
  2. Click Post.
  3. Click Select from computer and choose the content you want to share from your device. Click Media in the bottom right, then click Add to add another file.
  4. Click Next in the top right. From here you can:
    • Use the slider on the right below Cover photo to choose a cover photo from the clip or click Select from computer to choose one on your device.
    • Use the slider on the right below Trim to trim the beginning or end of your clip.
  5. Tap Next in the top right. Here you can write a caption, add a location, tag people, add alternate text, and adjust your post’s settings.
  6. Tap Share in the top right.

If you share your reel to Explore, it can also be seen on the Reels section of your profile.

How long your reel can be

You can record one or multiple clips that add up to 20 minutes. The progress bar at the top shows how long you’ve recorded.

Note: Reels over 3 minutes won’t be recommended to new audiences.

Start a project

Edits app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Camera at the bottom.

  • Rename a project by tapping Rename, entering a name and then tapping Done.

  • Delete a project by tapping Delete and confirming your choice.

You can also start a project with media from your device’s gallery by tapping New project in the bottom right of projects.

Replace muted audio

Why is my audio muted?

Can’t find song

I have a different question

If the audio track has been muted on your post, then you can replace the track.

Replace audio that’s been muted
  1. Open the Instagram app and find the post with the muted audio.
  2. Tap Audio unavailable.
  3. Tap Replace audio, then tap Replace audio again.
  4. Choose the part of the track you want for your post.
  5. Tap Done in the top right.
  6. Tap Done or Done.
Muted audio notifications

If your post has a muted audio track, you may see a notification to replace the audio when you view the post. You can replace the audio with another licensed audio that’s available from the Instagram audio library. You can only replace a muted track one time.

Why your audio might be muted

We have agreements with music rights holders meant to protect artists and creators. Any changes made to those agreements may result in your audio being muted. Your post can still be viewed even if audio tracks have been muted.

Licensed audio is copyrighted music available on the Instagram audio library. All licensed audio must be attributed or linked to the artist and include the name of the track.

When you start a new post on Threads, you can save it as a draft to revisit and post at another time.

Save a draft of your post
  1. Click in the bottom right to start a new post.

You can see your drafts by clicking in the bottom right and then clicking . To delete a draft, click next to the draft and then click Delete draft.

Currently, drafts that you save can only be accessed from where they were saved. For example, drafts that you save on threads.com can only be accessed on threads.com and a draft you save in the Threads app can only be accessed from the app.

Drafts are saved onto your device. You won’t be able to access a saved draft from another device, even if you log in to your account. If you uninstall the app, your drafts will be lost.

You can record a reel and save it to your Instagram account or camera roll before sharing it. Drafts will be saved until you share or delete them. There isn’t a limit to how many drafts you can save.

Share multiple photos or videos

Add multiple captions

I can’t upload multiple videos

I have a different question

You can share a post with up to 20 photos and videos as a single post, also known as a carousel, to your Instagram feed.

Share multiple photos or videos as a single post
  1. Click Create on the left.
  2. Click Post, then click Select from computer to browse and select a photo or video.
  3. Click , then click .
  4. Select up to 20 photos and videos from your computer. To adjust how each photo or video is cropped, click and hold it, then drag to adjust how it fits in the frame. Keep in mind that the orientation you choose (square, portrait or landscape) affects all of the photos or videos in your post. You can’t select a different orientation for each photo or video. When you’re done, click Next in the top right.
  5. To change the order of your photos and videos, click and hold one then drag it to another spot. To remove a photo or video from your post, click next to it. When you’re done, click Next in the top right.
  6. Click a filter to apply it to every photo and video you’ve selected, or click a photo or video to edit it and add filters individually.
  7. You can add one location and caption for your entire post, and tag someone in each individual photo. Click the photo to tag someone.
  8. Click Share.

In your feed, you’ll see the first photo or video from your post with a row of dots below it. People can swipe to see the rest of the photos or videos you’ve shared.

In your profile, you’ll see the first photo or video from your carousel with in the top right. You can tap the post, then swipe to view the rest of the photos and videos you’ve shared. Keep in mind that videos in carousels are not considered reels and will not show up in the Reels tab or have reels features.

People can like and comment on your post just as they would on any other post. Comments and likes appear on the entire post, rather than on the individual photos and videos that are part of your post.

After you’ve shared a post with multiple photos and videos, you can reorder the content, remove photos or videos, edit your caption or captions, edit the location and accounts you’ve tagged in your post.

To make these changes, select the three-dot menu on the right side of the carousel, select Edit, and then long press to reorder the photos or videos. To save your changes, select Done on the right side. While you can’t add new photos or videos after you’ve shared the carousel, you can delete the post.

Keep in mind that posts containing multiple videos may take longer to upload. If your post contains multiple videos, make sure you’re connected to a reliable network.

How do I tag a topic?

How do I find trending topics?

I have a different question

Tagging a topic in your post allows others on Threads to discover your post and other posts associated with that topic in real time. You can include up to 1 topic per post.

Tag a topic in your post

Threads.com from a computer

  1. Click Add in the bottom right to start a new thread.
  2. Click Tag or type # and then enter a topic. You can either:
    • Tag a topic without a # symbol by entering your topic or choosing from trending topics that appear (example: cats).
    • Tag a topic that includes a # symbol by entering # as the first character of your topic (example: #cats).
  3. When you’re ready, click Post in the bottom right. The text of the topic you tag in your post will appear blue.

Threads app for Android and iPhone

If people click the topic in your post, they’ll be shown search results for posts related to the topic.

Keep in mind that the topic you tag:

  • Can be up to 50 characters long.
  • May contain spaces and other special characters.
  • Doesn’t need to include the # symbol, but can if that is your preferred content strategy. Note: including the # symbol may enable additional functionality on other platforms when Threads becomes interoperable with the fediverse.

Learn why tagging certain topics isn’t allowed on Threads.

My ad was disapproved

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re based in or intend to target ads to audiences in the US and want to create an ad campaign that relates to credit, employment, housing, social issues or political ads, you must choose the category that best describes your ads from the Special Ad Category dropdown menu.

In most regions, an Apple service fee of 30% of your total ad payment, before any taxes and local fees, may apply when you add available funds to your ad account in the Instagram iOS app. This fee is retained by Apple, not Instagram or Meta. Learn how to avoid the Apple service fee when boosting on Instagram.

You can boost a post you create on Instagram to turn it into an ad and reach more people. When you create an ad using Ad tools on Instagram, you can choose whether your advertising goal is more profile visits, website visits or messages. Instagram posts that include product tags can also be boosted.

Learn how to boost an Instagram post from your computer and your mobile device.

Before you begin
  • Convert your profile to a business account.

Note: When you boost content on the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to pay with available funds. Learn how to add money to your ad account’s available balance. Available funds added through the iOS app will be charged through the Apple App Store, which retains a service fee on your total ad payment before applicable taxes and local fees. Applicable taxes and fees are not kept by Meta. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

Create ads directly from Instagram

To create an ad from Ad tools on Instagram:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap Professional dashboard.
  3. Tap Ad tools.
  4. Tap Choose a post.
  5. Choose a post or story that you’d like to boost.
  6. Tap Next.
  7. If you didn’t link to a Facebook Page when you set up your Instagram professional account, you will be prompted to connect a Page. You can choose an existing Page or tap Skip.
  8. If you tap Skip, you won’t see this step when you boost future posts. You can still connect a Facebook Page to your profile at any time.
  9. Fill in the details of your ad by setting things like Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next (iOS) or (Android) once you’ve completed these details.
  10. To complete your ad, tap Boost post under Review.

Your ad will be submitted for review to make sure it meets our ad policies. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

You’ll receive a notification in your Activity Feed after you submit an ad for review, when it’s getting reviewed, if it’s approved or disapproved and when the campaign ends.

After submitting your ad, you can use the Ad Tools section to view insights.

Before you begin
  • You need to have a public (personal or professional) account with at least 1,000 followers to use Instagram Live.

Available insights for live videos
  • Accounts reached: Number of unique accounts that have seen your content at least once during the live session.
  • Peak concurrent viewers: Highest number of viewers who were watching your live stream or video simultaneously at any given point during the broadcast.
  • Comments: Total number of comments left on your live video. This reflects the level of interaction and engagement from viewers.
  • Shares: Number of times your live content has been shared by viewers.
  • Accounts engaged: Total number of unique accounts that have interacted with your content through likes, comments, shares or other actions during the live video.

What audio you can use in your reel on Instagram

Android App Help

iPhone App Help

Computer Help

Add audio to my reel

Use original audio

My audio was muted

Remove reel from audio page

I have a different question

You can record a reel with your own original audio, with original audio by another Reels creator, or with audio from the Instagram audio library using the Audio tool in Reels. Note that you can’t use original audio from a feed video unless you remix the video.

You can also learn how to replace a muted audio track on your Instagram reel.

Original audio

Original audio is unique audio you created, either while filming your reel in the Instagram app or in a video you uploaded, or unique audio by another Reels creator. When someone posts a reel with original audio, it will display their username.

When you post a reel on a public account, anyone on Instagram, the Meta AI apps or Meta AI websites can record a reel using your original audio. You can turn this off for the Meta AI apps or websites at any time in your Instagram settings. Note: If you cross-post a public reel to Facebook, anyone on that app can create a reel with your original audio unless you’ve turned this off in your Facebook settings. Additionally, anyone on Instagram can record a reel using your original audio and crosspost it to their Facebook profile or Page.

To allow or disallow people on Meta AI apps or websites to create reels using your original audio:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Under How others can interact with you, tap Sharing and reuse.
  4. Under Allow people to create with and reuse your original audio on Meta AI, switch the toggle on or off next to Reels.

If you upload licensed audio as original audio, we may change the description to the artist’s name and song.

Licensed audio

Licensed audio is copyrighted audio available on the Instagram audio library and includes things like music, movies, TV shows and sound effects. All licensed audio must be attributed or linked to the artist and include the name of the track.

Keep in mind that as we make sure to uphold our agreements with music rights holders, audio tracks in your posts can become muted as a result of any changes made to these agreements. While the audio tracks of your post may be muted, your post can still be viewed.

Notification that your reel was added to an audio page

When we detect the audio you recorded or uploaded uses licensed audio, we’ll automatically change attribution from Original Audio to the artist and song title. Your reel will be added to the audio page for that song, where more people on Instagram may find it.

What if the attribution is wrong?

If we’ve identified the wrong audio track, you can remove your reel from the audio page.

On Android, tap Options at the bottom of the reel, then tap Remove From Audio Page.

On iPhone, tap Options at the bottom of the reel, then tap Remove From Audio Page.

Your audio will be attributed to you and will say Original Audio next to your username.

What happens if you repeatedly post content on Instagram or Threads that violates someone else’s intellectual property rights

My account was disabled

What is repeat infringer policy?

My content was restored

I have a different question

By using Instagram or Threads, you have agreed to our Terms of Use, which prohibit people from taking any action on Instagram or Threads that infringes or violates someone else’s intellectual property rights or otherwise violates the law.

Repeat Infringer Policy

If you repeatedly post content that infringes someone else’s intellectual property rights, such as copyrights or trademarks, your account may be disabled or your Page removed under Instagram’s repeat infringer policy.

Under this policy, your ability to post photos or videos may be limited, and you could also lose access to certain features or functionality on Instagram or Threads. The actions taken under the policy may depend on the nature of the reported content and where it was posted.

If something you posted is restored due to an appeal or because a rights owner withdrew their report, we’ll take that restoration into account under our repeat infringer policy.

Learn more about what you can do if you believe your account was disabled by mistake.

Get more information on how to avoid copyright infringement when posting to Instagram or Threads in the frequently asked questions article.

How Instagram recommends reels?

Why my reels are not shown?

Reels not appearing in feed

I have a different question

On Instagram, you can find and view public and suggested reels in places like the Reels tab, Explore, and in your feed. You’ll see reels from accounts you follow and from suggested accounts. The suggested reels you see are recommended to you based on a variety of factors, including which accounts you follow and the reels you’ve watched, liked, or engaged with recently.

How Instagram recommends reels
  • May be entertaining for a wide audience
  • Can inspire people to create (for example, start a trend others can participate in)
  • Have music from the Instagram music library or original audio made with the Reels audio tool
  • Are filmed vertically
  • Show events that are meaningful and relevant to our community
Reels you may see less often
  • Are muted, blurry, or low resolution
  • Contain borders, logos, or watermarks
  • Have the majority of the image covered by text
  • Are not original videos
  • Go against our Community Standards (for example, contain hateful conduct or graphic violence) or our Recommendation Guidelines

Note: Reels from people you follow will still be shown on their profile and in your feed, and we won’t make them less visible. Learn how to find reels to watch on Instagram.

Visit the Meta Transparency Center for information on how artificial intelligence (AI) selects, ranks, and delivers the content you see on Instagram Reels.

What to do if content you posted on Instagram or Threads gets removed because it was reported for intellectual property infringement

My content was removed

Appeal a copyright removal

Contact rights owner

I have a different question

If we remove content you posted because of an intellectual property report submitted through our online form, you’ll receive a notification that may include the name and email address of the rights owner who made the report and/or other details of the report. If you believe the content shouldn’t have been removed, you can follow up with the rights owner directly to try to resolve the issue.

If your content was removed because of a copyright report, you can submit an appeal. Learn more about our appeals process or how to use music in your videos on Instagram or Threads.

What to do if you don’t think Instagram should have taken down your post

Request a review

Check review status

Appeal to Oversight Board

I have a different question

We remove content (example: post, comment, story) from Instagram when we find that it goes against our Community Guidelines. Our Community Guidelines define what is and isn’t allowed on Instagram, and they apply all over the world. They’re designed to encourage expression and create a safe environment on Instagram.

We know we don’t always get it right when we decide to remove a post. If your post was taken down and you think it doesn’t go against our Community Guidelines, you can request a review in most circumstances. For some types of content, you can’t request a review, but we’re adding more options.

We use both technology and people around the globe to review content that we’ve been asked to look at again. Certain appeals may be prioritized for human review, which can limit the amount of requests we’re able to look at. Note: Because of this, it may take up to 90 days to hear back from us about our decision, but your request may be closed before we can review it.

There are a few ways to ask us to review our decision. When you receive the notification about your violation to learn more about why your content was removed, tap Ask for a review at the bottom and follow the on-screen instructions. You can also request a review from Account Status or Support Inbox.

When you request a review, we’ll take another look at the decision we made about your post.

Request a review from Account Status

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below More info and support, tap Help.
  4. Tap Account Status, then tap Removed content.
  5. Tap Removed content.
  6. Tap the content that was removed, then tap Request a review.
  7. Select the reason why you want another review, then tap Continue.
  8. Tap Submit, then tap Done.

Instagram app for iPad

Request a review from Support Inbox

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below More info and support, tap Help.
  4. Tap Support Requests, then tap Violations.
  5. Open the update we sent you about our decision.
  6. Tap See options at the bottom.
  7. Tap Request review, then follow on-screen instructions.

You can check the status of your review request at any time by opening Account Status or tapping the violation in your Support Inbox.

Instagram app for iPad

Once you ask us to take another look, your content will be reviewed again by Instagram. Once we’ve made a decision, you’ll receive a push notification. If we find we’ve made a mistake, we’ll let you know and your content will be reposted.

If you request a review and still don’t agree with our decision, you may be able to appeal to the Oversight Board. Keep in mind that not all decisions are eligible for appeal to the Oversight Board and the board only selects a certain number of eligible appeals, so they may not choose yours to review. You can read more about the board’s bylaws and structure on their website.

Learn more about how Instagram uses technology and review teams to detect, review, and take action on content.

What to do if your Instagram account posts unauthorized content

My account is posting content

Secure my Instagram account

Remove third-party apps

I think my account was hacked

I have a different question

If your Instagram account is leaving comments or sharing things that you haven’t posted, your password may be compromised. Additionally, if inauthentic activity is detected on your account, you may see an error message that says, “Try again later” when using Instagram.

If you can log in to your Instagram account, there are several things you can do to secure your account:

  • Change your password or send yourself a password reset email. Be sure to pick a strong and unique password. Use a combination of at least six numbers, letters and special characters (like !$@%), and try to avoid repetition. Note: Whenever you change your Instagram password, any devices logged into your Instagram account will automatically be logged out and you’ll need to sign in again.
  • Revoke access on Instagram to any suspicious third-party apps. You should never share your login information with an app you don’t trust. If you give these apps your login information, whether with an access token or by giving them your username and password, they can gain complete access to your account.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication for additional account security.
  • Confirm your phone number and email address in account settings are correct.
  • Check Accounts Center and remove any linked accounts you don’t recognize.

If you think your account has been hacked or taken over, there are other actions you may be able to take to secure your account. If someone gains access to your account or you’re unable to log in, visit this page on your desktop or mobile browser to secure your account.

Beware of scams

Be careful before giving third party apps or websites access to your Instagram account. In particular, you shouldn’t use apps that offer likes and followers in exchange for your Instagram login details. These websites and apps are likely attempts to use your account in an inappropriate way.

Learn more about how to avoid scams on Instagram.

Who can create a remix of your reels, videos, and photos on Instagram

Turn off remixing

Manage remix settings

Remixing for private accounts

Remixing for users under 18

I have a different question

The default remix settings of your reels, feed videos, and photos depends on your account’s privacy setting:

  • For private accounts: No one can remix your reels, feed videos, and photos.
  • For public accounts: Anyone on Instagram can remix your reels, feed videos, and photos shared after remixing became available.

At any time, you can turn off remixing for reels, feed videos, and photos or any combination without changing your account’s privacy settings. You can also turn remixing off for individual reels, feed videos, and photos from each post.

Manage who can remix your reels, feed videos, and photos

Instagram app for Android and iPhone:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below How others can interact with you, tap Sharing and reuse.
  4. Below Allow people to create with and reuse your content, tap or next to Posts or Reels to turn remixing on or off.

Note: changing this setting will affect all of your reels, feed videos, and photos. Turning off remixing won’t affect who can use your original audio.

Instagram app for iPad:

Instagram users under 18

Instagram users under 18 may further restrict who can remix their content by audience: everyone, people you follow, or no one. The default setting is “people you follow.”

You can manage this preference on the same screen as you turn remixing on or off.

Manage who can remix an individual reel, feed video, and photo

Instagram app for Android:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap the reel or photo you want to manage, then tap Options in the bottom right.
  3. From here you can tap Remixing, then:
    • Tap Turn off reuse and then Turn off to confirm. No one will be able to create new remixes with this video or photo, but existing remixes won’t be affected unless you delete your video or photo.
    • Tap Allow reuse and then Allow to confirm. Anyone will be able to create a remix with this video or photo.

Instagram app for iPhone:

Instagram app for iPad:

Notes
  • You’ll receive a notification if a public account remixes your content.
  • Reels can be remixed on Instagram and then shared to Facebook. However, remixed Reels that are shared to Facebook cannot be remixed further on Facebook.
  • Remixes will be deleted if you set your account to private for longer than 24 hours.
  • Remix creators can download your content as part of their remix. You can’t download remixes others have created with your reel, feed video, or photo.
  • If you turn off remixing, remixes of your reels, feed videos, and photos created before you changed your setting will stay on Instagram unless you delete your post.
  • If you restore a video or photo you’ve deleted within 30 days, all the remixes of your video or photo will also be restored.
  • If you allow your Instagram reel to be recommended on Facebook, remixes of that reel on Instagram can also be shared to Facebook or recommended to others on Facebook.
  • Deleting your reel or photo will also delete remixes created with it, including remixes shared to Facebook. You can also learn how to delete reels you’ve shared to Facebook. When your video or photo is indexed by search engines it may take time for search engines to de-index and remove remixes of your content, after you have deleted the reel or photo.
  • Depending on the settings of the account remixing your content, the remix may be indexable for search engines. Learn more about how content in Instagram can appear in search engine results.

Who can see and share your reels on Instagram

Who can see my reels?

Who can share my reels?

Turn off reel remixing

Turn off reel downloads

I have a different question

Who can see and share your reels follows your account’s privacy settings:

  • For public accounts: Anyone on Instagram can see and share your reels. People may see your reels on places like Feed, the Reels viewer, Explore and audio, effect and hashtag pages. Anyone on Instagram can record a reel using your original audio or text. Anyone can remix your reel, unless you turn off remixing in your account settings or on individual reels. Anyone can download your reel, unless you turn off reel downloads in your account settings or on individual reels.
  • For private accounts: Only your approved followers can see and share your reels. When someone shares your reel, only your followers will be able to see it. No one will be able to record a reel using your original audio or text or remix your reel.

Note that reels you share will appear in the Reels section on your Instagram profile. Who can see your profile also depends on your account’s privacy settings.

Reels include the videos you record or upload and the elements you add (effects, stickers, music, etc.). We sometimes save those components separately to enable product functionality, like translations, and for other processing consistent with our Privacy Policy.

Instagram reels on Facebook

If you choose to share your Instagram reels to Facebook, who can see your reels on Facebook depends on your Facebook audience settings. Learn how to update your audience setting by visiting the Facebook Help Center.

If you haven’t selected a default audience for reels on Facebook, your default audience will be based on your Instagram account’s privacy setting:

  • Public Instagram account: Your Facebook Reels audience will default to Public.
  • Private Instagram account: Your Facebook Reels audience will default to Friends on Facebook.

If your account is public and you choose to have your Instagram reels recommended on Facebook, your reels can be recommended to anyone based on what may be relevant to them.

Why certain posts on Instagram are not appearing in Explore and search results

Why can’t I find my post?

Why isn’t my hashtag searchable?

What are Community Standards?

What are Recommendation Guidelines?

I have a different question

Instagram has Community Standards that define what’s allowed in order to keep Instagram an authentic and safe place for inspiration and expression. If we’re made aware of a post that goes against our Community Standards, we’ll remove it from Instagram.

While some posts on Instagram may not go against our Community Standards, they might not be appropriate for our global community, and we’ll limit those types of posts from being recommended in places like Explore and search results. For example, a sexually suggestive post will still appear in Feed if you follow the account that posts it, but this type of content may not appear for the broader community in Explore and search results.

We only limit this type of content from accounts you don’t follow, you’ll still see content from all accounts you follow.

We’re working to ensure that the content we recommend is both safe and appropriate for our community, and that means we’re stricter about what content and accounts are recommended to people on Explore and search results.

Keep in mind:

  • Not all posts or accounts are eligible to be surfaced in Explore and search results. We use a variety of signals, for example, if an account has recently gone against our Community Standards, to determine which posts and accounts can be recommended to the community.
  • If content goes against our Recommendation Guidelines, it may be considered upsetting, offensive, or sensitive and we may make it harder to find, rather than removing it from Instagram. We’ve previously limited content like this in Explore, Search, Reels, Accounts You Might Follow and Recommendations. However, you and others can now choose to see more or less content and accounts that could be upsetting or offensive using the Sensitive Content Control.
  • If you see a post on search results or Explore that you think goes against our Community Standards, you can report it to us so we can take a closer look. If a post goes against our Community Standards, we’ll remove it from Instagram.
  • You can check your Account status at any time to find out if you’ve posted something that goes against Community Standards.

Learn more about why certain hashtags aren’t searchable.

Why posts on Instagram may be marked as false information

Why was my post marked false?

Who are the fact-checkers?

What happens to false information?

I have a different question

At Instagram, we’re committed to reducing the spread of false information.

You may come across a post on Instagram that’s been marked as false information by an independent third-party fact checker. We work with third-party fact-checkers across the globe who review content in over 60 languages and are certified through the non-partisan International Fact-Checking Network to help identify, review and label false information.

When third-party fact checkers identify false information, altered content or content with missing context on Instagram, we may make it harder to find by filtering it from Explore and Hashtags, and reducing its visibility in Feed and Stories. We also help people to decide for themselves what to read, trust and share by giving them more information on posts with false information warnings. See here and here for our approach in the United States.

Keep in mind that the original content of politicians is not sent to third-party fact checkers for review. You can learn more about how Facebook and Instagram fact-check political speech.

If a post has been identified by a third-party fact checker as false information, altered content or content with missing context, you can:

  • Tap See Why to view the fact-checking organization and why they identified the post as false information.
  • Tap See Post to view the post.

Learn more about tips for identifying false information on Instagram.

Why search engines might index public Instagram photos and videos

Remove my images from Google

Turn off search indexing

My images still appear

What happens to my data?

I have a different question

Search indexing is the process of organizing and storing information from the internet so that third party search engines can find it quickly and efficiently when you search for something. When content is indexed by third party search engines, they can show it in their search engine results to anyone on the internet. Meta does not own or control third party search engines. Third party search engines and others who access your content through search engine results may use your information at their discretion.

Instagram generally requests that search engines like Google and Microsoft Bing do not index the content of users’ photos and videos from stories, reels, posts, and highlights. However, we allow search engines to index photos and videos from public reels and posts that were uploaded or posted from January 1, 2020 onwards from accounts that meet all criteria listed below:

  • The account holder is currently over 18.
  • The account is currently public.
  • The account is currently a professional account.

Once an account meets the criteria for allowing search engines to index, all of the photos and videos from public reels, story highlights and posts posted by the account can be indexed–including those from before you turned 18.

Note: When you allow others (including users with professional accounts) on Instagram to remix or reshare your content, your remixed or reshared content may be indexed and displayed in search engine results. Learn more about how to control who can remix your content or who can reshare your content.

Search engines can process personal data from what’s visible on your profile for their own purposes, and their use of your data is subject to their own terms and privacy policies. Please refer to those policies for more information about the processing of your personal data by search engines and your rights under applicable privacy and/or data protection laws.

How to turn off indexing

If your account meets the criteria above (meaning if you are 18 or older, and have a public professional account) and you don’t want eligible public photos and videos from your Instagram reels, story highlights and posts to appear in search engine results like Google and Microsoft Bing, you can always do one of the following:

  • Visit your account privacy settings to turn off the ability for your public photos and videos to appear in search engine results.
  • Set your account to private.
  • Set your account from professional to personal.

It may take time for these third party search engines to de-index and remove your public photo and video content from search results, even if you delete your account. Your profile information, including your username, profile picture and bio information, may still appear in third party search engine results.

Keep in mind that we can’t guarantee if or when the third party search engine will de-index and remove your content. You can learn more about removing an image from Google’s search results from the Google Help Center, and on the Microsoft Bing website about how to block search results.

What happens to my video selfie?

I have a different question

Why you might be asked to upload a selfie to confirm your identity on Instagram

Sometimes you may be asked to upload a video selfie to confirm that you are who are say you are and that you’re a real person.

Why we use selfies

Instagram uses selfies to confirm your identity because photos and IDs can be digitally modified. By using a selfie that asks you to turn your head in different directions, we know you’re a real person.

While we review your video selfie, you will not have access to your account until we confirm that it’s you.

If you pass our review, you may receive an email from Instagram at the secure email address that you provided and receive a link to reset your password.

If you do not pass our review, you’ll receive an email from Instagram at the secure email address that you provided and you may be able to resubmit your selfie in the Instagram app.

If you choose not to confirm your identity with a selfie, you may not be able to log back in to your account.

Where is Meta Pay available?

Does name change affect me?

How do I use Meta Pay?

Is Meta collecting new data?

I have a different question

As part of Facebook company becoming Meta, Facebook Pay is now Meta Pay. If you’re an existing Facebook Pay user, there is no action required on your part. All of your existing Facebook Pay information will remain the same in Meta Pay, including account details, your payment method, and settings.

If you’re a new user, learn how to get started with Meta Pay.

Where is Meta Pay available?

Meta Pay is available across Meta technologies, including Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp, and anywhere you see the Meta Pay button when shopping online. Meta Pay will roll out globally over time, so you may still see Facebook Pay in some places when paying.

Why is Facebook Pay now called Meta Pay?

Facebook Pay is now called Meta Pay to align with Facebook’s company rebrand to Meta.

Does the name change to Meta Pay affect existing Facebook Pay users?

There is no change to the way existing Facebook Pay users use Meta Pay. Current Facebook Pay users can use Meta Pay immediately. All existing Facebook Pay information including account details, your payment method, and settings will stay the same.

How do I use Meta Pay to make purchases going forward?

Meta Pay works in the same way as Facebook Pay. To shop, donate, and send money across Meta technologies or to make purchases using the Meta Pay button, you’ll need to have Meta Pay linked with a payment method.

If you’ve already linked a payment method to Facebook Pay, there is no action needed on your part. Your current payment method linked in Facebook Pay will be available in Meta Pay.

Are my purchases protected with purchase protection when paying with Meta Pay?

Our Purchase Protection policy has not changed. Purchase Protection is available on eligible products bought with Meta Pay on Facebook and Instagram. Purchases made from third-party sites, other messaging services, local pickups, or sending money on Messenger with Meta Pay do not qualify for Purchase Protection.

Is Meta collecting new or additional data from Meta Pay users?

There are no changes to existing data collection or data use. Learn more about Meta’s data policy.

What payment information will be stored and protected with Meta Pay?

When you make payments with Meta Pay, we’ll collect information about your purchase such as your payment method, transaction date, billing, shipping, and contact details. Your payment card numbers are encrypted and securely stored.
