Hide message requests

I can’t hide comments

I have a different question

For Teens Accounts, the settings to hide unwanted comments and message requests will be turned on automatically. Teens under 16 will need their parent’s or guardian’s permission to update these settings. Changing the default settings could allow more people, including people you may not know, to send you message requests. You can always, view, delete or report the request. Some comments will also be hidden or filtered out entirely based on the content setting for teens, which hides content that’s inappropriate for people under 18. Teen Accounts are placed into the 13+ content setting by default.

There are a few ways you can hide potentially offensive comments and message requests you don’t want to see on Instagram.

Content that doesn’t go against our Community Standards, but may be age-inappropriate, disrespectful, or offensive (example: racial slurs, curse words, or scams) can be hidden using Hide unwanted comments and Hide spam. You can also create a custom list of words, phrases, numbers, and emojis you want to hide using Hidden Words.

Keep in mind that hidden comments are still included in your total comment count and when a comment or message is hidden, the person who sent it won’t know.

Automatically hide offensive words or phrases

You can choose to automatically hide comments and message requests you don’t want to see by turning on the following settings:

  • Hide unwanted comments: Comments containing common offensive words, phrases, or emojis that are likely to be abusive or mean, such as insults, sexual remarks, or personal attacks against an individual or group, are automatically hidden. This setting is on by default, but you can change it any time.
  • Hide unwanted message requests: Message requests that may contain scams or offensive words, phrases or emojis will appear in your spam folder. This setting is off by default, but you can change it any time. Note: Instagram cannot see your messages unless you report them. This feature is not currently supported on web browsers or Meta Quest.

To turn on automatic comment or message filtering

On Instagram.com, you can manage:

  1. Hidden Words to update your custom words and phrases list.

(Comment and message request filtering options may vary on web and may not be available in all experiences.)

Manage custom words and phrases

You can also add words, phrases, numbers or emojis that you don’t want to see in comments and message requests to your list of Custom words and phrases. These will be hidden from comments in posts you share and message requests. You can edit this list at any time. Note: This feature for message requests is not currently supported on web browsers.

To manage your custom word list

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Below How others can interact with you, click Hidden Words.
  3. Click Manage custom words and phrases at the bottom.
  4. Enter specific words, phrases, numbers or emojis you want to hide in the text box. Click Submit to save the list. Note: Separate each entry by a comma.
Manually hide comments on your posts

To manually hide or unhide comments on your posts

To manually hide a comment on your post:

  1. Log into your Instagram account using a mobile app on an iOS or Android device.
  2. Go to the comment you want to hide and tap Hide under the comment.

Please note: You can only manually hide comments under your own posts. When you manually hide comments, they are only visible to you and the person who made the comment. Other people won’t be able to see the comment after it’s been hidden and the commenter won’t be able to see that it’s been hidden.

To manually unhide a comment on your post:

  1. Log into your Instagram account using a mobile app on an iOS or Android device.
  2. Go to the post where the comment is hidden. At the bottom of the comment section, tap View hidden comments.
  3. Tap Unhide under the comment you wish to unhide.

How community notes work on Instagram and Threads

How do community notes work?

How to become a contributor?

What happens if I get a note?

I have a different question

Community Notes is currently in beta and only available in the US on iOS and Android devices. Some features might be unavailable.

If you find a bug while Community Notes is still in beta, you can report it by shaking your phone.

Community notes are written by contributors on Facebook, Instagram and Threads to help keep you better informed about a post that might be misleading or confusing. A community note may be shown on the post if enough contributors with different views have agreed that it’s helpful.

How to participate

Anyone on Facebook, Instagram and Threads can view a community note on a post. Only contributors can write a community note or rate other contributors’ notes as helpful or not helpful. Meta does not decide which community notes get rated or published.

To become a contributor, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Have a Facebook, Instagram or Threads account that’s at least 6 months old.
  • Have a verified phone number or have two-factor authentication enabled.
  • Have an account that hasn’t repeatedly broken Meta’s rules.
  • Have joined the waitlist to be a contributor on Instagram or on Threads.

Note: Contributors can sign up for each app. Visit the Facebook Help Center to learn how to join the waitlist for Instagram and Threads.

Keep in mind:

  • Community notes won’t have author names attached. That means people on Facebook, Instagram or Threads can’t see the name or photo of the contributor who wrote a note. They also can’t see the names or photos of the contributors who rated the note helpful.
  • Names and photos of contributors will be visible to Meta’s internal systems to ensure that community notes follow Meta’s Community Standards.
  • Details that contributors choose to include in their community note could reveal their identity.
How community notes work

How to write and rate notes

How rating works

How matching works

Impact on speech

Meta’s platforms are built to be places where people can express themselves freely. When a community note appears on a post, it won’t affect who can see that content or how widely it can be shared. If a community note appears on your post, you will receive a notification. You won’t be able to remove the note.

Meta may still remove content that goes against the Community Standards. It may also remove misinformation when it could lead to physical harm or could interfere with an election or civic process.

How Instagram and Threads process United States Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) counter-notifications

My content was removed

File a counter-notification

What happens to my content?

How long does this take?

I have a different question

Instagram and Threads comply with the notice-and-takedown procedures set out in section 512(c) of the United States Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), which applies to content reported and removed for violating U.S. copyrights.

If your content is removed under the DMCA, you’ll receive instructions about how to file a counter-notification in the messages we send you. You should only submit a counter-notification if the content was removed because of a mistake or misidentification. Please note that if your content was removed for reasons unrelated to a copyright report, you may not receive a response from us.

When we receive a valid DMCA counter-notification, we forward it to the party that reported the content. The information they receive includes your contact information, which they can use to contact you. If we provide your counter-notification to the party that reported the content, and they don’t notify us that they have filed a court action seeking an order to keep the content down, we will restore or cease disabling eligible content under the DMCA. This process can take up to 14 business days. Please note, in rare instances, we may not be able to restore content due to technical limitations. If this happens, we’ll send you an update letting you know you may repost the content at your discretion.

Content that is restored based on an effective DMCA counter-notification will not be counted against you under our repeat infringer policy.

How rating works for community notes on Instagram and Threads

What is consensus?

Why is consensus important?

What do note statuses mean?

I have a different question

Community Notes is a feature designed to publish notes that are helpful to the widest range of people by considering not just the number of contributors who rate a note as helpful or unhelpful, but also whether those contributors represent different perspectives. When this happens, we say that a note has reached consensus.

Why consensus matters

Consensus means that a diverse group of contributors—people with different perspectives and rating histories (example: they’ve rated notes differently in the past)—agree that a note adds valuable context to a post. This helps ensure that notes are not biased and reflect a broad understanding of the topic.

Requiring agreement from people with different perspectives helps ensure notes are fair and not one-sided.

Note statuses

In your Community Notes home, you’ll see notes with a few different statuses:

  • Needs more ratings: This means the note hasn’t reached consensus.
  • People agreed this note is helpful: This means the note has reached a “helpful” consensus, and is (or may soon be) published on the post.
  • People agreed this note is not helpful: This means the note has reached a “not helpful” consensus, and isn’t published anywhere.

To learn more about the status of a note, the author and how people rated it, you select Options on the note.

The consensus status of a note can change

As more contributors review and rate notes, or as new information becomes available, the status of a note may change. If you want to contribute, focus on providing clear, factual, and neutral information—this increases the chances that your note will reach consensus and be published.

How to handle threats to share private images or personal info

Report a threat

Block someone threatening me

What if I’m under 18?

I have a different question

**We worked with ConnectSafely.org on the following answer. To learn more, please visit http://www.connectsafely.org/.**

If someone is threatening to share things you intended to be private and asking you to send them money or anything else, you have options:

  • Contact local law enforcement and report this to them.
  • Report this person to us.
  • Block this person. Depending on your privacy settings, people on Instagram can see a list of your followers and who you follow. Once you block someone, they no longer have access to your profile.

The safest thing you can do is never share something you wouldn’t want other people seeing, even if you feel like you trust the person asking you to share.

If you’re under 18

If you’re under 18, we recommend talking with a parent or other adult you trust to help you think through what to do. We offer some tips for parents on safety and security on Instagram. Here are other resources for you to consider:

  • Contact a crisis hotline or chat service. These can be found all over the US and in many other countries. This is a good option if you want to remain anonymous while deciding what to do. Crisis lines can also often refer you to a victim advocate or other legal adviser near you. In the US, you can search for one by zip code at www.suicidepreventionlifeline.org/our-network/ or visit www.crisischat.org/.
  • Talk with a victim advocate or social worker in your town or city. In the US, there are victim advocates in county offices, police stations, domestic violence prevention centers, rape crisis centers, sheriff’s offices and offices of state attorneys general. Victim advocates can help you gather evidence, figure out how to keep you safe and get a civil protection or anti-stalking order against the person threatening you. If you’re in the US, call the National Organization for Victim Assistance at 1-800-TRY-NOVA/800-879-6682 or go to www.trynova.org.
  • Contact a legal aid society or organization near you for free advice.
  • Ask a lawyer or other counselor for advice.
  • Talk to a school counselor or administrator.

How to see shared activity on Instagram

See shared activity

Manage shared activity

What can I see?

I have a different question

Shared activity is currently only available on mobile devices and iPads.

Shared activity lets you see the tags, likes and comments you share with other accounts on Instagram. You can also see how long you’ve followed an account, and how long accounts have followed you. Shared activity is only available when one or both accounts follow each other.

When using shared activity, you can see the photos and reels where you’ve tagged each other, or liked and commented on each other’s content. You can also directly manage your shared activity by removing or deleting shared content.

See shared activity
  1. Open Instagram on your mobile device or iPad.
  2. Navigate to a profile of someone you follow or who follows you.
  3. Tap Options for iphone or Options for android in the top right.
  4. Select See shared activity.

You can also find shared activity by navigating to your Instagram profile and tapping Following, selecting Options or Options next to the profile, and choosing See shared activity.

What you can see on shared activity
  • Tags: Photos and reels where you and the other account tagged one another.
  • Likes: Likes made on one another’s photos and reels.
  • Comments: Comments made on one another’s photos and reels.
  • Follows: See when you followed each other, if applicable.

How to share an Instagram account with someone

Invite someone to my account

Manage shared access invites

Allow inbox access

View shared access activity

I have a different question

Shared access is only available to eligible Instagram accounts. This feature is not available to teens. Learn more about shared access if you’ve been invited to share an account.

With shared access, you can invite people, depending on eligibility, to your account so they can post content, like or comment on posts, and more without sharing your password. After you give someone shared access, you can control what they can view or do and see what actions they take on your account.

If you subscribe to a Meta One plan, you can invite a certain number of people to share access to your account based on your plan.

  • Meta One Advanced plan: Invite up to 4 people.
  • Meta One Expert plan: Invite up to 8 people.
  • Meta One Max plan: Invite up to 30 people.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta One.

Invite people to access your account

To invite someone to share access to your account:

  1. Tap Your profile or your profile picture in the bottom right.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Shared access.
  4. Tap Invite people.
  5. Find people to invite from the search bar.
  6. Tap Send invite.

People you invite to your account will have 7 days to accept will receive a notification and will have 7 days to accept. You’ll get a notification when they accept or decline your request, or if your request expires. If the request expires, you can resend the invitation.

Manage your shared access invites

To manage shared access invites:

  1. From Instagram, tap Your profile or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Menu.
  3. Tap Shared access.

From here you can:

  • See people you’ve shared access with.
  • See people you’ve invited to share access with.
  • Manage account activity, invite new people, and see people whose access has been removed.
Allow people to access your Instagram inbox

You can choose who has access to your messages, including who can view, send and respond to messages and make or receive calls from your inbox. Please note that access to your messages also includes access to your chats with Meta AI.

To choose who has shared access to your Instagram inbox:

  1. Tap Your profile or your profile picture in the bottom right.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Shared access.
  4. Tap Inbox access under Manage.
  5. Tap Toggle to the right of the person’s profile to grant inbox access.
  6. Tap Allow to confirm. When you allow inbox access, people will see that your account is shared in the Instagram chat.

You can tap Toggle to remove inbox access.

Allow people to add to your story on Instagram

You can choose who can add to your story from your Instagram account. People who accept your invite won’t have story access unless you allow it.

To choose who has shared access to your Instagram stories:

  1. Tap Your profile or your profile picture in the bottom right.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Shared access.
  4. Tap Story access under Manage.
  5. Tap Toggle to the right of the person’s profile to grant story access.
  6. Tap Allow to confirm.

You can tap Toggle to remove story access.

View shared access account activity

To view any actions taken on your account by people you’ve shared access with:

  1. Tap Your profile or your profile picture in the bottom right.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Shared access.

From here you can see some shared access activity on your account or see activity taken by one specific person only. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Shared posts and reels.
  • Comments on posts.
  • Liked posts.
  • New follows.

To see all shared access activity, tap Account activity. To see individual account activity, tap Options to the right of their profile, then tap Account activity.

How to write and rate community notes on Instagram or Threads

How to write community notes?

How to rate community notes?

What content is not eligible?

I have a different question

If you’re a contributor, you can add a community note to public posts you find in your Feed on Facebook, Instagram and Threads. Some content isn’t eligible for community notes like ads, reels, stories, and posts with limited audiences.

Writing a note
  1. Open Instagram or Threads on your device.
  2. From your profile, select for Instagram or for Threads and tap Community Notes.
  3. Tap Write at the top to find a posts that could use helpful context.
  4. Tap Write note.
  5. Add any additional information or helpful context.
    • Notes must be less than 500 characters
    • Only include links or URLs in the source section
  6. Add a link to a source that supports your note.
    • It’s required to add a link, and it will be shown with the community note
    • You can only add one link to your note.
  7. Select Submit to make your community note available for other contributors to rate its helpfulness. A submitted community note won’t be seen until enough contributors agree that it’s helpful.

Note: You can also write community notes from your Facebook Feed by selecting the Menu. You won’t be able to edit your note after you submit it.

Rating a note
  1. Open Instagram or Threads on your device.
  2. From your profile, select for Instagram or for Threads and tap Community Notes.
  3. Tap Rate at the top to see community notes that contributors submitted.
  4. Read the post and the community note submitted for the post, and select Helpful if the note provides helpful context, or Not helpful if the note doesn’t provide helpful context.
  5. Check the boxes for why you think the note is or isn’t helpful, then select Rate.
    • You can’t change or remove your rating

Note: You can only rate community notes from the same app you’re currently using (example: When rating community notes from Instagram, you’ll only see Instagram notes).

Find your notes and ratings

You can view the community notes you’ve rated and created from the Your contributions tab in the top right.

From here you can see if other contributors have rated your note and the reasons they selected. You can also delete your community note from this tab. Nobody will be able to see or rate your deleted note, and any ratings on the note will be lost.

Learn more about how to write helpful community notes.

What is a shared connection?

View shared connections as a teen

I have a different question

If you supervise your teen’s account on Instagram, you can visit Family Center to see the number of shared connections for each account your teen is following and each account your teen is followed by. A shared connection can be either of the following:

  • An account your teen follows who is also following another account your teen follows.
  • An account your teen follows who is also following an account who follows your teen.

For example, your teen, whose username is stellas_gr00v3, follows two accounts: e.manny.well.52 and lil_wyatt838. One of them, e.manny.well.52, also follows lil_wyatt838. This means that the user e.manny.well.52 is your teen’s shared connection with lil_wyatt838.

If you’re a teen who is supervised by a parent, you can also see what your parent sees and view your own shared connections.

Viewing shared connections as a parent

To view your teen’s shared connections:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision.
  3. In the left menu, under Accounts, click on your teen’s account.
  4. Under Followers and following, click See more.
  5. Click the Following or Followers tab.
  6. Scroll down to view the profiles your teen is following or that are following your teen. The number of shared connections will be under the username and name of a connection.

You can tap on any of the accounts on these lists to see their Instagram profile. Keep in mind that some Instagram accounts are private, so you will not be able to see a private account’s posts unless you also follow that account.

Viewing shared connections as a teen
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision.
  3. Click View what they can see.
  4. Click See more.
  5. Click the Following or Followers tab.
  6. Scroll down to view the profiles you are following or that are following you. The number of shared connections will be under the username and name of a connection.

How do I share an invite link?

How do I copy an invite link?

How do I reset an invite link?

How do I turn off an invite link?

I have a different question

Anyone in a group chat can share a link with others to join their conversation on Threads. Note: the chat admin needs to create an invite link to get started.

Share an invite link
  1. Click Messages.
  2. Click the group chat you’d like to share.
  3. Click More in the top right.
  4. Click Invite link. From here, you can:
    • Click the group chat link to copy it.
    • Send in Threads to share the invite link as a message in another chat.
    • Create post to share the link in a Threads post.
Keep in mind
  • When the invite link is on, admin approval to join the chat is required. Anyone with the link can see group chat info and request to join, but the admin can decide which requests to approve.
  • The chat admin can choose to reset the invite link at any time. When the link is reset, the old link can no longer be used to join the group chat.
  • If the chat admin changes, the invite link is also reset.
  • When a chat admin turns off an invite link, the link will no longer work and can’t be shared with others.

What can AI do?

This feature currently isn’t available to everyone.

When you start an Instagram chat with an AI, you can:

  • Ask questions and get advice
  • Receive recommendations for stickers, GIFs and text
  • Talk about shared interests

You can chat with Meta AI and custom AIs created by other people on Instagram and Messenger. You can also chat with other AIs created by Meta.

Start a chat with an AI
  1. Go to aistudio.instagram.com using a computer.
  2. Click Discover.
  3. Click on an AI, or search for one.
  4. Enter a message or click a message prompt. Note: Be mindful before including any personal information in your message (examples: name, address, email, or phone number).
  5. Click Send.

You can provide feedback on the AI’s response by hovering over the response, then clicking Thumbs up or Thumbs down.

AIs you choose to chat with may send follow up messages on previous conversations. You can turn these AI-initiated messages off using the Instagram app for iPhone and Android.

Note

  • Similar to other chats, interactions with AI are subject to our Community Standards and Terms of Service.

  • An AI’s response may be inaccurate or inappropriate and should not be used to make important decisions.

  • Meta uses your interactions with AIs to improve AI at Meta. If the AIs cannot answer your query, Meta shares the messages you send to AI and general information, like your region, with select partners so you can get better results. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service to learn more.

  • Meta AI uses your location information to give you more relevant responses. Your location information is based on things like the settings you’ve chosen on your device, or your activity across our products. Learn more about how to manage your location in the Privacy Center.

  • Other information from your profile such as your age and gender, and interests based on your activity across our products, such as the types of content, including ads, you view or interact with and how you interact with it, will be used to help personalize your interactions with AI. Learn more about how Meta uses this information in the Privacy Center. You can also see how information is used across your accounts in the same Accounts Center and export your information. Learn how to Export a copy of your information.

  • Depending on your prompt, the content generated may go against our Community Standards or Terms of Service of Meta’s platforms. Sharing AI-generated content on our platforms that go against these standards will be treated the same as sharing other content that go against our standards. If you share generated content that goes against our standards, your content may be removed and your account may be restricted or disabled. Learn more about the Community Standards and Terms of Service on:

    • Facebook, Messenger and Instagram
    • WhatsApp

  • Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products can be used to personalize content and ads.

  • If you permanently delete a chat with an AI on aistudio.instagram.com and start a new conversation with the same AI, your previous messages will no longer be available.

  • People who create an AI in Meta AI Studio do not have access to the chats other people have with that AI, unless they’re a creator using an AI based on themselves to respond to their personal messages. Learn more about AI auto replies.

  • Custom AIs are not licensed professionals or experts trained to help people. Chats with custom AIs can’t replace professional advice. You shouldn’t rely on AI chats for medical, psychological, financial, legal or any other type of professional advice. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service for appropriate ways to use AIs for self-help or other purposes.

Learn more about how Meta uses information for generative AI models.

What is a creator AI?

Turn off AI auto replies

I can’t find AI Studio

I have a different question

This feature currently isn’t available to everyone.

When you send a direct message or story reply on Instagram to creators who have made an AI based on them, you may receive an instant reply from their AI. These messages, designed to sound like the creator, will be labeled with “AI · creator name” and will be visible to both you and the creator in the chat.

Any messages you send will be visible to both you and the creator, just like a regular chat. You’ll also see a note when the creator has turned off auto replies in your chat, and their responses to you will no longer be marked as “AI · creator name.”

The creator can still reply to your message directly anytime, and you’re able to turn AI auto replies off or back on in your chat settings. Learn more about AIs on Instagram

When you send a message to a creator who has AI auto replies turned on, you can:

  • Ask something you’d typically ask the creator: Send a message and get an instant reply that’s designed to sound like how the creator might respond. Creators can also jump in and reply to your messages directly anytime.
  • Get responses based on real content: Each creator’s AI uses content and information provided by the creator to help inform message replies.
  • Help improve AI chats: We may use your feedback and messages sent to participating creators to improve AI quality. You can provide feedback on any AI response by tapping the thumbs up icon next to the reply for a good response, and a thumbs down icon for a bad response.

Note: If you send a message to a creator and do not see any mention of AI auto replies being turned on, you will not receive a response from the creator’s AI.

I have a different question

You can start an audio or video call with up to 8 people on Instagram.

Start a call

To begin an audio or video call on Instagram:

  1. Click Messages on the left.
  2. Click an existing conversation on the left or start a new conversation.
  3. From your chat, you can:
    • Click Call in the top right to start an audio call.
    • Click Video in the top right to start a video call.
  4. Click Start call.

The person or group you call will receive a notification that you’re calling them.

Keep in mind that anyone you’ve accepted a message from, except for verified accounts, can video call with you. To prevent someone from video calling with you, you can block them.

Manage a call

While on an audio or video call, you can:

  • Enter full screen. Click Expand in the top right to expand your call screen.
  • Update camera and audio settings. Click Settings in the top right to make changes to your camera and audio settings.
  • End a video call. Click End call at the bottom to end your video call.

My microphone isn’t working

My camera isn’t working

My speakers aren’t working

I can’t hear my friend

I have a different question

If something isn’t working with your camera, microphone or speakers for audio and video calling on Instagram, here are some things you can try.

Check your device’s hardware settings
  • Make sure that your camera and microphone are turned on. Close any open programs that may already be using your camera or microphone.
  • If you’re using any external camera, microphone or speakers, make sure that they’re selected for use from your device.
  • Make sure that your microphone isn’t on mute.
  • Make sure that the browser you’re using has permission to access your camera, microphone or speakers. You can check this on your computer or browser settings. Learn how to check your computer settings from Apple Support or from the Microsoft Support page. You can also check your Google Chrome browser settings on the Google Chrome Help page.
Restart your browser and device
  • Close your internet browser and restart your computer.
Check your internet connection
  • If your internet connection is slow, try re-connecting to your Wi-Fi network or connecting to a different network.
Ask your friend to check their device settings and internet connection
  • If you can’t hear or see the person you’re video calling with, ask them to try the steps listed above.
Let us know if you’re still having issues with your audio or video call
  • If you’re still experiencing a problem after trying these suggestions, learn how to report a problem.

To unsend a message you’ve sent in a chat on Instagram:

How do I delete hidden messages?

How do I accept hidden messages?

How do I report a hidden message?

How do I manage hidden words?

I have a different question

Message requests that may be offensive, unwanted, contain spam or are hidden based on your Hidden Words preferences will appear in a separate Hidden requests folder in your inbox. You won’t receive notifications for hidden message requests.

Manage hidden message requests
  1. Click Messages on the left.
  2. Click Requests at the top, then click Hidden.
  3. Click a message request to select it. You can select multiple requests to take bulk actions.
  4. At the bottom, you can click:
    • Accept. The conversation will be moved to your main inbox.
    • Delete or Delete all, then Delete again to confirm.

Messages from accounts you’ve already connected with won’t be hidden even if they include offensive words, phrases or emoji. If someone you are connected with is sending you offensive messages, you can restrict them or block them.

Note that some message previews will be hidden based on your Hidden Words preferences.

What happens when you report a message in Hidden Requests

If you report a hidden message, the content of that message will be sent to our Help Team for review.

Keep in mind that your report is anonymous, except if you’re reporting an intellectual property infringement. The account you reported won’t see who reported them.

You can reply and react to messages you receive on Threads. Note: The sender of a message will be able to see when you’ve seen their message.

React or reply to a message

Why you can’t find a message in your inbox

If someone you follow sends you a message, it’ll appear in your inbox.

If someone you don’t follow sends you a message, it’ll appear in your message requests inbox.

To decline or allow a message request:

  1. Click Messages on the left.
  2. Click Requests at the top of your messages inbox.
  3. Click a message request.
  4. Select Delete or Accept.

When you accept a message request from someone, their future messages will go directly to your inbox. Note that some messages may be moved to your hidden message requests folder.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

This setting controls whether we can show you relevant content on Instagram based on information about your Activity from other businesses.

If you don’t allow us to use this activity to show you more relevant content, the content you see may still be based on other types of information, such as your activity on our platform. What happens when I block?

I have a different question

There are multiple ways to block someone on Instagram. People aren’t notified when you block them.

Block or unblock an account from a chat with another person

  1. Click Messages on the left.
  2. Click the chat with the person you want to block/unblock, then click Information at the top.
    • Note: For Meta Quest users: Press and hold the chat name from your inbox.
  3. Click Block/Unblock, then click again to confirm.

Block or unblock an account from someone’s Instagram profile

You can view a list of accounts you’ve blocked from your settings. Learn more about what happens when you block someone.

Keep in mind
  • When you block someone from the Instagram app, it will block their account, other existing accounts they may have or any new accounts they may create.
  • If you choose to block someone’s account and other existing accounts they may have or create, this will not apply to other accounts of theirs that you already follow. You’ll need to block those accounts individually.
  • If you’re in a group chat with someone you’ve blocked, you’ll get a dialog asking whether you want to stay in the group or leave. If you choose to stay in the group, you and the blocked person will be able to see each other’s messages in the group.
  • If you don’t want to block someone, you can restrict them, delete their comments from your posts, or block multiple people from commenting on your posts.

Why did my likes decrease?

I have a different question

If you notice a change to the number of likes, follows or comments on your account, it may be because some came from accounts generating inauthentic activity.

Sometimes, non-Instagram apps create automated likes, comments and follows to make an account appear more popular than it is. This inauthentic activity goes against Instagram’s Community Guidelines. When these accounts are discovered, their activity is removed from Instagram.

We routinely remove disabled accounts to keep Instagram safe. This means related updates to the total number of followers on your account and the total number of accounts you follow may change, even within a short time.

Remove flagged followers

Review flagged follow requests

Turn off flagged account filtering

I have a different question

This product or feature may not be available to you yet.

Protect your account from unwanted followers by removing flagged accounts from your follower list on Instagram. Instagram may flag accounts if they’re potentially spam, bots or irrelevant.

You can also stop flagged accounts from affecting your discoverability and your ability to build authentic engagement with real followers by reviewing activity from accounts we’ve flagged.

Learn how Instagram detects potential spam, bot or irrelevant accounts at scale.

Before you begin
  • This feature is automatically available for any account that is set to public.
  • Keep in mind that a temporary limit, including approving follow requests on Instagram, may be placed on your Instagram account if you switch between your public and private accounts too often.
Remove flagged accounts that already follow you

To remove flagged followers on Instagram:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Followers.
  2. If Instagram has flagged any followers, you’ll see a notification called Flagged for review that you can tap.
  3. From here, tap Remove all to remove all flagged followers at once.
    • To review and remove each individual account, tap Remove next to the account.
    • To give feedback that an account shouldn’t be flagged, tap Options next to the account and tap Not spam or irrelevant to confirm.
  4. Tap Remove to confirm.

Once these flagged followers are removed, they’ll also be removed from your follower count and follower list. They won’t be notified that they’ve been removed from your followers.

Review incoming follows from flagged accounts

Even if your account is public, incoming follows from flagged accounts will be sent as a request, which you can approve or deny.

To review incoming follows from flagged accounts:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Followers.
  2. In the Flagged folder, you can review all follow requests from flagged accounts.
  3. Tap Delete all requests to remove all flagged follower requests at once, or you can choose to Delete or Confirm each individual account.

Note: If you don’t approve these follower requests within 30 days, they’ll be automatically declined. You can turn off automatic filtering of flagged accounts at any time by following these next steps.

Turn off automatic filtering of flagged accounts

To opt in to or out of automatic filtering of follower requests from flagged accounts:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Menu.
  2. Tap Follow and invite friends and turn off Flag for review . You can turn this back on at any time.

On Instagram, you can control who can see your likes on other people’s posts and reels.

Change who can see your likes on content
  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Likes you’ve made.
  5. Select your preferred setting for who can see what you like.
    • Allow everyone to see likes: Everyone can see what you like.
    • Allow people you follow to see likes: Only people you follow can see what you like.
    • Allow close friends to see likes: Only your close friends can see what you like.
    • Don’t allow anyone to see likes: No one can see what you like.

Note: Regardless of your setting choice, the account that posted the content you liked can see that you liked their post or reel.

You can always see your own likes on posts, reels and in Your Activity. Learn how to see recent photos and videos you’ve liked on Instagram.

When are parents notified?

Manage supervision settings

I have a different question

This feature is not available everywhere.

This information is not a substitute for crisis services or medical support. If you are in immediate risk of harming yourself, or know someone who is, please contact local emergency services immediately.

When parents are notified about teen search activity

When a parent or guardian supervises their teen’s Instagram account through Family Center, they may receive notifications if their teen repeatedly searches for content related to suicide or self-harm. The notifications do not show or provide access to teen search history. These notifications are designed to help parents support their teens and start important conversations about their well-being.

Note: Teens may search these topics for a variety of reasons, including exploring difficult topics, researching something they saw or heard, or finding help for a friend. This notification does not necessarily mean a teen is in crisis.

Why teens might search for this content

Research shows teens search for content related to suicide or self-harm for many different reasons. Understanding this can help in responding with empathy.

Common reasons include:

  • Curiosity or academic research - Learning about mental health topics for school or general knowledge
  • Concern for a friend - Researching how to support someone they care about
  • Seeking understanding - Trying to make sense of their own difficult emotions
  • Looking for community - Finding others who share similar struggles or experiences
  • Coping with stress - Searching for ways to handle overwhelming feelings
  • Repeating something - Repeating language from a video game, TV show, or conversation they overheard
  • Trying to be funny - Searching for dark or shocking terms as a joke or to get a reaction from friends, without understanding the seriousness of the topic

Important to remember:

  • Searching for information related to suicide or self-harm doesn’t necessarily indicate a crisis, but it’s always worth having a caring conversation
  • Early, supportive conversations guide teens toward healthy coping strategies and help you build a trusting relationship
How parents can support teens when they receive a notification

Here are some suggestions from outside professionals for ways to support someone.

Check on their safety first

Outside experts recommend first reaching out to your teen to check on them.

  • Do your best to stay calm and approach your teen with care and understanding.
  • If you believe your teen is in immediate danger:
    • Contact your local emergency services
    • Find crisis support resources in your area
Start a supportive conversation

Once you’ve ensured their safety, aim to have a direct and caring conversation:

  • Choose a time when you and your teen can talk privately without distractions
  • Acknowledge the situation honestly: “I got a notification on my phone that you may have searched about suicide or self-harm.”
  • Reassure them they’re not in trouble: “You haven’t done anything wrong. I care about you. Can we talk about this?”
  • Ask open-ended questions: “I’m curious, what was happening for you at that moment?”
Listen without judgment

If your teen opens up, try to resist the urge to immediately offer solutions

  • Listen and validate their emotions: “That sounds really hard. It makes sense that you’re feeling this way.”
  • You might say: “It sounds like you were feeling [sad/confused/worried]. It’s okay to feel that way. I want you to know you can always talk to me when you feel that way. I’m here to listen”
It’s okay to talk about suicide and self-harm
  • Many parents worry that asking about suicide or self-harm will plant the idea in their teen’s head. However, professionals have determined that asking directly provides clarity, lowers anxiety, and opens a bridge to communication.
  • Important questions to ask:
    • “Have you had any thoughts about killing yourself?
    • “Have you been hurting yourself?”
    • “Do you have a plan?” “Do you have means?”
Next Steps

If you believe a teen needs additional support, consider these additional options for professional support.

  • Healthcare provider
  • Local mental health professional
  • Counselor or trusted staff member at school
  • Spiritual advisor or counselor
Managing your supervision settings

You can access and manage your supervision tools through Family Center:

  1. Go to Family Center on Instagram or at familycenter.meta.com
  2. Select your teen’s account.

From here, you can:

  • Review supervision settings and notification preferences
  • Explore Instagram’s built-in safety features for teens
  • Review privacy and safety settings together with your teen

Remember: Supervision is voluntary and requires mutual agreement between you and your teen. Focus on building trust and open communication rather than monitoring alone.

  • NAMI (National Alliance on Mental Illness): “How to Talk to Your Teen About Suicide”
  • The Jason Foundation: Parent Resource Program for Youth Suicide Prevention
  • Mayo Clinic: “Teen Suicide: What Parents Need to Know”

You can remove profiles from your followers list on Threads.

Threads.com from a computer

  1. Click Profile on the left of your profile.
  2. Click Followers below your profile info. You’ll see a list of people who follow you.
  3. Click a username to go to their profile.
  4. Click Options in the top right of your profile, then tap Remove follower.

Threads app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile in the bottom right of your profile.
  2. Tap Followers below your profile info. You’ll see a list of people who follow you.
  3. Tap a username to go to their profile.
  4. Tap Options in the top right of your profile, then tap Remove follower.

When you remove a follower, they aren’t notified that you’ve removed them.

If you’ve turned on sharing to the fediverse, you can follow users from other servers on Threads. Users, from their servers, can search for and follow your profile, view your posts, interact with your content, and share your content to anyone on or off their server. Your followers list in Threads will include users that follow you on Threads and a separate list of your fediverse followers. Your Threads follower count will only include users that follow you on Threads.

If someone is bothering you on Threads, you can block them.

If you see comments that aren’t following our Community Guidelines, you can report them. This may include comments like spam, hateful conduct and false information.

Report a comment:
  1. Click Comments below the post.
  2. Hover over to the comment you want to report.
  3. Click Options below the comment.
  4. Click Report.
  5. Select an option for why the comment is abusive, then follow the on-screen instructions. Note: After you report a comment you’ll no longer see it, but this doesn’t mean the comment was removed by Instagram.

After you report a comment, you can also choose to restrict or block the person whose comment you reported.

Keep in mind that your report is anonymous, except if you’re reporting an intellectual property infringement. The account you reported won’t see who reported them.

If someone leaves an inappropriate comment on your post, you can delete it.

When your Activity Status is on, people you follow and anyone you message will see when you were last active or currently active on Instagram.

You can turn your Activity status on or off at any time.

What happens when you block someone on Instagram

What happens if I block?

Can they see my old comments?

What about group chats?

How do I unblock someone?

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Please update your Instagram app to the latest version to have the most up-to-date experience for blocking.

When you block someone from the Instagram app, you’ll have the option to block their account, or to block their account and other existing accounts they may have or accounts they may create. Note: If you’re following multiple accounts owned by the same person, you’ll need to block each account individually. People aren’t notified when you block them.

Likes and comments
  • After you block someone, their likes and comments will be removed from your photos and videos. Unblocking someone won’t restore their previous likes and comments.
  • People that you block can still see your likes and comments on posts that were shared by public accounts or accounts they follow.
Mentions and tags
  • After you block someone, they won’t be able to mention your username or tag you.
Messages
  • After you block someone, your messaging threads with them will remain in your Direct inbox, but you won’t be able to message them.
  • If you’re in a group chat with someone you’ve blocked, you’ll get a dialog asking whether you want to stay in the group or leave. If you choose to stay in the group, you and the blocked person will be able to see each other’s messages in the group.
  • If the person you blocked sends you any messages in Direct, you won’t receive those messages, and they won’t be delivered later if you unblock them.
  • After you block someone, they won’t be able to join a room you create if they’re logged in to their Instagram account.
  • If the person you blocked has multiple Instagram or Facebook accounts, you may need to block each account.
  • If you have a Facebook account that isn’t set up in Accounts Center, the account you blocked will still be able to message or call your Facebook account, unless you also block them on Facebook.

If you don’t want to block someone, you can remove them as a follower, restrict them, or block them from commenting on your photos and videos.

If you no longer want to block someone, you can unblock them.

If you keep getting an error message that a comment can’t be deleted, it may be because the comment was already deleted in our system. The comment may still appear because you’re viewing an old version of the page. We’re aware of this issue and are working on a fix.

Why you should not use apps that offer likes and followers on Instagram

My account was compromised

Change my Instagram password

My account was disabled

I have a different question

You shouldn’t use apps that offer likes and followers. Some non-Instagram apps offer likes or followers in exchange for your Instagram login details. None of these services are affiliated with or endorsed by Instagram, and you shouldn’t use these apps or let anyone else access your Instagram account.

How these services compromise your account security

If you give these apps your login information, whether with an access token or by giving them your username and password, they can gain complete access to your account. They can see your personal messages, find information about your friends, and potentially post spam or other harmful content on your profile. This puts your security, and the security of your friends, at risk.

Keep in mind that accounts that generate inauthentic activity are also against our Community Standards. If it looks like you’ve shared your login details with one of these apps, we may remove any likes or other engagement that they generated. Accounts that continue to use non-Instagram apps to get more followers may notice that certain parts of their Instagram account are limited. If you use one of these apps to gain likes or followers, your account may be disabled or terminated.

Keep your account secure

If you’ve shared your username and password with one of these apps, you should change your Instagram password to protect your account. If however, you think your account has been hacked or taken over, there are several actions you may be able to take to secure your account. Learn more about what to do if you think your account has been hacked. You can also manage the privacy settings for apps you’ve connected to on Instagram and remove them at any time.

Learn more about how to keep your Instagram account secure.

Manage my activity

I have a different question

Your Activity is where you can view and manage things like your photos, likes, account history and activity on Instagram. To access your Instagram activity, you must be logged into your account.

From Your activity you can:

  • View how much time you spend on Instagram each day.
  • Archive multiple posts you’ve shared
  • View and delete photos and reels you’ve shared.
  • Edit and delete highlights you’ve saved.
  • Review and delete likes, comments and sticker responses you’ve made.
  • View posts you’ve been tagged in, remove tagged posts from your profile, or remove yourself from tagged posts.
  • View changes you’ve made to your account since you created it.
  • View and clear things you’ve recently searched for on Instagram.
  • View links you’ve recently visited on Instagram.
  • View and manage posts you’ve archived and content you’ve recently deleted.

About Instagram teen privacy and safety settings

My teen’s privacy settings

What are default teen settings?

Parental supervision tools

I have a different question

Instagram is committed to providing young people with safer and more private experiences. We have dedicated teams focused on youth safety, and we work closely with experts to inform the features we develop. Here are some of the default settings and additional tools for teens on Instagram. Age requirements may vary by country.

Default Instagram settings

Age Verification

We require people to be at least 13 years old to sign up for Instagram, though some regions like South Korea, Spain, Quebec or Florida have different age requirements. People can confirm their age by providing their birthday, photo identification, and/or submitting a video selfie. Confirming your age is a requirement for everyone on Instagram. You can learn more about age verification in Newsroom.

Private Accounts

Teens under 18 years old have their account set to private as a default when they join Instagram. Private accounts let people control who sees or responds to their content. Learn more about private Instagram accounts.

Audience Controls

As of May 2022, when teens under 18 sign up for Instagram, accounts they don’t follow cannot tag, mention or use their content in Reels Remixes or Guides by default.

Direct Messaging

We restrict adults over 18 from starting private chats with teens they’re not connected to on Instagram and Messenger. Learn more about direct messaging for teens.

Protections from Suspicious Adults

We’ve developed technology that allows us to find adult accounts that have shown potentially suspicious behavior, such as adults who have recently been blocked or reported by a young person. We stop these adult accounts from interacting with teen accounts the following ways:

  • We don’t show teen accounts in Explore, Reels or ‘Accounts Suggested For You’ to these adults.
  • If these adults find young people’s accounts by searching for their usernames, they do not have the option to follow them.
  • These adults are not able to see teen accounts when scrolling through the list of people who have liked a certain post.
  • These adults are not able to see comments from teens on other people’s posts.
  • These adults are not able to see teen accounts when scrolling through an account’s Followers or Following list.
  • If these adults follow a teen account, we may send that teen a notification prompting them to review and remove the new follower.
  • If these adults are already connected to a teen account and send the teen a direct message, we send a safety notice to the teen encouraging them to be cautious and provide options to end the conversation, block, report, or restrict the adult.
  • Note: All of the above interventions also apply to teen accounts’ ability to discover, search, view or interact with suspicious adult accounts.

Content setting for Teen Accounts

Teen Accounts are automatically set to Ages 13+ so that teens see content, messages, profiles and comments generally aligned with movie ratings for ages 13+ across all of Instagram, including from accounts the teen follows.

Content Restrictions

For all users on Instagram, we remove content that goes against our Community Standards and we do not recommend content that goes against our Recommendation Guidelines.

For teens under 16, we hide certain sensitive content on Instagram even if it’s been shared by friends or people they follow. For example, content that discusses self-harm and eating disorders, or that includes borderline adult nudity. We’re working on applying these policies for people under 18 within the coming months.

For teens under 18, content that is reviewed and may be disturbing (for example, some instances of graphic and violent content) is removed.

Lastly, for teens under 18, we restrict the visibility of certain restricted goods and services including content related to alcohol, tobacco, bladed weapons, weight loss products, cosmetic procedures, sex toys, sexual enhancement products, gambling or entheogens.

Additional Instagram tools

Parental Supervision

Supervision is a set of tools and insights that parents and guardians can use to help support their teens ages 13-17 on Instagram. Supervision is optional, and both the parent and the teen must agree to participate. When supervision is set up in Family Center, a parent can set time limits, schedule breaks, see their teen’s time spent on Instagram, see their teens followers and who they follow, shared connections, who they’ve blocked or reported, and see the Teen Account settings selections.

Alternate Topic Nudge

Teens under 18 in certain countries will see a notification that encourages them to switch to a different topic if they’ve been looking at the same type of content on Explore for a while. This nudge is designed to encourage teens to discover something new. Learn more about this type of nudge.

About safety settings for teens on Threads

How do I manage teen settings?

How do I change privacy settings?

How do I change sensitive content settings?

How do I turn off sleep mode?

I have a different question

Threads profiles for teens 13-17 are automatically set to more protective teen safety settings. These settings aim to help keep teens safe by limiting unwanted interactions, showing content that’s right for their age and helping them manage their time on Threads.

For now, teens 13-15 can’t update these settings. We’re working to build a complete supervision experience for Threads. Once this is available, parents will be able to help teens manage their safety settings.

Teen safety settings

When a teen creates a Threads profile, the following safety measures are automatically set:

  • Private profiles:
    • New profiles: When teens 13-17 sign up for a new Threads profile, they will be defaulted to private profiles. Teens 16-17 can change their profile to public.
    • Existing profiles: With the introduction of teen safety settings, existing profiles for teens under 16 will be set to private, even if their profiles were previously public. Teens 16-17 with existing public profiles will not be automatically set to private profiles, and they can keep their profiles public.
  • Messages: Currently, messaging is not available for teens on Threads.
  • Online status: Settings for teens default to allow no one to see when the teen is online.
  • Tags and mentions: Settings for teens default to only allow tags and mentions by people who they follow.
  • Potentially offensive comments: Settings for teens default to hide potentially offensive comments through the Hidden Words settings.
  • Sensitive content control: Settings for teens default to show less sensitive content.
  • Sleep mode: Settings for teens default to have sleep mode turned on from 10PM to 7AM every day. During sleep mode, Threads notifications are muted and the teen will see a reminder to close Threads.
  • Daily time limits: Settings for teens default to send a reminder to close Threads after a total of 60 minutes is spent on the app each day.

About Sensitive Content Control on Instagram

Change Sensitive Content Control

What is sensitive content?

I can’t change my settings

I have a different question

Learn how to change your Sensitive Content Control settings.

Teens under 18 have a different content setting for their Teen Account. They’re automatically defaulted into the Ages 13+ content setting so they see content, profiles and comments similar to content ratings for ages 13+. Teens under 18 need their parent’s or guardian’s permission to change their content setting to More content.

The Sensitive Content Control allows you to choose how much content you see in Explore, Search, Reels, Comments, Accounts You Might Follow and Recommendations in your feed that you might find upsetting or offensive.

If content goes against our Recommendation Guidelines, it may be considered upsetting, offensive, or sensitive and we may make it harder to find, rather than removing it from Instagram. We’ve previously limited content like this, but you can also choose to see more or less content that could be upsetting or offensive using the Sensitive Content Control.

The Sensitive Content Control only limits this type of content from accounts you don’t follow, you’ll still see content from friends, family and other accounts you follow.

This control is automatically set to the default (Standard), which is the same level of potentially upsetting or offensive content we’ve previously allowed on Instagram. Teen Accounts for teens aged 13-17 are automatically defaulted to See less. You can change this setting at any time to see more or less of this type of content and accounts. Anyone 16 or older can change this setting at any time to see more or less of this type of content and accounts. Teen Accounts for teens 13-15 will need parental approval to change it.

Learn more about how to change your Sensitive Content Control settings.

Learn more about ways to make your experience on Instagram safer.

What types of content and accounts does Instagram consider sensitive?

There are some categories of content and accounts that are allowed on our platforms because they don’t go against our Community Standards, but may not be eligible for recommendations. You can change the Sensitive Content Control setting at any time to see more or less of this type of content.

Content that impedes our ability to foster a safe community, such as:

  • Content that may depict violence, such as people fighting. (We remove graphically violent content.)
  • Content that may be sexually explicit or suggestive, such as pictures of people in see-through clothing. (We remove content that contains adult nudity or sexual activity.)
  • Content that promotes the use of certain regulated products, such as tobacco or vaping products, adult products and services, or pharmaceutical drugs. (We remove content that attempts to sell or trade most regulated goods.)
  • Content that may promote or depict cosmetic procedures.
  • Content that may be attempting to sell products or services based on health-related claims, such as promoting a supplement to help a person lose weight.

If someone is trying to blackmail you by threatening to share private information unless you send money or something else you’re uncomfortable with, please report it. Also, contact your local law enforcement.

If you don’t want someone to see your posts or contact you on Instagram, you can block that person. Read our tips on how to address abuse on Instagram.

What can you do if someone is blackmailing you for intimate images, videos or messages

Your private content is your own. Instagram wants you to know that it’s wrong and against our rules for someone to share or threaten to share your intimate images, videos or messages without your consent.

If this is happening, it isn’t your fault, and you can take steps to protect yourself.

  • Report to Instagram: Learn how to report profiles or posts or messages.
  • You’re not alone: People who experience these kinds of situations can sometimes feel scared or desperate or can experience depression. If you’re struggling and thinking about hurting yourself, get support. Please don’t wait.
  • Tell someone you trust: Message or call a friend or adult you trust, such as a relative, teacher, school counselor or family friend. They can help you protect yourself.
  • Get help from experts: Find more support for general issues with non-consensual intimate images in your region or use the resources listed below.
    • Brazil: Safernet
    • United States: Thorn

Health & Safety Warnings for Meta Spark AR Walk Experiences

Is Spark AR Walk safe?

What are AR Walk risks?

AR Walk age restrictions

I have a different question

WARNING: Read and follow the warnings below to reduce the risk of personal injury and property damage.

AR Walk experiences are not intended for and should not be used by children under the age of 13. Adults should ensure that children (age 13 and older) are supervised at all times while using AR Walk experiences and that they use the app in accordance with these safety warnings.

Meta Spark AR Walk (“AR Walk”) experiences invite you to move around in the real world. The experience does NOT alert you to any potential risks or hazards you may encounter, and conditions in the real world may not match what you see in the app. You are solely responsible for ensuring that your use of the app provides a safe experience for both you and everyone/everything you may encounter. For your safety and the safety of others, always be alert and aware of your surroundings before and while using AR Walk experiences.

AR objects in AR Walk experiences are developed and placed by third-party creators. Depending on real-world conditions, AR objects may not have been placed in an accessible location, and may not be safe or appropriate to approach. You must use your independent judgment and common sense when determining whether, when, and how to approach an AR object.

Do not enter unsafe areas when attempting to reach AR objects. The safety of any given location will depend on numerous factors including but not limited to:

  • Your abilities, awareness, and behavior
  • The time of day
  • The current and forecast weather conditions
  • Current conditions of roads, sidewalks, stairs, paths, and terrain
  • Vehicle, human, and animal traffic, behavior, and congestion
  • Construction
  • Emergency situations
  • Geopolitical events such as rioting or police or military presence

Be aware of potential fall, trip and bump hazards around you. Choose a safe route to approach AR objects, even if entering a dangerous area would be more convenient. If entering a dangerous area is the only way to approach an AR object, do not attempt to reach the object.

Never trespass on private property, enter a location outside its operating hours, or enter a location you do not have permission to access, even if doing so would be the most convenient or only way to approach an AR object.

Obey all laws, local rules, and traffic regulations. Pay attention to and obey all posted signs governing both motorized and non-motorized vehicles and pedestrians.

Never use an AR Walk experience while operating a vehicle.

Never use AR Walk experiences in situations that require your full attention or where distractions could put you or others in harm’s way. Situations or activities that may require your full attention could include crossing busy streets, supervising animals or children, or traveling on steep or uneven terrain.

Never use an AR Walk experience while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

AR Walk experiences are not intended as fitness programs but may involve physical activity. Consult with your doctor before using if you are pregnant, elderly, or have a heart or other serious medical condition. Stop immediately if you experience dizziness, lightheadedness, nausea, or fatigue, and seek medical attention if symptoms persist.

How do I turn on fediverse sharing?

What information is shared?

How do I turn off fediverse sharing?

What happens if I delete a post?

I have a different question

Our Beta experience for sharing to the fediverse is currently only available to Threads profiles in certain areas.

When someone turns on sharing to the fediverse, users on other servers can search for and follow their Threads profile, view their Threads posts, and interact with and share their Threads content with anyone on or off another fediverse server. Learn more about Threads and the fediverse.

When you turn on sharing to the fediverse on Threads, your Threads profile and content you post on Threads will be shared globally with users on other servers not controlled or moderated by Meta. Those users will be able to:

  • View posts you share on Threads, if the post’s format is supported and doesn’t limit who can quote or reply to it. Note: This includes posts you make using Threads API.
  • See if you’ve liked a reply from a user on another fediverse server
  • Search, find, and follow your Threads profile
  • Reshare your Threads posts with anyone on or off their server
  • Interact with your Threads posts (examples: comment, like)

Keep in mind that information you share to other fediverse servers is no longer in Meta’s control and is subject to those servers’ policies and practices. Other servers can use your information at their discretion and may not implement the same privacy standards as Meta. You may lose control of your information and may not be able to delete, access, edit, or download your data with those servers in the same way you can with Meta.

For example, if you delete a post on Threads or archive a post on Threads, we will request that other servers delete the post from their servers. We cannot guarantee that they will delete your post and it may remain publicly visible despite your decision to delete it.

Similarly, if you turn off sharing to the fediverse, delete your Threads profile, or deactivate your Threads profile, we will request that other servers delete your profile and content. We cannot guarantee that they will delete your information and it may remain publicly visible.

You can turn off sharing to the fediverse at any time.

Learn more about how sharing to the fediverse impacts your privacy in our Fediverse Guide.

How to combat bullying and harassment on Instagram

Filter unwanted comments

Limit unwanted interactions

Report bullying or harassment

Stop spam comments

I have a different question

We’re committed to protecting and supporting you on Instagram. We have developed features and tools to help keep you safe, so that you can focus on creating and sharing your content with a safe and supportive community.

Protect against unwanted messages

Hidden Words and Advanced Comment Filtering not only protect against unwanted comments but also unwanted direct messages. These options are on by default and help prevent comments that may contain profanity, bullying or spam but you also have access to a custom word list which we highly recommend!

  • This allows you to prevent custom words, emojis or phrases from appearing in your comments or inbox.
  • You can also search for custom word lists that already exist (example: if you’re particularly worried about a certain topic or subject, you can find relevant lists that already exist).
  • Filter out even more comments that may be spam with Advanced Comment filtering, or may contain offensive words or phrases. Comments from the people you follow and those who follow you will not be hidden. This setting is on by default, but you can change it at any time.
Limited your interactions

If you’re experiencing unwanted engagement you can use Limited Interactions to manage interactions with people in bulk. This is an account level tool that temporarily limits your comments and direct messages from specific accounts.

  • You can choose to limit interactions from people who aren’t following you, or people who recently followed you within the last week. These accounts will not be able to direct message you or comment on any of your content. You can also set a time limit for Limited Interactions, which you can change at any time.
  • Keep in mind that Limited Interactions do not impact your reach in Feed or the Explore tab.
Reachability settings

From your Instagram settings, you can find multiple options to customize your experience and how people are able to interact with your account.

  • You can leave your direct messages open where anyone can message you–even if they follow you or not. You can also opt to only allow people you follow to direct message you, and all other messages appear in a separate inbox. You can also disable direct messages altogether.
  • There are also settings to control who can tag or who can @mention you, and who can comment on your posts.
  • You can also turn off comments on a post, which you can do from the post itself.
Reporting, blocking, and restricting

We encourage you to report accounts, posts, and comments that you feel go against our Community Standards, whether it’s bullying, harassment, hate speech, or doxxing.

  • Reporting the content you want our teams to review helps us properly take action against potentially harmful content. When reporting direct messages, for example, you should report the chat and not the account because the team that reviews the profile doesn’t have access to direct messages. This is because we take privacy seriously and only specific support teams can access direct messages.
  • After you report, we encourage you to block the account. When you block someone, it now gives you the option to include any new and existing accounts someone may have.
  • You can also use our other moderation tools like restricting accounts or hiding or deleting individual comments.
Reducing spam

We know that spending time deleting spam comments from your posts or removing fake accounts from your followers isn’t how you want to spend your time. To help with this, our teams built tools to give you more power to stop spam and bot accounts from interacting with you and your community:

  • Bulk Unfollow: We made it easier for you to review existing followers by placing suspected bots or other suspicious users into a folder for your review. You can then choose to remove and block them at once. Select your followers list to find this folder.
  • Hold Followers for Review: We also want to prevent new unwanted followers from following you. Going forward, we’ll hold new requests from suspicious users in a folder for your review as well. You’ll be notified to review and can choose to add, deny, or block all in one place. You can choose to opt out at any time from your settings.
  • Spam Comment Filtering: Our existing Advanced Comment Filtering in Hidden Words now works at filtering out spam comments too.
  • Hold Tags for Review: We know it’s frustrating to get spam tags on content from other accounts. To combat this, we also filter suspected spam tags into a folder for your review. You can choose to approve them if you’d like, or you can hide and remove them.

Here you’ll find resources that help young people and adults discuss bullying as well as best practices for staying safe on Instagram.

  • Beatbullying.org is a bullying prevention charity, working to empower people to understand, recognize, and say no to bullying, violence and harassment by giving them the tools to transform their lives and the lives of their peers.
  • ConnectSafely.org is an online forum designed to give teens and parents a voice in the public discussion about youth online. It also offers social-media safety tips for teens and parents, the latest youth-tech news, and many other resources.
