We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

When you install an app from the App Store, you may see some information that Apple now asks all app developers to provide about how the app handles your data. Apple offers a small range of specific options to choose from when describing an app’s data use and collection practices, and these options are not specific to you or the settings and controls you may have used in each of our apps.

As a reminder, Instagram is part of a group of different products that are provided by the Meta Company (including Facebook, Messenger and Portal) under Meta’s Privacy Policy. The information that you see reflects the data types and data uses across all the different apps falling under the Meta Privacy Policy, and may not be specific to the particular app that you are using.

The Privacy Policy is the most comprehensive source to understand how we collect, use and share your information across the Meta Products so we recommend reviewing the policy for details and examples.

Below are a few examples of how these data types are used
  • Contact Information. The information you provide when you sign up for an account allows you and others to connect, communicate and share content across our Products.
  • Health and Fitness. If you have a Facebook account, you may provide a health-related life event that may be used to help you remember important moments from your life.
  • Location. Location-related information such as your current location, where you live, the places you like to go, and the businesses and people you’re near may be used to provide, personalize and improve our Products, including ads, for you and others.
  • Financial Information. Financial information may be used for purchases, such as shopping or making a donation.
  • Contacts. Imported contacts help you and others find people you may know.
  • User Content. Camera or voice-enabled features may help suggest effects and filters that you might like, or respond to your voice commands.
  • Browsing History. To show you more relevant ads, we receive and use data that advertisers and other partners provide to us about your activity on their websites and apps, as well as some of your offline interactions, such as purchases. For example, we may show you an ad for a shirt based on your visit to a clothing website.
  • Search History. When searching Instagram (for example, accounts, tags or places) you can access and delete those searches from within your search history.
  • Identifiers. Account and device identifiers we collect can be used to match and store information with your Instagram account.
  • Purchases. If you choose to use Instagram Shops, we are able to understand your shopping activity, such as the products you view and purchase. This means that what you browse and purchase within Shops may influence what you see in Shops and other Meta Products.
  • Usage Data & Diagnostics. Information about the features you use, what you’re doing on your device (such as taking screenshots while using the app), and the duration of your activities when you use our products may help us personalize your experience and improve the products for you and others.
  • Other Data Types. We conduct and support research and innovation on topics of general social welfare, technological advancement, public interest, health and well-being. For example, we analyze information we have about migration patterns during crises to aid relief efforts.
Some ways to review and manage your information on Instagram:
  • Use Activity from other businesses to adjust how ads on Instagram are shown to you based on your activity off of Meta technologies. If you don’t want to see ads from a specific advertiser, you can hide ads from them.
  • If you have a Facebook account, review your Facebook Ad Preferences, which include settings that can apply to your ads experience on Instagram. These settings adjust how we use information about your activity on Meta Company Products to show you ads that we think will be most relevant for you. Learn more about ads on Instagram.
  • View your account data in a single place or export a copy of your information.
  • You can also manage your connected experiences across Facebook, Instagram and Messenger using Accounts Center.

If you have a Facebook account, learn how to review and manage your information on Facebook.

Change Sensitive Content Control

What is sensitive content?

My content setting is 13+

I have a different question

Teens under 18 have a different content setting for their Teen Account. They’re automatically defaulted into the Ages 13+ content setting so they see content, profiles and comments similar to content ratings for ages 13+. Teens under 18 need their parent’s or guardian’s permission to change their content setting to More content.

If content goes against our Recommendation Guidelines, it may be considered upsetting, offensive, or sensitive and we may make it harder to find, rather than removing it from Instagram. We’ve previously limited content like this, but you can also choose to see more or less content that could be upsetting or offensive using the Sensitive Content Control.

The Sensitive Content Control applies to some content that goes against our Recommendation Guidelines, but does not apply to content that goes against our Community Standards. Our Community Standards define what is and isn’t allowed on Instagram. These guidelines help us keep Instagram an authentic and safe place. If we’re made aware of a post that goes against our Community Standards, we’ll remove it from Instagram.

Change your Sensitive Content Control

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Content Preferences, then tap Sensitive content.
  4. Tap Select next to Less to see less content you may find upsetting. Tap Select next to More to see more content you may find upsetting.
  5. Tap Confirm.

Instagram app for iPad

Keep in mind that when you choose to see more Sensitive Content, you’ll see more photos, videos or comments that you may find upsetting in Explore, Search, Reels, Comments, Accounts You Might Follow, hashtag pages and Recommendations in your feed.

We’re constantly making improvements to ensure you have more control over the content you see on Instagram. However, the Sensitive Content Control does not apply to content that goes against our Community Standards and content that appears with a warning.

Keep in mind that if you see a post you think goes against our Community Standards, you can report it to us so we can take a closer look. If a post goes against our Community Standards, we’ll remove it from Instagram.

Learn more about ways to make your experience on Instagram safer.

What types of content and accounts does Instagram consider sensitive

There are some categories of content and accounts that are allowed on our platforms because they don’t go against our Community Standards, but may not be eligible for recommendations. You can change the Sensitive Content Control setting at any time to see more or less of this type of content.

Content that impedes our ability to foster a safe community, such as:

  • Content that may depict violence, such as people fighting. (We remove graphically violent content.)
  • Content that may be sexually explicit or suggestive, such as pictures of people in see-through clothing. (We remove content that contains adult nudity or sexual activity.)
  • Content that promotes the use of certain regulated products, such as tobacco or vaping products, adult products and services, or pharmaceutical drugs. (We remove content that attempts to sell or trade most regulated goods.)

I have a different question

We work hard to keep Instagram a safe and enjoyable place for everyone. Please take a minute to read through these tips about the tools we’ve built and the best practices we’ve defined to help you stay safe on Instagram:

  • If someone is sharing photos or videos that make you uncomfortable, you can unfollow or block them. You can also report something that you feel violates our Community Standards right from the app.
  • Make sure you know whether your account is public or private. When you set your posts to private, anyone who wants to see your posts, followers or following list will have to send you a follow request first.
  • If someone is bullying you, reach out to a trusted family member or teacher for help. You can also remove a comment from a photo you’ve shared and report bullying and harassment through the Help Center.
  • If you have 1,000 or more followers, you can manage and remove bot and spam accounts that follow you.
  • Make sure you’re comfortable letting the photos and videos you share represent who you are to a wide audience, such as your parents, teachers or employers.
  • Never agree to do something or share anything that makes you uncomfortable.

Learn more about safety on Instagram and the differences between private and public accounts on Instagram.

I have a different question

Apps and websites that you connect to your Threads profile can be active, removed or expired from your profile based on the state they’re in and how often you use them.

Edit or remove an app or website from Threads
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Account, then click Website permissions.
  3. Click Active at the top. From here you can:
    • Click Remove next to the app you’d like to remove.
    • Click View and edit to view info you’re sharing with an app and manage other available settings.
Information an app or website can access on Threads

Some information about you is part of your public profile or is information you’ve made public. An app or website can access this public information at any time.

Other information is not public and an app or website can access it only if you choose to share it with the app or website when you connect to Threads.

If you choose to share your Threads information with an app or website, it will receive ongoing access to your Threads information and Threads will record when the app or website accesses it. Note: If you’ve turned on sharing to the fediverse, posts you make using Threads API will also be shared to the fediverse.

An app or website can be:

Active

Expired

Removed

Keep in mind
  • If you start using an app or website again after 90 days of inactivity, it may become active again and can access the non-public information you previously chose to share with it.
  • An app or website may ask you for permission to continue accessing your non-public information after its access has expired. You can approve or deny its request directly or by updating your Threads settings at any time.
  • We aren’t always able to tell when you haven’t used an app or website for 90 days, so we may sometimes stop an app or website from accessing your non-public information, even if you’ve used it in the past 90 days.

I have a different question

Apps and websites that you log into with Instagram or connect to your Instagram account can be active, removed or expired from your account based on the state they’re in and how often you use them.

Remove an app or website from Instagram
  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Below Your app and media, click Website permissions.
  3. Click Apps and Websites, then click Active.
  4. Click Remove next to the app you’d like to remove.
What information an app or website can access on Instagram

Some information about you is part of your public profile or is information you’ve made public. An app or website can access this public information at any time. Other information is not public and an app or website can access it only if you choose to share it with the app or website when you log in with your Instagram account.

An app or website can be:

  • Active: If it appears that you’ve used a third-party app or website within the last 90 days, it can access any information on Instagram you’ve shared with it at any time.
  • Expired: For personal Instagram accounts set to private, if it appears that you haven’t logged into an app or website with your Instagram account in the last 90 days, its access to your non-public information automatically expires. It may still have non-public information you previously shared with it while it was Active, like your photos or videos. There are a couple of exceptions:
    • We only expire access to information you can make non-public on your Instagram account. Certain information that is always public on Instagram, like your username, bio and profile picture, can still be accessed after 90 days of inactivity. This information is publicly accessible to everyone, and an app or website can access this information even if you’re not an active user.
    • Some apps and websites have permissions that are used to monitor or manage information from business and creator accounts on Instagram. We do not expire these apps and websites after 90 days of inactivity because they may need to access these products continuously (even if you haven’t logged into the app or website recently).
  • Removed: When you remove an app or website, or the app developer has made an app unavailable for you, it can only access public information on your Instagram account. Keep in mind:
    • The app or website may have stored information from when you were using it.
    • Removing the app or website only prevents it from continuing to access your non-public information through Instagram.
Keep in mind
  • If you start using an app or website again after 90 days of inactivity, it may become active again and can access the non-public information you previously chose to share with it.
  • An app or website may ask you for permission to continue accessing your non-public information after its access has expired. You can approve or deny its request directly or by updating your Instagram settings at any time.
  • We aren’t always able to tell when you haven’t used an app or website for 90 days, so we may sometimes stop an app or website from accessing your non-public information, even if you’ve used it in the past 90 days.

Visit the Facebook Help Center to learn more about how long apps and websites you’ve added have access to your information on Facebook.

Report a custom AI

Give feedback on AI response

AI generated inappropriate response

I have a different question

Custom AIs on Instagram aren’t yet available for everyone.

While chatting with a custom AI on Instagram if you think the AI goes against our Community Standards you can report it.

AIs can sometimes generate inaccurate or inappropriate responses. If you think that an individual response is inaccurate or inappropriate you can submit feedback on it.

Report a custom AI
  1. While chatting with a custom AI on aistudio.instagram.com, click Information in the top right.
  2. Click Report AI.
  3. Follow the onscreen instructions.
Give feedback on an AI response
  1. While chatting with an AI on aistudio.instagram.com, hover over the message you want to send feedback about.
  2. Click Good response or Bad response to send feedback.

An custom AI’s creator can see how much positive feedback the AI’s received in the last 30 days. They won’t know that you sent feedback.

Note

  • Similar to other chats, interactions with AI are subject to our Community Standards and Terms of Service.

  • An AI’s response may be inaccurate or inappropriate and should not be used to make important decisions.

  • Meta uses your interactions with AIs to improve AI at Meta. If the AIs cannot answer your query, Meta shares the messages you send to AI and general information, like your region, with select partners so you can get better results. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service to learn more.

  • Meta AI uses your location information to give you more relevant responses. Your location information is based on things like the settings you’ve chosen on your device, or your activity across our products. Learn more about how to manage your location in the Privacy Center.

  • Other information from your profile such as your age and gender, and interests based on your activity across our products, such as the types of content, including ads, you view or interact with and how you interact with it, will be used to help personalize your interactions with AI. Learn more about how Meta uses this information in the Privacy Center. You can also see how information is used across your accounts in the same Accounts Center and export your information. Learn how to Export a copy of your information.

  • Depending on your prompt, the content generated may go against our Community Standards or Terms of Service of Meta’s platforms. Sharing AI-generated content on our platforms that go against these standards will be treated the same as sharing other content that go against our standards. If you share generated content that goes against our standards, your content may be removed and your account may be restricted or disabled. Learn more about the Community Standards and Terms of Service on:

    • Facebook, Messenger and Instagram
    • WhatsApp

  • Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products can be used to personalize content and ads.

  • People who create an AI in Meta AI Studio do not have access to the chats other people have with that AI, unless they’re a creator using an AI based on themselves to respond to their personal messages. Learn more about AI auto replies.

  • Custom AIs are not licensed professionals or experts trained to help people. Chats with custom AIs can’t replace professional advice. You shouldn’t rely on AI chats for medical, psychological, financial, legal or any other type of professional advice. Visit our Meta AI Terms of Service for appropriate ways to use AIs for self-help or other purposes.

Learn more about how Meta uses information for generative AI models.

Note: Information about your device and Instagram account related to the issue you’re reporting will be automatically included in this report in order to help us understand and resolve the error, flaw, failure or other issue reported.

You can further help us fix this problem by tapping Include Complete Logs and Diagnostics when you send your report. This includes information such as user activity logs, network logs, crash logs and memory dumps associated with the user’s account. You may also choose to attach a bug description, screenshot, or video in your report. Please do not attach any unnecessary or irrelevant content in your report.

We will store the information in your report and other reports like it only for as long as required to resolve the issue you are reporting. We will not use the information in your report for other purposes. Your information may be transferred to and processed in the United States. Report a Threads user under the minimum age

How do I report underage user?

How do I delete underage account?

What is Threads minimum age?

I have a different question

The minimum age to use Threads varies by region. Most countries and states require you to be at least 13 years old to use Threads. Some countries and states have different minimum age requirements:

  • South Korea: 14 years old.
  • Quebec, Canada: 14 years old.
  • Spain: 14 years old.
  • Florida, USA: 14 years old.
  • Australia: 16 years old

In some regions, you may be required to confirm your age before you can use, or continue to use, Threads.

If you’d like to report an account belonging to someone under the minimum age to use Threads, or if you believe someone is impersonating your child who is under the minimum age, please fill out this form. We will delete the account if we can’t verify that the account is managed by someone who is old enough to use Threads.

Accounts that represent someone under the minimum age must clearly state in the account’s bio that the account is managed by a parent or manager, and provide identification to prove the account is run by an adult if requested. If your child is younger than the minimum age in your region and has an account that isn’t managed by you or a manager, the account will be deleted. If your child created an account on Threads, you can show them how to delete their account.

We ask for and use age-related information from people using our platform for age verification and other purposes, including to help ensure compliance with our Terms of Service. These initiatives are part of our efforts to promote safety, security and integrity. Learn more about how we work to keep Meta a safe place for everyone.

I have a different question

We ask that all people follow our Community Standards and Terms of Use. If your teen encounters someone on Instagram who’s not following these standards or Terms, they can report that person’s posts directly from Instagram.

People can report abusive behavior or posts with our built-in reporting. This includes nude photos, abuse and excessive spam. Reporting is totally anonymous. No information about the reporter is sent to the person whose account or photo has been reported.

Report a photo
  1. Click Options above the post.
  2. Click Report.
  3. Follow the on-screen steps.
Report a comment
  1. Hover your cursor over the comment you want to report, then click Options.
  2. Click Report.

Please also talk to your kids and educate them about internet safety. If they’re experiencing abuse from other people on Instagram, ask them to use blocking and our privacy settings.

There are also lots of great online resources with more information for parents on bullying:

  • connectsafely.org
  • stopbullyingnow.hrsa.gov
  • ncpc.org/cyberbullying
  • cyberbullying.us

It’s important to note that if your teen is a victim of abusive behavior on our service, we’re unable to provide non-public information (like the offending person’s email address) without a search warrant or subpoena from law enforcement. If there’s an emergency, we suggest contacting your local police department. Get more information about law enforcement.

I have a different question

Instagram takes safety seriously. If you notice an Instagram or Threads account pretending to be you or someone you know, you can report it to us in the Instagram app.

If you’re being impersonated on Instagram or Threads but don’t have an Instagram or Threads account, you can contact Meta for support.

Note: We offer an impersonation protection benefit for Meta Verified subscribers.

When to report an imposter account

You can report an impostor account if it’s pretending to be:

  • You
  • Someone you follow
  • A celebrity or public figure
  • A business or organization

If the impostor account is impersonating someone you’re authorized to represent (example: your child), you can report the account by contacting Meta.

You can only report an account for impersonating someone or something, but not for misrepresenting itself. Learn more about other types of reports.

Report someone for impersonation
  1. Click or tap their username from their Feed or story post, or click or tap Search and search their username to go to their profile.
  2. Click or tap Options next to their username.
  3. Click or tap Report, then click or tap Report Account.
  4. Click or tap It’s pretending to be someone else.
  5. Select the type of impersonation and follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep in mind that your report is anonymous, except if you’re reporting an intellectual property infringement. The account you reported won’t see who reported them.

  • Quebec, Canada: 14 years old.
  • Spain: 14 years old.
  • Florida, USA: 14 years old.
  • Australia: 16 years old

In some regions, you may be required to confirm your age before you can use, or continue to use, Instagram.

If you’d like to report an account belonging to someone under the minimum age to use Instagram, or if you believe someone is impersonating your child who is under the minimum age, please fill out this form. We will delete the account if we can’t verify that the account is managed by someone who is old enough to use Instagram.

Accounts that represent someone under the minimum age must clearly state in the account’s bio that the account is managed by a parent or manager, and provide identification to prove the account is run by an adult if requested. If your child is younger than the minimum age in your region and has an account that isn’t managed by you or a manager, the account will be deleted. If your child created an account on Instagram, you can show them how to delete their account.

We ask for and use age-related information from people using our platform for age verification and other purposes, including to help ensure compliance with our Terms of Service. These initiatives are part of our efforts to promote safety, security and integrity. Learn more about how we work to keep Meta a safe place for everyone.

Convicted sex offenders aren’t allowed to use Instagram. If you’ve seen an account that may belong to a convicted sex offender, please report it to us.

Please provide one of the following with your report:

  • A link to a listing in a national sex offender registry
  • A link to an online news article
  • A link to a court document

If you aren’t able to include this with your report, we recommend that you ask a local law enforcement representative to contact us so we can take action on your report.

Once we’re able to verify someone’s status as a sex offender, we’ll immediately disable their account.

In the case that you are an authorized representative submitting a report, we provide the name of the organization or client that owns the right in question. What happens if I restrict?

I can’t restrict someone

I have a different question

There are multiple ways you can restrict someone on Instagram. If you restrict someone:

  • They won’t be able to see when you’re online or if you’ve read their messages.
  • Their new comments on your posts will only be visible to that person, and you can choose to see the comment by tapping See comment. If you want others to be able to see their comment, you can tap Approve, then tap Approve to confirm, or you can delete it or ignore it.
  • You won’t receive any notifications for future comments from that person.

Note: You can also restrict multiple people from your comments.

If you feel like you’re being harassed, you can also temporarily limit unwanted comments on your posts from groups of accounts.

Restrict or unrestrict someone through messages

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Messages at the bottom.
  2. Tap the chat with the person you want to restrict.
  3. Tap the person’s name at the top of your chat.
  4. Tap Options in the top right, then tap Restrict.
  5. Tap Restrict to confirm.

Instagram app for iPad

Instagram Lite app for Android

Keep in mind that:

  • Your chat with the restricted person will move from your main Direct inbox to Message Requests, and future messages from people that you’ve restricted will automatically move to Message Requests.
  • You’ll be able to see the person’s message without the person knowing that you’ve seen it. You can then choose to delete the message or block or unrestrict the person.
  • If you’re in a group chat with someone that you’ve restricted, you’ll get a warning that you’ll see a restricted account’s messages. You can choose to stay or leave the group.
Restrict or unrestrict someone through a comment

Instagram app

  1. Go to your post and tap Comments to view the comments.
  2. Tap and hold the comment.
  3. Tap Restrict account or Unrestrict account.

If a restricted person comments on your post, you can tap See comment to reveal what the comment says, or you can tap Delete to delete the comment. If you tapped See comment, you can tap Approve, then tap Approve to make the comment visible to others, or you can tap Delete to delete the comment.

Keep in mind that you won’t receive notifications for any future comments made by someone that you’ve restricted.

Restrict or unrestrict someone through settings

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below How others can interact with you, tap Restricted.
  4. Tap Next.
  5. Search for the account you’d like to restrict and tap Restrict next to their username, or tap Unrestrict to unrestrict someone.

Instagram app for iPad

Instagram Lite app for Android

Instagram.com from your computer

Keep in mind that if you’re using the Instagram Lite app, you can only restrict someone through their profile.

Restrict or unrestrict someone through their profile

Instagram app

  1. Tap their username from their Feed or story post, or tap Search and type their username to go to their profile.
  2. Tap Options (iPhone and iPad) or Options (Android) in the top right.
  3. Tap Restrict to restrict their account or tap Unrestrict to unrestrict their account.

Hidden Words preferences for spam are not currently supported on web browsers or Meta Quest.

Message requests that may be offensive, unwanted, contain spam or are hidden based on your Hidden Words preferences will appear in a separate Spam folder. You won’t receive notifications for spam.

Manage spam

To manage spam:

  1. Click Messages on the left.
  2. Click requests next to Messages in the top left, then click Spam.
  3. Click Delete all at the bottom to delete all hidden message requests or click the message thread you want to open.

Ways to increase safety on Instagram

Make my account private

Block someone on Instagram

Report a post or profile

Hide offensive comments

I have a different question

If you’ve navigated to this page, it’s likely that you’ve had a negative experience on Instagram. We understand that it can be frustrating when online interactions become difficult. You may have had an argument with someone else on Instagram or come across posts that you find offensive.

We care about your safety and want to help you have more control over the content and accounts you see and the interactions you have on Instagram.

We already take steps to make Instagram safe, like:

  • Removing content that goes against our Community Standards.
  • Making content and accounts that go against our Recommendation Guidelines, but don’t go against Community Standards, harder to find in Explore and hashtag pages.
  • Adding a warning screen to photos and videos that contain sensitive or graphic content to let people know about the content before they view it. This warning appears when viewing a post in Feed or on someone’s profile.

You can also control some of your experiences on Instagram by using different features and settings like:

  • Setting your account to private so that only the followers you approve can see what you share on Instagram.
  • Using the Sensitive Content Control to choose how much content you see in Explore, Search, Reels, Accounts You Might Follow and Recommendations in your feed that you might find upsetting or offensive. Note: Teens under 18 have a different Content setting for their Teen Account.
  • Unfollowing or blocking someone who’s sharing photos or videos that make you uncomfortable.
  • Restricting someone so their comments on your posts aren’t visible to others on Instagram.
  • Temporarily limiting unwanted comments and messages from accounts that aren’t following you.
  • Hiding potentially offensive comments and message requests you don’t want to see.
  • Reporting posts, profiles, and comments that you think go against our Community Standards. Keep in mind that your report is anonymous, except if you’re reporting an intellectual property infringement. The account you reported won’t see who reported them.

Request another review

What are Community Guidelines?

Appeal to Oversight Board

I have a different question

When you report a piece of content (example: post, comment, story) to us, we will take action to hide or remove that content from Instagram if we find that it goes against our Community Guidelines. Our Community Guidelines define what is and isn’t allowed on Instagram, and they apply all over the world. They’re designed to encourage expression and create a safe environment on Instagram.

After you report a piece of content to us, you’ll receive a notification in your Support requests, where you can check the status of something you’ve reported to us. After we review the content we’ll let you know whether it did or did not go against our Community Guidelines.

Even if we don’t remove the content or profile you reported, we understand that you likely want to see less of this type of content on Instagram. We may use your report to make content similar to what you reported appear lower in your feed or in the recommendations we make for you, like Suggested Posts and Explore.

What if you disagree with Instagram’s decision about content you’ve reported

Instagram will remove content when we find it goes against our Community Guidelines. If you reported content from others but we find the content doesn’t go against our Community Guidelines, we’ll let you know. At that time, if you disagree with our decision to leave the content up, we usually offer the chance to request another review. When you request a review, we’ll revisit the content and review it once more. For some types of content, you can’t request a review, but we’re adding more options.

To request a review of the content you reported:

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Below More info and support, tap Help.
  4. Tap Reports and violations, then tap Reports.
  5. Open the update we sent you about our decision.
  6. Tap See report details.
  7. Tap Request review, then tap Continue.
  8. Tap Continue again, then tap Submit request.

Once you ask us to take another look, your content will be reviewed again by Instagram, usually within 24 hours. If we find we’ve made a mistake, we’ll let you know, and the content your reported will be removed.

If you’ve requested another review and we uphold our decision for the second time, you may be able to appeal to the Oversight Board. Keep in mind that not all decisions are eligible for appeal to the Oversight Board and the board only selects a certain number of eligible appeals, so they may not choose yours to review. You can read more about the board’s bylaws and structure on their website.

Why your account has been restricted for data scraping and what can you do

My account was restricted

What is data scraping?

Protect my account

I have a different question

Your account may have been restricted and flagged for further review because we may have detected activity that goes against our Terms of Use for accessing and collecting information in unauthorized ways, commonly known as data scraping.

What is data scraping

Data scraping is the automated access and collection of data from a website or app. Unauthorized scraping involves automation to collect information in violation of our Terms of Service. Unauthorized scraping is often done in a way that disguises the activity so that it blends in with ordinary usage.

Our Terms of Use don’t allow you to attempt to create accounts, access or collect information in unauthorized ways. We have teams dedicated to detecting, investigating and blocking patterns of behavior associated with scraping

There are several reasons our systems might detect suspicious behavior like data scraping from your Instagram account, such as:

  • Your account is automating access to, or collecting information in an automated way without our permission.
  • You may have provided your username and password to a third-party app or website (like apps that offer likes or followers on Instagram).
  • You used an app or service to interact with Instagram in unauthorized ways.
What can you do to protect yourself from unauthorized scraping

Because scrapers often target data that’s public, it’s important to make sure that your Instagram privacy settings align with what you want to share publicly. By default, your Instagram account is public and you can choose to make your account private at any time.

If you’re able to log into your account, there are several steps you can take to help make your account more secure, like:

  • Check your account’s recent login activity and remove any recent logins you don’t recognize.
  • Be careful before giving third party apps or websites access to your Instagram account. You can remove a suspicious third party app’s access to your account at any time.
  • Change your password whenever you see suspicious activity on your account. Doing so will log you out of all logged in devices, including any suspicious logins.
  • Pick a strong password. Use a combination of at least six numbers, letters and special characters (like !$@%), and try to avoid repetition.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication for additional account security.
  • Check your information on the independent website Have I been pwned to help you review your possible exposure in other data incidents. Learn more about the Have I been pwned website and its founders.
  • Learn more helpful tips about how to generally protect your information online on the Online security page provided by the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC).

About supervision on Threads

How do I set up supervision?

How do I set time limits?

How do I remove supervision?

What can parents see?

I have a different question

Supervision is a set of tools and insights that parents and guardians can use to help support their teens under 18 on Threads. Supervision is optional, and both the parent and the teen must agree to participate. It can be removed at any time by either person from the Family Center settings. The other person will be notified if you remove supervision.

When supervision is set up, in Family Center a parent and guardian can:

  • Set a time limit for how long their teen can use Threads. By default, we remind teens to close Threads after a set time each day. If Threads is used on multiple devices, time limits apply to the total time spent using Threads. Parents can choose whether their teen sees a reminder to close the app, or is blocked from using Threads after reaching the time limit.
  • Set up sleep mode to limit their teen’s use of Threads during select days and hours. By default, we remind teens to close Threads during nighttime hours. If Threads is used on multiple devices, sleep mode applies to Threads access across all devices. Parents can choose whether their teen sees a reminder to close the app, or is blocked from using Threads during sleep mode.
  • See the average amount of time their teen has spent on Threads across all devices over the past 7 days.
  • See how much time their teen has spent on Threads across all devices for each specific day over the past 7 days.
  • See their teen’s profile privacy setting.
  • See their teen’s content setting.
Supervision and Teen Accounts

With Teen Accounts, supervision also enables parents and guardians to view their Teen Account settings and approve or deny their requests to make their settings less protective. Parents and guardians can also set time limits to make other Teen Account settings even more protective.

Parents and guardians can also view and approve or deny their teen’s requests to make the following Teen Account settings less protective:

  • Their teen’s profile privacy setting.
  • Their teen’s content setting.
  • Their teen’s settings for who can tag or mention them.
  • Their teen’s Hidden Words settings, which hide potentially offensive comments and message requests. Note: This setting for message requests is not currently supported on web browsers or Meta Quest.
  • Their teen’s sleep mode setting.
  • Their teen’s daily time limit.

Teens 13-15 need to request parent or guardian approval to change their Teen Account settings to be less protective. Parents receive a notification when their teen requests to make changes to any of these settings.

With supervision set up, a teen can see a preview of what the parent sees while supervising.

Learn how to set up supervision.

Note: Supervision features require the latest version of the Threads app for iPhone and Android. The teen must update the Threads app. The parent must either update the Threads app, or visit www.threads.com using a desktop or mobile browser. If some features of supervision aren’t working appropriately, update the Threads app.

Privacy for teens

Teens aged 18 and older

Supervision will automatically end after a teen turns 18. Meta will send a reminder to the parent and teen as the teen approaches their 18th birthday.

If supervision is removed for a teen aged 13–15, their settings will return to the default teen safety settings.

Users under 13 aren’t allowed on Threads.

Note: It’s important that your supervisor is your parent or guardian, because they will be given controls and insights into your activity to help keep you safe. You can remove supervision at any time from the Family Center settings.

About Teen Accounts on Threads

Teen Accounts are for teens 13-17 and are automatically set to more protective settings. These settings aim to help keep teens safe on Threads by limiting unwanted contact, showing content that’s right for their age and helping them manage their time.

Teens under 16 need their parent’s or guardian’s permission if they wish to update their Teen Account settings to be less protective. Teens 16-17 can change these settings themselves, unless their Teen Account is supervised by a parent or guardian.

Supervision

A parent or guardian must supervise a Teen Account before they can:

  • Approve Teen Account setting changes.
  • Set controls, including time spent limits, for who can tag the teen and profile privacy settings.
  • View insights reports, such as average time spent on Threads across devices.

Learn how to set up supervision on Threads.

Teen Account settings
  • Private profiles: When teens 13-17 sign up for a Threads profile, it will be set to private by default. Teens under 16 will need their parent’s or guardian’s permission to switch their profiles to public. Teens 16-17 can change their profiles to public without permission, unless they have set up supervision with their parent or guardian.
  • Tags and mentions: Teen Accounts are automatically set to only allow tags and mentions by people who they follow.
  • Potentially offensive comments: Teen Accounts are automatically set to hide potentially offensive comments through the Hidden Words settings.
  • Sleep mode: Teen Accounts automatically have sleep mode turned on from 10PM to 7AM every day. During sleep mode, Threads notifications are muted, auto-replies to messages are turned on, and the teen will see a reminder to close Threads.
  • Daily time limits: Teen Accounts automatically get a reminder to close Threads after a total of 60 minutes is spent on the app each day.

If you’re a teen, learn more about managing your Teen Account settings. If you’re a parent, learn more about supporting your teen on Threads.

With supervision, a parent or guardian won’t be able to:

  • See their teen’s search history or chats (only profiles that your teen has chats with).
  • Post for them.
  • Reset their password.

Note: If you have a Teen Account and are over 18, you can edit your birthday in your settings. Learn more about editing or adding a birthday on Threads.

Change content setting

What is Limited content?

What is More content?

I have a different question

People ages 18 and older will be defaulted into the Standard setting for Sensitive content control.

Teens who tell us they are under 18 are automatically placed into Teen Accounts. You can manage the content and messages, profiles and comments you see on Instagram with your Teen Account content setting. The setting you choose impacts the content you may see from accounts you follow, as well as content on the explore page, search results, direct messages, reels, in-feed recommendations and more.

If you’re a teen under 18, you’ll be defaulted into the Ages 13+ content setting. This means we’ll try to hide more content that may be inappropriate for people under 18. For example, we’ll increase the strength of and expand the filters we use to hide certain content from teens. You also may not be able to message or see content from accounts that primarily share content that may be inappropriate for teens unless your content setting is More content.

Note: This setting doesn’t apply to all filtering we do. For example, you won’t be able to see content that is hidden for all Teen Accounts on Instagram. In addition, our AI experiences apply a default level of protection for all Teen Accounts. If you’re in the Limited Content setting, additional restrictions are applied to AI conversations, AI-generated images, and AI content in Reels.

There are three options for your content setting:

  • Limited content: Best if you prefer the most restrictive Instagram experience. You’ll see more limited content, you won’t be able to view, leave or receive comments and people won’t be able to @mention you. AI conversations, AI-generated images, and AI content in Reels will also be more restricted. You can change your setting to Limited content at any time.
  • Ages 13+: You’ll see content generally aligned with content ratings for ages 13+. Your ability to see or interact with some accounts will be limited.
  • More content: You may see more content generally aligned with content ratings for ages 18+. In the “More Content” setting we won’t apply stricter content filters and restrictions across Live, Comments, and Search that are part of the 13+ and Limited Content settings. You’ll need permission from your supervising parent or guardian to choose More content.

Note: Teens under 18 can view content from and chat with people over 18, as long as their content hasn’t been identified as inappropriate for people under 18. We have other protections in place, like hiding unwanted message requests to help keep teens safe.

To change your content setting to Limited content, or request permission to update this setting to More content:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. In Settings and activity, click Teen Account settings.
  3. Click What you can see.
  4. Click Content setting.
  5. To change your setting to Limited content, click Limited content and then click Confirm .
  6. To request to change your setting to More content, click More content, then click Confirm on the following screen, then click Send request or Add parent.

You can also find this content setting from your profile:

  1. From your profile, click in the top right corner and scroll down to What you see.
  2. Click Content preferences, then click Content setting.

Our Community Standards define what is and isn’t allowed on Instagram. These guidelines help us keep Instagram an authentic and safe place. If we’re made aware of a post that goes against our Community Standards, we’ll remove it from Instagram. The Teen Account content setting impacts how strongly and expansively we filter content that may go against our age-appropriate guidelines.

The following types of content are examples of what may be inappropriate for people under 18:

  • Suicide, Self-Injury, and Eating Disorders: We hide certain suicide and self-injury related content that we find, to help protect teens from potentially distressing or sensitive material. For example:
    • A post where someone is describing their own personal experiences with suicide, self-injury or eating disorders, except in the context of recovery.
    • A photo or video showing people in a hospital engaging in euthanasia or assisted suicide.
    • A Story where someone is talking about their own extreme weight loss behavior.
  • Restricted Goods and Services: We hide content that we find from teens that could influence them to engage in activities that are potentially harmful. For example:
    • A post offering to sell tobacco, nicotine products, alcohol, or firearms when shared by a legitimate brick-and-mortar business.
    • A Story encouraging people to take psychedelic drugs (also known as entheogens) or cannabis products.
    • Images with recipes for alcoholic drinks.
    • A post selling weight loss products or services.
  • Threatening and Graphic Content: We hide most graphic and disturbing imagery that we find from teens, even if we’d allow it behind a warning screen for adults. For example:
    • A photo of a severely burned person, which we’d cover with a warning screen for adults.
    • A photo or video of shootings, brutality, or deadly car crashes.
  • Nudity, Sexual Activity, and Sexually Explicit Language: We hide additional content that we find from teens that don’t contain explicit nudity or sexual activity but could be considered sexually suggestive. For example:
    • A post with near nudity such as nudity covered by digital overlay.
    • A photo zoomed in on someone’s buttocks.
    • A Story with sexually suggestive language describing sexual encounters, including the use of sexual metaphors

Learn more about how we help teens see age-appropriate content.

These features are only available in some regions. This article covers supervision of your teen’s Instagram profile.

Parents and guardians of teens under 18 can set up supervision on Instagram to help teens balance their time and provide support. The supervision features we provide everyone are optional—parents or teens can invite each other to set them up and can remove them at any time.

To set up supervision, you must be 18 or older, both you and your teen must agree to participate in supervision, and the teen you are supervising must be 13-17 years old, depending on where they live.

In some regions, laws give parents the right to set up extra supervision features. Parents can request to set up these features if their teen lives in one of these regions and meets the age requirements outlined in the law. Only parents can remove these features until a teen turns 18 (or the relevant age in their region), at which point they’ll automatically be removed.

Setting up extra supervision features

If your teen lives in one of the regions listed below, and they meet the age requirements outlined in the law, you can set up extra supervision features on Instagram by clicking the link under the relevant region. You can choose the app (Facebook and Messenger, Instagram or Meta Horizon) you’d like to use to supervise your teen.

You may be asked to verify your identity before you can invite your teen to set up extra supervision features. To do this, we’ll ask you to upload a valid government ID, or two forms of non-government IDs. Confirming your identity may take up to 48 hours. Your ID will be stored securely and deleted within 30 days after we’ve finished confirming your identity. It won’t be used for anything else, including ads. We might use trusted service providers to help review your information.

Once we’ve confirmed your identity, you can invite your teen to set up extra supervision features. They’ll be asked to confirm that you’re their parent or guardian before features are set up. If your teen doesn’t confirm that you’re their parent or guardian, or they don’t respond within 7 days, you can invite them again. If your teen remains unresponsive or doesn’t confirm, you can set up supervision features by providing us with more information like their birth certificate.

Using another Meta app to supervise on Instagram

You can use some other Meta apps (Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, Threads or Meta Horizon) to supervise your teen’s Instagram profile. When setting up, you’ll choose which app you’d like to receive notifications on. You can still use the other apps to manage supervision.

If you want to set up extra supervision for your teen’s profile on another Meta app, go to that app’s Help Center article for instructions:

  • Facebook
  • Threads
  • Messenger
  • Meta Horizon
Instagram supervision features available by region:

Florida

Connecticut

Puerto Rico

Indonesia

European Union

Vietnam

Brazil

Managing or removing supervision

Parents can manage supervision features, including removing supervision at any time. If you’ve added extra supervision features available under regional law, all features will be removed when you remove supervision. Extra supervision features provided in your region will automatically be removed when your teen turns 18 (or the relevant age in your region).

If your teen moves out of that region, we’ll remove extra supervision features. You’ll still be able to supervise your teen by seeing insights into their activity, setting time limits, responding to requests to change their Teen Account settings and more. We’ll notify you of any changes if this happens.

How ads are shown to teens

How ads are shown to adults

Adjust my ad preferences

I have a different question

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

We want to make sure everyone who uses Instagram sees ads that are appropriate and useful to them. All ads on our platforms must follow our Community Standards and Advertising Standards.

We have additional policies in place for ads shown to teens (people under 18 years old globally and under 20 in Thailand). For example, our Advertising Standards prohibit ads about restricted topics, like alcohol, financial products and weight loss products and services, to be shown to people under 18 (and older in certain countries).

Additionally, we limit the options advertisers can use to show ads to teens. For example, we don’t allow advertisers to select interests, behaviors, gender or activity on other apps and websites when choosing to show their ads to teens. Advertisers can decide to include teens in their audience based only on age and location.

In contrast, advertisers have more options for showing ads to adults who use our products. For example, an advertiser could choose to show their ads to people with certain interests or based on information that they, or other partners, share with us. This could include the products someone is interested in, interactions they have had with our AI products, websites they visited or accounts they interacted with on Instagram.

Since advertisers have more options when reaching adults, these audiences will have additional Ad settings to manage their personalized ads experience.

Learn how Instagram decides which ads to show you, and how to adjust your ad preferences.

For all account holders, no matter what your age, your use of Instagram is governed by our Terms of Use.

This feature is only available for parents and teens who are using supervision on Instagram.

If you reach your daily time limit on Instagram and need more time, you can request additional time from your parent.

If your parent gives you additional time, you can use that time throughout the day unless your account is blocked from using Instagram during sleep mode.

If your request is accepted, you can’t use your additional time:

  • During scheduled breaks
  • After midnight
Request additional time

You’ll see a screen that lets you know when you reach your daily time limit.

To request more time:

  1. Click More options.
  2. Click Ask for 15 more minutes, Ask for 30 more minutes or Ask to ignore limit for today.

If your parent doesn’t respond to your request, the request expires after midnight in your timezone.

Note: If your parent declines your request, you won’t be able to send another request for 15 minutes.

Setting up supervision on Instagram requires both a teen and their parent to agree to supervision. First, a teen or their parent sends an invite for supervision. Then, the invite must be accepted for supervision to start. Keep in mind, only one parent can be supervising a teen’s account.

To be supervised, teens must be 13-17, and the parent must be over 18 years old.

Sending invites

Teens or parents can send invites for supervision. Parents who want to supervise more than one teen can send the same invite to each teen they want to supervise.

Keep in mind, invites expire 7 days from the time they are first created. If the invite has expired, follow the steps to create a new invite again.

For Teens

For Teens

For Parents

Accepting invites

Supervision and multiple accounts or people

A parent can supervise more than one teen account, but they can only send one active invite link at a time. For security purposes, Instagram may limit the number of teen accounts that a parent account can supervise at any given time.

If the teen sends supervision invites to more than one person, the first person to accept will be the parent to supervise the teen’s account.

Blocked accounts

You can’t invite someone to supervise you if you have blocked them on Instagram. Learn how to unblock someone.

You can’t block your parent or teen’s account while using supervision with them. If you want to block them, you’ll need to remove supervision first.

Notifications

Parents and teens will get notifications in Activity on Instagram about supervision activity. If a parent or teen has turned on push notifications for Instagram, they may get push notifications as well.

If some features of supervision aren’t working appropriately, update the Threads app.

Daily time limits

You can limit the amount of time your teen can spend before they see a reminder to close Threads or are blocked from using Threads entirely. By default, we remind teens to close Threads after they spend 1 hour over the course of a day. Your teen will still be able to access their settings even if they’ve reached the time limit.

Your teen will be notified when you set or change a time limit.

To set up or change a time limit for your teen:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision for Teen Accounts. From here, you can see the profiles you supervise.
  3. Click a profile you supervise, then click Time management.
  4. Click on the amount of time below Daily limit, then select the amount of time you would like instead, and then click Save.

You can choose Remind teen to close Threads if you want your teen to see a reminder to close Threads but still be able to use it, or Block teen from Threads if you don’t want your teen to be able to use Threads after reaching their daily time limit.

Sleep mode

You can mute your teen’s notifications and remind them to close Threads during certain times of day and on certain days of the week with the sleep mode setting. You can also choose to block them from using Threads during the days and times you choose. By default, we remind teens to close Threads from 10 PM - 7AM every day.

Your teen will be notified when you set up a new time or day for sleep mode for their profile or if you turn off sleep mode.

To set up or adjust sleep mode for your teen’s profile:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision for Teen Accounts. From here, you can see the profiles you supervise.
  3. Click a profile you supervise, then click Time management.
  4. Click the preset time period or Off below Sleep mode.
  5. Click Set.

You can also choose whether your teen sees a reminder or is blocked from using Threads during sleep mode.

To choose what should happen during sleep mode:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision for Teen Accounts. From here, you can see the profiles you supervise.
  3. Click a profile you supervise, then click Time management.
  4. Below Sleep mode, you can choose Remind teen to close Threads if you want your teen to see a reminder to close Threads, but still be able to use it. Choose Block teen from Threads if you don’t want your teen to be able to use Threads during sleep mode.
Time spent

To view the total time your teen spent on Threads in the last 7 days:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision for Teen Accounts.
  3. Click your teen’s profile.
  4. Below Their time spent, you can see information about the time they’ve spent on Threads.

Below Time on Threads, you can see your teen’s daily average time spent on Threads for the past 7 days. You can also see how much time they spent on Threads each day of the past week. If Threads is used on multiple devices, you’ll see the total time spent using Threads.

Note: If your teen spends time in their settings or the Help Center, it won’t count toward their daily time limit but will appear in their total time spent, which may sometimes cause their total time spent to exceed their daily time limit.

To supervise your teen’s time spent on Instagram, you and your teen must have already set up supervision.

If supervision is set up, you can visit Family Center to view the accounts you supervise, and:

  • View how much time your teen has spent on Instagram across all devices over the past 7 days. If Instagram is used on multiple devices, you’ll see the total time spent using Instagram. You can see both an average amount of time spent per day and see how much time was spent on each specific day.
  • Set a daily time limit for how long your teen can use Instagram, and choose whether your teen sees a reminder to close the app or is blocked from using Instagram entirely. If Instagram is used on multiple devices, time limits apply to the total time spent using Instagram.
  • Set up days and times when your teen’s account will be in sleep mode. During sleep mode, your teen’s notifications will be muted and auto-replies to messages will be turned on. You can choose whether your teen sees a reminder to close the app or is blocked from using Instagram entirely during sleep mode. If Instagram is used on multiple devices, sleep mode will apply to all devices.

Note: Supervision features require the latest version of the Instagram app for iPhone and Android. The teen must update the Instagram app. The parent must either update the Instagram app, or visit www.instagram.com using a desktop or mobile browser. If some features of supervision aren’t working appropriately, update the Instagram app.

Daily Time Limits

You can limit the amount of time your teen can spend before they see a reminder to close Instagram or are blocked from using Instagram entirely. By default, we remind teens to close Instagram after they spend 1 hour over the course of a day. Your teen will still be able to access their Settings even if they’ve reached the time limit.

Your teen will be notified when you set or change a time limit.

To set up or change a time limit for your teen:

  1. Click More in the bottom left, then click Settings.
  2. Click Supervision for Teen Accounts. From here, you can see the accounts you supervise.
  3. Click a Teen Account you supervise, then click Time management.
  4. Click on the amount of time below Daily limit, then select the amount of time you would like instead, and then click Save.

You can choose Remind teen to close Instagram if you want your teen to see a reminder to close Instagram but still be able to use it, or Block teen from Instagram if you don’t want your teen to be able to use Instagram after reaching their daily time limit.

Requests for more time

When a teen reaches their daily time limit, they can request additional time on Instagram from their parent. The parent will receive a notification when the teen requests additional time.

If the parent gives their teen additional time, the teen can use that time throughout the day unless their account is blocked from using Instagram during sleep mode.

To decline your teen’s request for more time

Sleep mode

You can mute your teen’s notifications and remind them to close Instagram during certain times of day and on certain days of the week with the sleep mode setting. You can also choose to block them from using Instagram during the days and times you choose. By default, we remind teens to close Instagram from 10 PM - 7AM every day. Learn more about sleep mode.

Your teen will be notified when you set up a new time or day for sleep mode for their account or if you turn off sleep mode.

To set up or adjust sleep mode for your teen’s account:

  4. Click Time management.
  5. Click the preset time period or Off below Sleep mode.
  6. From here, you can click Toggle next to Sleep mode to turn sleep mode on or off for the teen’s account.
  7. Click Set.

You can also choose whether your teen sees a reminder or is blocked from using Instagram during sleep mode.

To choose what should happen during sleep mode:

  3. Click your teen’s account.

Time spent

To view the total time your teen spent on Instagram in the last 7 days:

Under Time on Instagram, you can see your teen’s daily average time spent on Instagram for the past 7 days. You can also see how much time they spent on Instagram each day of the past week. If Instagram is used on multiple devices, you’ll see the total time spent using Instagram.

Please note that if your teen spends time in their settings or the Help Center, it won’t count toward their daily time limit but will appear in their total time spent, which may sometimes cause their total time spent to exceed their daily time limit.

AI features on Instagram are being gradually introduced and may not be available to you yet. For the most up-to-date experience, make sure to install the latest version of the app.

You can use Meta AI in your chats on Instagram to help you:

  • Ask questions and get personalized suggestions. You can mention @Meta AI in a reply to a message. For example, in a group chat with your friends, you can reply with Meta AI to get dinner suggestions when someone mentions wanting Mexican food.
  • Summarize unread chats
  • Write or rephrase messages
  • Edit photos
Sharing with Meta AI on Instagram

When you or others use these AI features for messages or content in your chats, messages from the past 30 days are shared. This means people can share your messages and photos from chats with Meta AI.

Because others in your chats can share your messages and photos with Meta AI to use AI features, be mindful before sharing sensitive information in chats that you do not want AIs to use, such as passwords, financial information or other sensitive information. We take steps to try to remove certain personal identifiers from your messages that others share with Meta AI prior to improving AI at Meta.

If you don’t want others to share certain messages with Meta AI, you can delete the chat or delete the messages in the chat. You can also edit a message or delete information from the chat.

Build my creator AI

How creator AIs work

Delete my creator AI

I have a different question

This feature is being gradually introduced and may not be available to you yet.

This feature is only available on the Instagram mobile app.

With Meta AI Studio, you can create an AI that sounds like you, based on your Instagram content and information. Your AI can help you save time by engaging with more fans and connecting in a new way, starting with chats.

Once you create your AI, you can chat with it and ask questions you think your fans might ask to see how it responds. You can also add facts, links you’d like your AI to share and topics you’d like your AI to avoid.

When you’re ready, turn on AI auto replies so your AI can respond to messages from an audience you select. Once you turn on auto replies, people who you’ve included in your selected audience will also be able to look for your AI based on you in AI Studio. Learn more about AI auto replies for Instagram

How creator AIs work
  • Make it a true extension of you. Chat with your AI to see how it responds and make changes to help it sound more like you.
  • Open it up to your audience. When you’re ready, turn on AI auto replies so your AI can respond to messages from your selected audience.
  • Reach more of your fans. Your AI can answer common questions for you so you have time to connect with more people and your fans can get quicker responses.
Before you begin
  • You must have a professional account on Instagram.
  • You must agree to the Instagram Creator AI Terms.
How to build a creator AI

To build a creator AI for Instagram:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Professional dashboard.
  2. Under Your tools, tap See All and select Your AIs.
  3. Under Create an AI based on you, tap Try It.

Instagram will begin preparing your AI, which may take a few minutes. Your AI will continue to be prepared even if you navigate away from the screen or close the Instagram app. Once your AI is ready, it will show up in your inbox.

How to delete your creator AI

To delete your creator AI from Instagram:

  1. In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Professional dashboard.
  2. Under Your tools, tap Your AI.
  3. Tap the gear icon to access Your AI Settings.
  4. Tap Delete your AI.

You’ve now deleted your AI. You can always create an AI based on you again in your Professional dashboard.

Note: This will permanently delete your AI and all its information. This includes anything that was added or edited in your AI settings, as well as any feedback given on responses to chats.

Generative AI can create images, help brainstorm ideas, entertain people and more. By creating a custom AI on Instagram, you can define the personality of an AI for a specific purpose or style. Once you’ve created your AI, you can share it with other people on Instagram.

Learn more about how to chat with AIs, including AIs created by other people.

Create a custom AI
  1. Go to aistudio.instagram.com using a computer.
  2. Click Create an AI on the left.
  3. Click Get started. You’ll see examples of different AIs you can create.
  4. Click an example you’d like to use, or click Custom AI and type in a description.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Click the avatar you’d like to use.
    • You can click to generate new options, or click Edit Avatar to change the prompt used to generate options.
  7. Once you’re ready, click Create AI.
  8. Set your AI’s audience in the top right. Setting your AI’s audience doesn’t affect your account privacy. You can set the audience to:
    • Everyone - Everyone on Instagram can see your AI, see that you created it and use it as a template to create their own AI. You can also share your AI on your Instagram profile and to Messenger and WhatsApp by clicking Discoverability, then toggling where you want your AI to be seen.
    • Close Friends - Only your close friends on Instagram can see your AI and use it as a template to create their own AI. You can show your AI on your Instagram profile to your close friends by toggling Show in Instagram profile.
    • Only Me - Only you will be able to see and interact with your AI.
  9. When you’re ready to publish, click Done.

Your AI will be reviewed before people can chat with it. You’ll be notified when it’s available. Learn more about acceptable AIs.

I have a different question

Professional accounts on Instagram can be connected to a Facebook Page. When you connect a Facebook Page to your Instagram professional account, you can:

  • Run Instagram and Facebook ads from your Page. If you choose to advertise from your Facebook Page, you can reach more people with your ads because they can also run on Instagram. You can also integrate third-party apps.
  • Manage your messages. When you link Facebook and Instagram, you can manage comments and Instagram Direct messages from Inbox in Messenger or Meta Business Suite.
  • Gain access to cross-app tools. By linking Facebook and Instagram, you’ll gain access to tools such as appointment booking buttons, donation stickers and camera effects.
  • Promote your posts and stories. When your Page and professional account are linked, you can share posts on both platforms, or add to your Page’s story from Instagram.
  • Conveniently pay for promotions. By linking Facebook and Instagram, you’ll be able to use the payment method you use on Facebook on Instagram. You can also pay for promotions from the Instagram app, if that works better for your business.
  • Raise money for your nonprofit. If your nonprofit is enrolled and approved to use Facebook fundraising tools, you can add a support button to your nonprofit’s Instagram business account.

Note: In some cases, your active Meta Verified subscription may be canceled if you disconnect a subscribed Facebook Page and Instagram account.

What are creative optimizations?

How do optimizations work?

What is a caption card?

I have a different question

When you boost an Instagram post, it may be automatically eligible for creative and format optimizations to help your ad perform better. Instagram will determine which optimizations may increase the performance of the ad, as well as adjust your ad to your viewers’ preferences.

Note that not all variations are shown to your viewers. When your ad is delivered to people, they’ll see the version that they’re most likely to prefer. Therefore, two people with different preferences may not see the same version of your ad.

Currently, optimizations will only apply to the Instagram Stories placement. Possible optimizations include, but are not limited to, applying automatic Stories templates, adding a new card with your caption, showing the call-to-action in the center of the image towards the end of the ad, and varying your caption length. An ad may be eligible for any number of these optimizations. Learn more about each type of optimization and view visual examples below:

Automatic Stories templates

Instagram may automatically adjust your image using a set of templates designed to fit fullscreen vertical screens. To improve your ad performance, Instagram will determine which templates will likely work best for your ad and dynamically adjust to your audience preferences. See the example below for potential variations on your ad’s image:

Caption card

If your caption is longer than 100 characters, it may be placed on a second card to allow for a more interactive ad experience. In this case, the first card of your ad will display your image without the caption. Then, the second card will display the full text of your caption overlaid onto your image:

Call-to-action experience at the end of the ad

If your ad has a call-to-action, Instagram may display select ad elements, such as your account name, post-click destination information, and call-to-action button, in the center of your ad, if viewers reach the end of your ad.

Other optimizations

Instagram may apply other optimizations, including but not limited to:

  • Changing how the text appears in an ad to better suit the viewer’s device.
  • Varying the number of lines of text shown before people need to tap to see the rest.
  • Cropping an image or video automatically so it fits the fullscreen vertical format of Instagram Stories ads.
  • Showing text or additional creative across multiple cards to improve the way information is displayed. For example, we may include a snapshot of your Instagram profile to provide more information to viewers about your business or brand.
  • Automatically split video ads that are 10 seconds or longer into cards and tailor the number of cards displayed to viewers.

How identities show up?

Run ad from my account only

What is dynamic identity?

I have a different question

When you create a partnership ad, you can select up to 2 identities, or account handles, to show in the ad’s header. In Ads Manager, under Identities, here are the options for displaying accounts in your partnership ad:

  • Both advertiser and partner (creator): Run your ad from both your account and your partner’s. Consider using when you want to showcase your partnership or cross-promote both accounts.
  • Partner (creator) only: Run your ad from your partner’s account only. Your brand’s account will not show in the ad’s header. Consider using for campaigns when the partner is authentically promoting their use of a product or service.
  • Dynamic identity: This optimization allows our system to select whether to feature both the advertiser and partner, or the partner’s account only in the ad’s header, depending on which option will drive the best results for your campaign objectives. As a best practice, we recommend leveraging dynamic identity optimization.

Note: Regardless of which identity is selected in the header, ranking will use signals from both accounts.

How identities show up in partnership ads

A maximum of 2 identities can be displayed in a partnership ad. This means that if 3 accounts have collaborated on a post, and want to boost it as a partnership ad, one of the collaborators will not have their identity in the ad header.

The first identity in the ad has to be the Instagram account that authored the post. If the partner authored the post, they will appear first on the ad.

If the advertiser authored the post, they will appear first on the ad, even in the case that the brand is boosting the post in Ads Manager. In that case, the partner would be the second identity.

Ad previews will reflect your header format selection.

General insights

Total Followers

The total number of followers for this account.

Accounts Engaged

The number of accounts that have interacted with this account’s content, including in ads, in the last 30 days. Content includes posts, stories, reels, videos and live videos. Interactions can include actions such as likes, saves, comments, shares or replies.

Accounts Reached

The number of unique accounts that have seen this account’s content, at least once, including in ads in the last 30 days. Content includes posts, stories, reels, videos and live videos. Reach is different from impressions, which may include multiple views of this content by the same accounts.

Badges

Content
