Certain messaging-related metrics, ad campaigns and organic messaging features for businesses and ads delivered to and from Europe and Japan will be unavailable.

If you have a public account on Instagram, you can use free insights to learn more about overall trends across your followers and your content’s performance with your audience. You can also view insights for specific posts, stories, reels, and live videos you’ve created to see how each one performed and how people engaged with them.

From the Instagram app, you can see an insights overview that includes Views, Interactions, New followers, and Content you shared. You can also view Account and Content insights overviews on instagram.com. Learn how to view account and content insights on Instagram.

Tap each insight to see more detailed metrics, and tap the (i) in the top right corner to see definitions for each metric. You can also tap the dropdown menu at the top of the screen to select a preset or custom timeframe, within the past 90 days, for when to view insights.

You can also tap View insights under individual posts and reels, or open your stories and Instagram live videos and swipe up or tap to view insights specific to that content, including:

  • Views
  • Accounts reached
  • Interactions
  • Accounts engaged

When you boost content on Instagram, you’ll also have access to ad insights, where you can see these metrics for your ad and additional insights like ad goal results, cost per ad goal, or spend.

Note: Boosting content on Instagram is only available to professional (business or creator) accounts.

Available insights for your account and content

View some of the insight names and definitions available for public accounts on Instagram:

  • Views: The number of times your content was played or displayed. Content includes reels, posts, stories, live videos and ads. Note: This metric is being gradually introduced and may not be available to you yet.
  • Accounts reached: The number of unique accounts that have seen your content on screen at least once and demographic information on the accounts you’ve reached, including top countries, top cities, top age ranges and gender breakdown.
    • Audience demographics are available based on accounts reached data. To view audience demographics, use preset timeframes and reach over 100 accounts. If you can’t see audience demographics for Last 7 days, you can try choosing a longer preset timeframe such as Last 30 days, Previous month or Last 90 days.
    • For reels, accounts reached is the number of unique accounts that have seen your reel on screen at least once, whether or not your reel was played. Accounts reached is different from views, which may include multiple views of your reel by the same accounts. Note: These metrics are estimated and in-development.
  • Interactions: The number of actions people take when they engage with your content, such as likes, comments, saves and shares.
  • Accounts engaged: The number of unique accounts that have interacted with your content and demographic information on the accounts you’ve engaged, including top countries, top cities, top age ranges and gender breakdown.
    • Audience demographics are available based on accounts engaged data. To view audience demographics, use preset timeframes and engage over 100 accounts. If you can’t see audience demographics for the last 7 days, you can try choosing a longer preset timeframe such as Last 30 days, Previous month or Last 90 days.
    • For posts, stories and Instagram Live, you can see the Accounts engaged metric broken down into followers and non-followers.
      Note: These metrics are estimated and in-development.
  • Total followers: View trends across your followers when you have at least 100 followers. These insights include:
    • Growth (number of followers you’ve gained or lost)
    • Top locations of your followers
    • Age range
    • Times they’re most active on Instagram
  • Content you shared: The number of stories, reels or posts that you’ve posted for your selected preset or custom timeframe within the past 90 days. If you want to see all the posts, stories, videos, reels and live videos on your account, you can tap under each content type to go to the content library. Here, you can view and filter all your content by media type, reach, interactions and time frame.

About labeled state-controlled media on Instagram and Threads

What is state-controlled media?

How is state-controlled media identified?

Appeal a state-controlled media label

What is editorial independence?

I have a different question

Instagram defines “state-controlled media” as media outlets that Meta believes may be partially or wholly under the editorial control of their government, based on our own research and assessment against a set of criteria developed for this purpose. We hold these accounts to a higher standard of transparency because we believe they combine the influence of a media organization with the backing of a state.

Instagram seeks to identify these organizations by using our definition and standards to review the available information about their ownership, governance, sources of funding, and processes that may help to ensure editorial independence. As these organizations are identified, a label will appear under the person’s profile and under the About this Account section on Instagram and Threads. Labels will be applied on a rolling basis to organizations globally when we determine that publishers meet our criteria, outlined below, which we use to assess the likelihood that they may be under the partial or whole editorial control of their government.

We appreciate that not all organizations will agree with Instagram’s assessment. Organizations that believe they are mislabeled can submit an appeal. This appeals form can only be viewed by the account owner.

Note: We do not consider public media organizations that are publicly financed, retain a public service mission, and demonstrate independent editorial control to be state-controlled media under our definition and will not apply the label to these organizations at this time.

About less-personalized ads on Threads

How do I manage ads?

What information is used?

What are the limitations?

I have a different question

This option is only available in the European Region.

If you choose to use Meta Company Products free of charge with ads, you can manage whether you see personalized or less-personalized ads.

With less-personalized ads, you’ll have a different ad experience. You’ll see a variety of products and brands through ads that are less related to your interests. Your browsing may be paused by ad breaks. Your ability to advertise and monetize with ads will be limited. Learn more about these limitations.

We’ll use some of your information for ads:

  • How you engage with ads, such as clicking or liking them

  • Your age, the gender you provide and your location

  • Your device information, like the device or browser you’re using

  • Information about the content you’re viewing while you browse on our products

    • For example, Bente opens Instagram in the morning and she scrolls her Feed. She sees ads based on the content she’s viewing while she browses. This information is used to show her ads only while she’s browsing this time. When she opens Instagram again in the afternoon, she sees ads related to the content she’s viewing while she browses this time. Her ads are not based on the content she viewed while browsing last time.

You’ll also no longer have access to some Ad preferences that aren’t relevant to you, because we won’t use that information to show you ads.

Manage your ad experience

You can adjust your Ad experience setting in your Ad preferences to manage whether you see personalized or less-personalized ads. Learn how to manage your ad experience.

Boosting on Instagram

When you boost on Instagram, you can boost with a Meta Ad Account or without a Meta Ad Account.

Boosting with a Meta Ad Account

If you’ve already boosted posts on Instagram, you won’t experience any changes when boosting your Instagram posts or stories.

When boosting with a Meta Ad Account:

  • You can access your Facebook payment account and ad settings on Instagram when you connect both of your accounts.
  • You’ll be able to access other features of your ad account, such as your saved audiences. Note: Anyone who can log in to your Instagram professional account can use your ad account for ads and will have access to your payment information.

Boosting without a Meta Ad Account

You can create Instagram ads without having a presence on Facebook. If you are boosting a post from your Instagram professional account for the first time, you won’t have to connect to a Meta Ad Account or Facebook Page. Note: The ability to create Instagram ads without an ad account connection is limited to businesses who are boosting their Instagram posts for the first time.

When boosting without a Meta Ad Account:

  • You’ll need to enter your payment information the first time you boost on Instagram. You also won’t have access to some beneficial features and settings of your Ads Manager account, such as your saved audiences.
  • You’ll be able to manage your ad campaign and track ad performance on Instagram. You won’t need to manage your Instagram ads on Meta Ads Manager.

Even if you don’t connect your Meta Ad Account to your Instagram professional account, you can still create and use an ad account. Your ad account will remain separate from your Instagram professional account. You’ll be able to view and manage all Facebook ad campaigns on your ad account. You can view and manage all your Instagram campaigns on your Instagram account.

We recommend boosting with your Meta Ad Account. Note: You’ll need to log in to Facebook in order to boost with your ad account. Learn how to connect your Instagram professional account to a Meta Ad Account

How your information is used across Facebook and Instagram:

  • If you’ve added accounts to the same Accounts Center, your information from Facebook will still be used for purposes beyond boosting on Instagram, such as suggesting friends and cross-posting between apps. Learn more about how your information may be used across accounts
  • If you haven’t added accounts to the same Accounts Center, your information from Facebook will be used for the purpose of boosting on Instagram (in addition to the purposes described in Meta’s Data Policy).

How do I change political content control?

What is political content?

I have a different question

We may recommend political content from profiles people don’t already follow based on personalized signals. If you want to adjust how much political content you see from profiles you don’t follow, you can change your Political Content Control setting at any time. This control identifies whether content is political in nature but does not make determinations about political opinion.

Political content includes content that mentions:

  • Governments
  • Elections
  • Social topics
Change your Political Content Control setting
  1. Open the Threads app.
  2. Tap Profile in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right to access your settings.
  4. Tap Account, then tap Political content.
  5. Select your preferred suggested political content setting:
    • Next to Suggest political content, tap Toggle to see suggested political content, or tap Toggle to stop seeing suggested political content.

Switch to a professional account

What is a creator account?

What features do I get?

I have a different question

Professional accounts on Instagram can either be set to Business or Creator.

Business accounts are best for retailers, local businesses, brands, organizations and service providers. Creator accounts are best for public figures, content producers, artists and influencers. Setting up a professional business or creator account gives you access to features to help you grow your account, monetize, create ads, understand your growth, and manage your messages.

It’s recommended to connect your business Facebook Page with Instagram to get the most out of Instagram’s business tools. Learn more about connecting a Facebook Page to your Instagram professional account.

You can switch back to a personal account, or change your professional account type anytime. Changing your personal profile to a professional account will limit your ability to take certain actions on Instagram:

  • Professional accounts can’t be set to private. All pending follow requests will be automatically accepted when you go public. Learn more about the differences between public and private accounts on Instagram.
  • If you’ve linked a Facebook page to your professional account on Instagram, you’ll only be able to share your Instagram posts to Facebook through that page. You won’t be able to share to another Facebook page or to a Facebook profile.

When you set up a professional account on Instagram, you’ll have access to these features:

  • Professional dashboard: Track your performance, access and discover professional tools, and explore educational information curated by Instagram.
  • Monetization and ads: When you set up a professional account on Instagram, you can run ads from your Instagram professional account and use Meta tools to create ads that appear on both Instagram and Facebook.
  • Contact information: You can add a Contact button to your professional account that will appear near the top of the profile. You’ll be able to include directions, a phone number and an email address. Your contact information is displayed and you can edit this at any time. When you turn this feature on, your information can be seen by anyone who taps Contact.
  • Category label: Professional accounts show a category directly below the profile image. This category is the same as the category of your linked Facebook page. You can choose to display or hide your category label on your public profile after setup.
  • Insights: Insights provide information on who your followers are, when they’re online and more. View insights for specific posts you’ve created to see how each performed and how people are engaging with them. Understand what content helps grow your audience by mapping new and existing posts to net follower changes. Learn more about Instagram Insights.
  • Secondary inbox: You’ll have access to an inbox with Primary, General and Requests folders. You can use this inbox to organize your messages and control your notifications.
  • Ranked requests: You’ll be able to sort your requests by received date or by top accounts.
  • Manage followers: Protect your account from unwanted followers by reviewing potential spam follower requests and removing suspected spam and bot accounts from your followers.
  • Improved discovery: Your posts and reels may appear in search engine results so people outside of Instagram can discover your content more easily. Learn more about how posts and reels show up in search results, and how you can turn off this setting.

How do I reply to a thread?

How do I limit who can reply?

How do I attach media to a reply?

How do I delete my reply?

I have a different question

You can add to a discussion by replying to a post on Threads. When you reply to a post, your reply will appear as its own thread in the replies tab on your profile and people will be able to reply to it.

Note: If you have a public profile, anyone on or off Threads can see your replies. Learn more about the differences between public and private profiles.

Reply to a post
  1. Click below the post you want to reply to. Note: If you have a private profile and reply to someone you don’t follow, only that person can see your reply.
  2. Enter your reply.
  3. To choose who can reply to your thread, click Anyone can reply in the bottom left before posting your thread. You can limit who can reply to Profiles you follow or Mentioned only.
    • If you limit replies, your thread won’t be shared with your fediverse followers.
    • This setting is not available to private profiles replying to a person that doesn’t follow them.
  4. Click Post in the bottom right.
Keep in mind
  • If someone replies to you and you delete your post, their reply won’t be deleted. Note: If you reply to a post that has approvals on for replies, your reply will go into a queue to be approved by the poster.
  • If you have a private profile and reply to someone who doesn’t follow you, your reply will include in the top right to denote that only that person can see your reply.
  • If you’ve chosen for replies to your ghost post to be sent as a message to your inbox, only you can see those replies.
  • If you and the author of the post have both turned on sharing to the fediverse, a message will appear at the top, as you’re drafting your reply, to indicate that your reply to the post will be shared with users on other servers. Your replies won’t appear on other fediverse servers if the format of the post you’re replying to isn’t supported or the post limits who can reply to it.
  • If you have turned on sharing to the fediverse and someone from another fediverse server replies directly to your post, you’ll be able to see their reply on Threads. Note: Replies from other servers will appear on Threads after a short delay and currently can only be seen by the author of the post. Certain replies may not be visible on Threads for various reasons, such as the reply’s format being unsupported or for its non-compliance with our safety measures.
  • While you currently can’t share or reply back to replies you see on Threads from users on other fediverse servers, you can like their reply on Threads.

Learn how to edit your reply or like, quote, repost or share a thread.

About reuse of media on Threads

How do I manage media reuse?

How do I turn off media reuse?

How do I remove reused media?

How do I control who can reuse my media?

I have a different question

This feature currently isn’t available to everyone.

If you have a public profile, other Threads users may be able to create new posts that reuse your published media like photos or videos.

Your privacy settings determine default reuse settings

Your privacy settings determine the default reuse settings for your media.

  • If your profile is set to private: No one can reuse your media.
  • If you’re over 18 and your profile is public: Anyone on Threads can reuse your media.
You can control your media reuse settings

At any time, you can turn off or allow reuse of your media in settings. If you turn off reuse, any existing posts that reused your media before you changed your settings will still appear on Threads unless you delete your original post. This setting does not prevent people from reposting or quoting your posts.

Change your media reuse settings

  1. Open the Threads app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Account, then tap Media.
  5. Tap Toggle off or Toggle on next to Media reuse to turn media reuse on or off.

You can also prevent reuse of your media on specific posts by managing who can reply and quote your post, or by removing reused media from individual posts.

Remove media reuse for individual posts

  1. Tap Options next to a post that’s reused your media.
  2. Tap Remove quote to remove your media from the post.

Keep in mind

  • If a profile reuses your media, you’ll receive a notification in Activity Feed. Only public profiles can reuse your media.
  • If you delete your content, your post will also be removed from all posts that have reused your content.

Shops provide access to a set of features across Instagram that let people shop your photos and videos. It gives your business an immersive storefront for people to explore your best products.

When you set up a shop on Instagram, you’ll have access to seller tools such as:

  • Shops: A customizable digital storefront that lets people shop directly on business profiles. People can learn more about a business by tapping View Shop on the app to see the shop’s name, a featured image, customer ratings and the Follow and Shop all products action buttons.
  • Product tags: Tags that feature products from your catalog that can direct customers to purchase those products from your website. A tab in Explore lets people browse tagged shoppable content from brands and creators.
  • Collections: A set of products that businesses can curate for their shop to help customers find the products they love.
  • Product detail page: A product focused page that showcases relevant information of an item, such as pricing and product descriptions.
  • Ads with product tags: Businesses can create new ads with product tags or boost existing shopping posts in Ads Manager and the Instagram app, to increase the reach of their shoppable content. These ads drive conversions, link clicks and post engagement.
    Note:You don’t need a Shop to create ads with product tags or boost posts with product tags.

For creators on Instagram who have a merchandise provider:

  • Merchandise launches: If you have an account with a merchandise provider like Spring, Represent, Fanjoy or Universal Music Group, you can create a merchandise launch on Instagram to encourage shoppers to buy your products as soon as they become available.

Add shopping tags

Manage product tags

I have a different question

Shopping tags on Instagram feature products from your catalog, collections or promotions, and direct customers to purchase those products from your website or the Instagram app.

Shopping tags can be added to Instagram Reels, Stories, image and video posts. Businesses can grant permission for everyone or only approved branded content partners to tag products from their shop.

You can manage how people use your product tags on their Instagram posts by controlling who you allow to tag your products and removing tags from a feed post or Instagram story. By enabling people to tag products from your brand in their Instagram post or story, shoppers can find products more easily from people that they trust.

Note: While you’re no longer able to add product mentions and hyperlinks in captions and profiles, any product mentions in captions and profiles you’ve previously added will still appear. Hyperlinks that were added are removed. Learn how to add shopping tags to Instagram posts

For businesses, shopping tags are an opportunity to:

  • Drive increased distribution of your products when people tag products they love.
  • Encourage engagement with your community by allowing everyone to share what inspires them.
  • Help shoppers understand how products look in different styles by leveraging your community on Instagram.

You can also use a third-party platform to tag products in feed posts on Instagram, but you can’t add product tags on Instagram Stories, Reels and mentions. Contact your third-party platform directly with any issues, like if your post fails to publish or if it publishes without product tags. Learn how to import and manage items in your catalog from a partner platform.

We’ve implemented additional controls to protect the integrity of shopping on Instagram. While we encourage everyone to tag products, they must have an active account, be over the age of 18, and not have been reported for repeated Instagram policy violations. We’re also ensuring that people don’t interact with potentially harmful or duplicate catalogs by providing eligibility to businesses with a good account health status.

Signing up to Threads with your Facebook account helps unlock features that work across Threads and Facebook, like using the same login info to access both apps.

If you create a Threads profile with your Facebook account, we’ll combine your info across Threads and Facebook. Here’s what we’ll use it for:

  • If we show you ads, we’ll personalize them for you and others and measure how they perform. This means we do things like
    • Show you more relevant ads on Facebook and Threads based on your profile information and activity across accounts.
  • We’ll personalize content and suggestions for you and others. This means we do things like:
    • Recommend relevant content to you on Threads and Facebook.
    • Help organizations understand how people are engaging with their posts, videos and other content.
  • We’ll improve our products and provide optional activities that span across them. This means you can do things like:
    • Participate in surveys and other research about what you like about our products.

If you no longer want to use Threads with your Facebook account, you can delete your Threads profile. This will not delete your Facebook account.

Why you can’t sign up to Threads with your Facebook account

If you can’t sign up to Threads with a Facebook account, this may be because the Facebook app or the Threads app are not installed on the same device. You will need to have both apps installed on the same mobile device in order to sign up to Threads with your Facebook account.

Note: If you’ve already signed up to Threads with a Facebook account and no longer see the option to sign in with your Facebook account, this may be because the Facebook app has been removed from your mobile device.

About Threads

How do I start a thread?

How do I reply to a thread?

How do I create a Threads profile?

How do I deactivate my Threads profile?

I have a different question

Threads is an app from Instagram where you can view and share public conversations. Depending on how you use Threads, you can also post threads, reply to others and follow profiles you’re interested in. Threads and replies can include short pieces of text, links, photos, videos or any combination of them.

People can also follow you to see your threads and replies in their feeds and from your profile. Who can see your posts is determined by your profile’s privacy setting and other settings. People can reply to your posts to add to the discussion or like, share, quote or repost your content. Anyone who has an Instagram or Facebook account can create a Threads profile.

Start a thread

You can start a new thread and choose who can reply to it.

Learn how to start a new thread.

Reply to a thread

You can add to a discussion by replying to others. Your reply will appear in the thread and on your profile where people will be able to reply to it.

Who can see your posts is determined by your profile’s privacy setting. You can also like, share or repost a thread.

Learn how to reply to a thread and how to like, repost or share a thread.

How information from your Instagram or Facebook account is used on Threads

When you create a profile on Threads, it’ll be connected to the Instagram or Facebook account you logged in with.

We use your Instagram and Facebook information in accordance with Meta’s Privacy Policy and Threads Supplemental Privacy Policy to do things like import your profile information, personalize and improve your Threads experience, and help you stay safe. We use data from Threads to personalize and improve your experiences across Instagram or Facebook and to promote the safety and integrity of our services.

Data from your Instagram or Facebook account is used for Threads and can include:

  • Your login information
  • Your account ID
  • Your name and username
  • Your profile information like your profile picture and bio
  • Your connections
  • Your age
  • Your account status relating to intellectual property violations and instances of going against our Community Standards.

Note: Information relating to your Threads profile will be processed in accordance with Meta’s Privacy Policy and Threads Supplemental Privacy Policy. The Instagram Terms of Use and Threads Terms of Use apply to your use of Threads.

To adjust your Ad topic preferences

Instagram app for Android and iPhone

  4. Tap Customize ads.

  6. Below Ad topics advertisers can use to reach you, you’ll see topics that represent interest categories advertisers can use to reach you. We add you to these categories based on your activity.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try updating your app or go to accountscenter.instagram.com on your web browser.

On the Ad topics page, you’ll now see this topic under Your ad topic choices. You can change your preference at any time by selecting a topic and choosing No preference.

You can also browse for all ad topics and choose to see less of the ones you aren’t interested in by using the search bar at the top of the Ad topics page.

Note:

  • Your ad topic preference selections will apply across your Facebook and Instagram accounts if you have linked them. If you have not linked your accounts, you can learn how to update your ad topic settings for the ads you see on Facebook and on other Meta Company Products.
  • If you choose to see less of an ad topic, you won’t get as many ads about that topic, and advertisers can’t target you based on an interest in it. You may still see some ads related to these topics even if you chose to see less of them. If you do see an ad related to a topic that you chose to see fewer of, you can hide the ad and we’ll use your feedback to improve the relevance of the ads you see.

For teen users

On the Ad topics page, you’ll now see this topic under Your ad topic choices. You can change your preference at any time by selecting a topic and choosing No preference.

You may still see some ads related to these topics even if you chose to see less of them. I have a different question

In most regions, an Apple service fee of 30% of your total ad payment, before any taxes and local fees, may apply when you add available funds to your ad account in the Instagram iOS app. This fee is retained by Apple, not Instagram or Meta. Learn how to avoid the Apple service fee when boosting on Instagram.

When you set up a professional account on Instagram, you can run ads from your Instagram professional account and use Meta tools to create ads that appear on both Instagram and Facebook. Learn more about Meta Ad Account options for ads on Instagram

How to boost ads with a Meta Ad Account

To create ads on Instagram with a Meta Ad Account:

  1. On the Instagram app, go to your profile.

  2. Tap the post you’d like to boost.

  3. Below the post’s image, tap Boost.

  4. Next, you’ll be able to choose how you’d like to boost on Instagram. Select With a Facebook ad account.

  5. Tap Continue.

  6. Log in to your Facebook account, which should have Admin access to your ad account.

    • If you already have a Meta Ad Account associated with the Facebook account you’ve logged in with, you’ll be able to review the Facebook ad account you’re using.
    • If you’d like to use a different ad account than the one that is displayed, tap Change Facebook ad account to select a different Meta Ad Account. Tap Continue to use the payment method and ad settings from the selected ad account for your Instagram ads.

  8. Fill in the details of your ad by setting your Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next once you’ve completed these details.

  9. To complete your ad, tap Create ad below Review.

Once you’ve created your ad, your ad will be reviewed to ensure it meets our ad policies. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

When you’ve connected your Instagram and Meta Ad Account, you’ll have the option to confirm or change your payment details each time you boost on Instagram.

How to pause boosted ads before switching account types

If you decide to switch to a Meta Ad Account from a non-Meta Ad Account, you will lose access to the ads you’ve created with your non-Meta Ad Account and will be unable to pause any active ads. Before you switch, make sure you pause your ads with your non-Meta Ad Account first to avoid losing access.

To pause any active ads on the Instagram app:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap Professional dashboard.
  3. Under Your tools, tap Ad tools.
  4. Tap Edit on your currently running ad.
  5. Tap Pause ad.
  6. Tap Pause to confirm.
How to boost ads without a Meta Ad account

To create ads on Instagram without a Meta Ad Account:

  1. On the Instagram app, go to your profile.
  2. Tap the post you’d like to boost.
  3. Below the post’s image, tap Boost.
  4. Next, you’ll be able to choose how you’d like to boost on Instagram. Select Without a Facebook ad account.
  5. Fill in the details of your ad by setting your Goal (what results you’d like from this ad), Audience (who you want to reach), Budget (how much you want to spend daily) and Duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next once you’ve completed these details.
  6. To complete your ad, tap Create ad below Review.

Once you’ve created your ad, your ad will be reviewed to ensure it meets our ad policies. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

Can I still violate another person’s copyright on Instagram or Threads if I didn’t intend to infringe?

What is copyright infringement?

What is fair use?

Can I use copyrighted content?

What if I give credit?

I have a different question

It’s possible to infringe someone else’s copyright, even if you don’t intend to do so. In most cases, you shouldn’t use someone else’s copyrighted work if you don’t have permission.

Keep in mind that your use of someone else’s content may infringe their copyright, even if you:

  • Gave credit to the copyright owner
  • Included a disclaimer that you don’t intend to infringe copyright
  • Think that the use is a fair use
  • Didn’t intend to profit from it
  • Legally bought or downloaded the content (example: a copy of a DVD or a song from the Internet)
  • Modified the work or added your own original material to it
  • Found the content available on the internet
  • Recorded the content onto your own recording device (example: from a movie, concert or sporting event)
  • Saw that others have posted the same content as well

Learn more about copyright and what copyright laws protect.

Confirming your age on Threads

How do I confirm my age?

How do I appeal age deactivation?

How do I download my data?

How do I update my birthday?

I have a different question

In most regions, we require people to be at least 13 years old to sign up for Threads. In some regions, you may be required to confirm your age to continue using your account. You may also be required to verify your age to access certain features or to change your birthday on your account. You can confirm your age by providing your birthday, photo identification, and/or submitting a video selfie. You can learn more about confirming your age in Newsroom. If you need to confirm your age on Threads, you’ll be asked for additional information to help us verify your age.

We partner with Yoti, a third party age verification service, to confirm people’s ages on Threads. Yoti is verified by the Age Check Certification Scheme and is the leading age verification provider for several industries around the world including social media, gaming and age restricted e-commerce.

With Yoti, you can verify your age on Threads by taking a video selfie or uploading your ID.

The information provided in each age verification option is used to confirm your age and won’t be visible on your profile, to friends or other people on Threads.

You can review and edit your birthday in your settings.

If you have an account with Spring, a platform for designing products, you can import your products to manage a shop on Instagram from Meta.

With shops, you can display and sell products on Instagram from Meta. People who visit your shop can browse your products, make purchases, and get to know your brand.

Note: If you’re a business, you can set up a shop through Commerce Manager.

Before you begin

To manage a shop on Instagram from Meta with a Spring account:

  • Make sure you have a business account set up and select Creator in Business settings.
  • You must meet Commerce eligibility requirements.
  • If you don’t have a Spring account, you can create one in the Instagram App before you publish your shop.
Manage your shop

To connect your Spring store to your shop in the Instagram App:

  1. On your profile, select Add Shop.
    Note: You can also go to your account settings and choose Creator.
  2. Tap Get Started and choose Spring.
  3. Tap Next and log in to your Spring account.
  4. Complete the login process to connect your account and tap Create shop.
  5. Add products to your shop and then select Publish Shop so it becomes visible to your customers.
    Note: It may take up to 24 hours for your products to be imported. Digital goods can’t be sold at this time, so they won’t be imported.

You’ve now connected your Spring account to your shop. Next, you’ll want to:

  • Tag products in your Instagram posts
  • Set up a merchandise launch on Instagram from Meta, so people can learn more about your products.

If you don’t complete the steps to set up your shop, a banner will appear at the top of your profile to finish. You can also add your products and publish your shop when you tap View Shop at the top of your profile.

This feature is only available for business and creator accounts on Instagram.

This product or feature may not be available to you yet.

Campaigns make it easier to collaborate with creators on Creator Marketplace.

Note: If you decide to opt out of Creator Marketplace, you must not have any active campaigns and must make any pending project payments.

How to create a campaign

To create a campaign on Instagram’s creator marketplace:

  1. On Meta Business Suite, click Creator marketplace in the left hand navigation bar.
  2. Click Campaigns in the left hand toolbar.
  3. Click Create campaign in the top right.
  4. Select a campaign goal. Note: You can enter your own goal by selecting Other from the dropdown menu.
  5. Choose whether you would like your campaign to be discoverable by creators or invite-only.
  6. Toggle the Fixed offer button on if you would like your offer to be fixed, meaning that changes can’t be made to the content request or compensation.
  7. Click Next.
  8. Enter your campaign name, description and add a cover image that the creator will see when they receive your project details. Your cover image can help your campaign stand out and display what your brand style is. Then, click Next.
  9. If you made your project discoverable by creators, you’ll be able to narrow the creators you’d like to be able to apply. You can add specifications around gender, age, follower count and target audience. Then, click Next.
  10. Select your deliverables. You can choose:
    • The number of each type of content you would like created, choosing from Stories, Posts and Reels.
    • Any details about the content and the date you would like creators to register their interest in this campaign. Note: This date isn’t enforced by Meta.
    • The date range for the creators to post their content. Note: This date isn’t enforced by Meta.
  11. Click Next.
  12. Enter the compensation you’re offering for the project. You must offer a minimum of $100 as payment for content. This can include payment for the content and for permission to boost the ads, as well as any free product. Note: All payments are made off the Meta platform.
  13. Click Next.
  14. Review your campaign details and click Publish.

To edit your campaign name, goal, description and cover image, click on your campaign in the Campaigns tab. Then click Edit.

How to invite a creator to your branded content campaign

You can reach out to a creator directly through Creator Marketplace and invite them to collaborate on your campaign.

  1. On Meta Business Suite, click Creator marketplace in the navigation bar on the left.
  2. Click the Campaigns tab.
  3. Click on View creators for the campaign you would like to invite creators to.
  4. Click Invite creators in the top right of the campaign summary page. You will be able to invite creators from lists you have created.
  5. Click View list next to the saved list that includes the creator you’d like to invite.
  6. Click to check the box next to the creator you’d like to invite. When you’re ready, click Invite creator.

If you set your project to be discoverable by creators, you can also review creators who have expressed interest under Interested creators on the Campaigns summary page.

This feature is only available on the Instagram mobile app.

This feature is slowly rolling out to specific countries and may not be available to all advertisers yet.

Certain Messaging-related metrics, ad campaigns, and organic messaging features for businesses and ads delivered to and from Europe and Japan will be unavailable.

You can now create ads that deliver to Instagram and Facebook directly on the Instagram app. By selecting certain goals when you boost your Instagram post, you can enable it to deliver to Facebook placements as well.

Before you begin
  • You’ll need
    • an Instagram business or creator account
    • a Facebook personal account
    • a Facebook Page
  • You’ll need to create either an ad that clicks to WhatsApp or a lead ad if you’d like your ad to deliver to Facebook.
Create Instagram ads that deliver to Facebook

To create Instagram ads that deliver to Facebook:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Tap the post you’d like to boost.
  3. Below the post, tap Boost post.
  4. Below Goal, you have 3 options:
    1. To create an ad that clicks to WhatsApp:
      1. Select More messages.
      2. Tap Choose a messaging app.
      3. Select WhatsApp.
    2. To create a lead ad:
      1. Select More messages.
      2. Select More leads.
        • Note: This ad type may not be available to you right now.
    3. To create an ad that clicks to Instagram chat:
      1. Select More messages.
      2. The Facebook placement will be toggled on by default. Note: This ad type may not be available to you right now.
  5. Below Audience, tap to toggle on Allow Facebook placement.
  6. Continue creating your ad as usual, filling in details for audience (who you want to reach), budget (how much you want to spend daily) and duration (how long you want your ad to run). Tap Next once you’ve completed these details.
  7. To complete your ad, tap Boost post below Review.

Once you’ve tapped Boost post, your ad will be submitted for review to make sure it meets our ad policies. Your ad will begin running after it’s been reviewed and approved.

Available insights for Instagram ads that deliver to Facebook
  • When you create Instagram ads that deliver to Facebook, ad impressions insights won’t be available.
  • People reached, ad taps and your ad goal (leads or messages) include data from both Instagram and Facebook placements of your ad.
  • Some metrics may also be currently unavailable due to a lack of data to provide a value.

What happens if I delete?

Can I get my account back?

How do I cancel deletion?

How long does deletion take?

I have a different question

Threads in Accounts Center isn’t available everywhere.

When you delete your Threads account, your content, likes and followers will be permanently removed. If you’d just like to take a break, you can temporarily deactivate your account instead.

For security reasons, we can’t delete a Threads account for you. You’ll need to log into your account to request deletion. Before deleting your account, you may want to download a copy of your information.

Permanently delete your Threads account

Note: Deleting your Threads account won’t also delete your Instagram or Facebook account.

To request the permanent deletion of your Threads account:

  1. Open the Threads app.
  2. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Menu in the top right.
  4. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Personal details.
  5. Tap Account ownership and control, then tap Deactivation or deletion.
  6. Tap the account you’d like to permanently delete.
  7. Tap Delete account.
  8. Select the reason to delete your account, then tap Continue.

If you don’t have Threads in Accounts Center available yet, you can delete your Threads account by:

  1. Tap Profile or your profile picture in the bottom right to go to your profile.
  2. Tap Menu in the top right.
  3. Tap Account settings, then tap Personal details.
  4. Tap Deactivation or deletion.
  5. Tap the account you’d like to deactivate.
  6. Tap Delete profile at the bottom.
  7. Follow the prompts.

Your profile, content, likes and followers will be permanently deleted 30 days after your request is submitted, and you’ll no longer be able to retrieve your information. During the 30-day period, the content of your profile remains subject to Threads’ Terms of Use and Supplemental Privacy Policy and is not visible to other people using Threads.

You can cancel your Threads account deletion request before the 30-day deadline by logging back into your Threads profile and then tapping Log in to confirm the cancellation. After canceling your profile deletion request, your profile and its content will be visible again on Threads.

Note: The number of days that you can cancel an account deletion varies by region.

Keep in mind
  • After your Threads account is deleted, you will have to wait 90 days before you can sign up again with the same Instagram account.
  • If your account is removed for violating Community Standards, you may not be able to sign up again with the same Instagram or Facebook account.
  • It may take up to 90 days to complete the deletion process after it begins. Copies of your information may remain after the 90 days in backup storage that we use to recover in the event of a disaster, software error, or other data loss event. We may also keep your information for things like legal issues, terms violations, or harm prevention efforts. Learn more about how long we keep your information in Meta’s Privacy Policy.
  • If you’ve turned on sharing to the fediverse, we will turn off sharing to the fediverse from your Threads account and will request that other servers on the fediverse delete your Threads account and content from their servers. We cannot guarantee that they will delete your information, and it may remain publicly visible despite your decision to delete your Threads account. Note: If you decide to cancel your profile deletion request, you’ll need to wait 30 days from when your deletion request was submitted to turn on sharing again to the fediverse.

I have a different question

To increase transparency around the ads we show you about social issues, elections or politics, we have measures to help ensure the authenticity of these types of ads on Instagram. A social issue, electoral or political ad in feed or stories can be identified on Instagram by the Paid for by disclaimer.

We consider ads to be about social issues, elections or politics if:

  • They’re made by (or on behalf of), or about a candidate running for public office, a political figure, a political party or advocates for the outcome of an election to public office.
  • They’re about any election, referendum, or ballot initiative, including “go out and vote” or election campaigns.
  • They’re about social issues in the location where the ad is placed. Learn more about what we consider to be ads about social issues.
  • They’re regulated as political advertising.

Learn more about what’s considered an ad about social issues, elections or politics in our Business Help Center.

Please note, if you’re an advertiser looking to run ads about social issues, elections or politics, you’ll need to authorize your account and let us know the topic of the ads.

Reporting an ad about social issues, elections or politics

If you see an ad about social issues, elections or politics on Instagram that doesn’t have a disclaimer showing information about the organization or individual responsible for the ad, you can report it.

Report an ad
  1. Click Options in the top right of the ad.
  2. Click Report ad, then click It refers to a political candidate or issue.

Learn more about how to see fewer ads about social issues, elections or politics. Please note, the social issues, elections or politics topic preference is not available in every country.

What is GDPR?

How does GDPR affect ads?

What is Meta’s Data Policy?

I have a different question

Want to learn more about the information we receive and how it’s used? See our Data Policy.

The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) takes effect on May 25, 2018, and creates consistent data protection rules across Europe. It applies to companies (regardless of where they are based) who process personal data about individuals in the EU.

While many of the principles build on current EU data protection rules, the GDPR has a wider scope, more prescriptive standards and substantial fines. For example, it requires a higher standard of consent for using some types of data and broadens individuals’ rights with respect to accessing and porting their data.

Businesses who advertise with Instagram and the Facebook companies can continue to use our platforms and solutions in the same way they do today. Each company is responsible for ensuring their own compliance with the GDPR, just as they are responsible for compliance with the laws that apply to them today.

More information and frequently asked questions

For more information about specific ad products and frequently asked questions about the GDPR, visit our GDPR microsite.

How Instagram ads use machine learning

How do Instagram ads work?

What determines which ads I see?

How do I manage ad preferences?

Why am I seeing this ad?

I have a different question

To decide which ads to show you, we use advertisers’ audience selections and the results of our ad auction to determine the best ad to show you at a given point in time.

Our machine learning models are part of our ads delivery system that learns as it receives new information, without being explicitly programmed. This allows the machine learning models to carry out tasks quickly and efficiently, like delivering ads that might be relevant to you.

What determines which ads you see

The two main factors we use to determine which ads to show you are:

  • Advertiser audience selection
  • Results of our ad auction

During the ad auction our machine learning models calculate a “total value score” from three major factors: the advertiser bid, the estimated action rate and the ad quality score.

The ad with the highest total ad value is the one that is delivered to you.

Advertiser audience selection

When creating an ad campaign, advertisers first choose their desired audience through our business tools.

Advertisers can create audiences based on criteria like age, location, interests and categories. For example, some information you provide us, combined with actions you take, might suggest to us you’re interested in something, like cooking or fitness, or that you might be part of a larger group (called a category), like a mobile user.

Advertisers can also use information they have about their audiences, like a list of emails or people who’ve visited their website, to build a custom audience or a lookalike audience.

Note:

  • There are limits to how advertisers can reach young people (those under 18 years old globally or under 20 in Thailand).
  • When advertisers show ads about credit, employment or housing opportunities, we limit the categories they can choose to create an audience.
Ad auction

The second step we use is an ad auction to determine the best ads to show you at a given point in time.

Our system gathers ads for which you were included in the advertiser’s selected audience and moves them into the auction stage.

For ads that enter the auction, our system selects the top ads to show to you based on which ads have the highest total value score to make sure the winning ad maximizes value for both people and businesses. The total value score is a calculation that takes into account three major factors: the “advertisers bid”, the “estimated action rate” and the “overall ad quality.”

  • Advertiser bid. This is the bid placed by an advertiser for an ad. Because we use the total value score to determine the winner of the ad auction, an advertiser with the highest bid doesn’t always win the auction.
  • Estimated action rate. The estimated action rate is an estimate of how likely it is that you’ll take the advertiser’s desired action, like visiting the advertiser’s website or installing their app. To estimate this, our machine learning models may consider things like your activity on and off Meta technologies, as well as other factors.
  • Ad quality. The ad quality score is a measure of the quality of an ad. The ad quality score is determined by machine learning models and uses many sources including feedback of people viewing or hiding the ad, as well as assessments of low-quality attributes (like too much text in the ad’s image, sensationalized language or engagement bait).

The estimated action rate and ad quality help make sure that you see ads that are more relevant to you, even if that ad did not have the highest advertiser bid.

Note:

  • If an advertiser engages in clickbait and engagement bait, it does not improve the performance of their ad.
  • We may make adjustments that could affect auction outcomes and prices. Learn more about ad auctions adjustments.
How machine learning improves ad delivery

As more people view an ad, share feedback, or click through to make a purchase on an advertiser’s website, our models get better at predicting the estimated action rate and ad quality of an ad.

Ways to review and manage your privacy and ads on Instagram
  • Customize your Ad preferences to influence the ads you see. You can also update your Activity from other businesses settings to choose whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads. Note: You must be logged in to change your Ad preferences and Ad settings.
  • Hide an ad that isn’t interesting or useful to you or review how Instagram decides which ad to show you.
  • Update your visibility and walk through Security Checkup to make sure you’re sharing your information with who you want.
  • Export your Instagram information for review.
  • Learn more about why you’re seeing a particular ad with the “Why you’re seeing this ad” feature that helps you see more details about who the advertiser wants to reach and gives you access to the ad in Meta Ads Library. You can access this feature from the … menu on any ad you see on Instagram.

How Threads addresses false info

How does Threads reduce false info?

How do third-party fact-checkers work?

How do I report false information?

What happens to false information?

I have a different question

At Threads, we’re committed to reducing the spread of false information.

We use both technology and feedback from our community to identify posts and profiles that may contain false information. We also work with third-party fact-checkers across the globe who review content in over 60 languages and are certified through the non-partisan International Fact-Checking Network to help identify, review and rate false information.

Learn more about the global list of third-party fact checking organizations and their contact info in the Facebook Help Center.

Reducing the distribution of false information
  • Making false information harder to find: When third-party fact-checkers identify information that is false, partly false, altered, or missing context on Threads, we may make it harder to find by reducing or filtering it in your feed and search results.
  • Using technology to find the same false information: When a post is rated false, altered, partly false or missing context by third-party fact-checkers on Threads, Instagram or Facebook, we use image matching technology to find further instances of this content. We automatically label identical content if it is posted elsewhere on Threads, Instagram or Facebook.
  • Labeling posts with false information warnings: Posts that have been identified as false information by third-party fact-checkers are labeled so people can better decide for themselves what to read, trust and share. When a fact-checking label is applied, it appears to everyone around the world viewing that content. On Threads, the label can be seen on content from people you follow in feed, search and on their profiles. The label will link out to the rating from one or multiple fact-checkers and their article(s) that debunk the information in the post.
  • Removing content and profiles that go against Community Standards: When we find that a post or profile goes against our Community Standards, we remove it. We use the same guidelines each time we review whether something goes against our Community Standards. These standards apply to all types of content.
Giving you more tools to identify and give feedback on false information
  • Learn how to spot false information. Knowing what to look out for can help you make more informed decisions about what to read, trust and share.
  • Report posts you think contain false information. Let us know if you think a post is false. This is one of the signs we use when trying to identify false information.

Keep in mind that the original content of politicians is not sent to third-party fact-checkers for review. Learn more about our fact-checking policies.

How to appeal the removal of content on Instagram or Threads for copyright reasons

Appeal content removal

DMCA counter-notification

My appeal was rejected

I have a different question

If your content was removed because of a copyright report, you can submit an appeal or a DMCA counter-notification. You received instructions in the message we sent you.

If we have informed you that content you posted was removed under the notice and counter-notice procedures of the United States Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), you may be able to file a DMCA counter-notification. Learn more about DMCA counter-notifications.

If your content was removed because of a copyright report submitted outside the DMCA procedures, you can submit an appeal. Instructions about how to submit an appeal are included in the message we have sent you. If your account has been disabled, you can submit an appeal by logging into your account and following the on-screen instructions.

Once we are in receipt of a valid and adequately substantiated appeal, we will review it expeditiously. Appeals can often be resolved quickly when our requests for further information are responded to promptly, where the content in question is not infringing and does not violate our Terms of Service or Community Standards, or where the initial report was a mistake. Appeal decisions can take longer in circumstances where additional review or analysis by our teams is required.

If you are uncertain whether you should file an appeal or a DMCA counter-notification, you may want to seek legal advice. Please note that if your content was removed for reasons unrelated to a copyright report, you may not receive a response from us.

  2. Click Account status.

By checking your Account Status, you’ll be able to:

  • View any content (like posts and replies) that has been removed from your account for going against our Community Standards and may lead to your account being taken down by selecting Removed content.
  • View certain features on Threads that you can no longer use and take action to resolve the issue, such as appealing content that was removed for going against our Community Standards or not following our Terms of Use, by selecting Features you can’t use.
  • Request a review of our decision to remove your content if you don’t think Threads should have taken down your content by selecting Request a review.

If you repeatedly post content that is removed for going against our Community Standards, you may lose access to your account. Note: In most cases, you’ll get a warning before losing access to your account.

Learn more about how to request a review of our decision to remove your content.

I have a different question

Branded content ads are now called partnership ads.

We are rolling out a new recommended setup experience to the Traffic, Awareness and Engagement objectives which is similar to the Advantage+ campaign setup for the Sales, App promotion and Leads objectives.

You may see a campaign score of 100 and Advantage+ on for some options. Manual options are still available.

This means you may see slightly different steps to those described here for some objectives. Learn more.

Special ad category campaigns and pharmaceuticals campaigns may not have access to all Advantage+ features, or may see a different experience.

Partnership ads allow advertisers to run ads with partners: creators, brands, and other businesses. The partner and/or advertiser accounts are featured in the ad’s header and the ads leverage signals from both accounts for improved ranking and incremental performance. Learn more about partnership ads.

Note: If you are an advertiser that works with an agency to run partnership ads, then you’ll need to grant your agency permissions across your Instagram account, Facebook page, and ad account.

Before you begin
  • You must meet eligibility requirements for partnership ads and branded content.
  • The content you’re turning into a partnership ad must be in an eligible format.
  • We recommend that you link your Instagram and Facebook accounts.
  • Partnership ads are not the same as organic branded content. If you want to allow a partner to tag your account with the paid partnership label when they post organic branded content, you’ll need to grant them permission separately from partnership ads permissions. Learn more about branded content.
  • You’ll need to get partnership ads permissions from your partners. With account-level permissions, advertisers can create a partnership ad by boosting existing content or uploading new content in Ads Manager. If a partner grants content-level permissions to an advertiser by sharing an ad code, the advertiser will be able to boost that content into a partnership ad.
Create a partnership ad with an ad code

To create a partnership ad with an ad code or post info:

  1. Go to Ads Manager and click + Create.
  2. Select your ad objective. Learn more about supported objectives and placements for partnership ads.
  3. Complete the rest of the details of your ad, including conversion location, budget, schedule and audience. Then click Next.
  4. At the ad level, turn on the partnership ad toggle.
  5. Click Enter ad code or post info.
  6. You can paste your ad code, post ID or post URL. This will set the first identity of the partnership ad and will use the media associated with the code or post.
  7. Select the Second identity you’d like to appear in your ad’s header.
  8. Choose which partner identities to display in your ad: both identities, the first identity only in the header, or dynamic identity. If you choose dynamic identity, the option predicted to make the ad perform best will be automatically selected.
    Note: Dynamic identity is turned on by default. Both identities will be displayed for unsupported placements.
  9. Click Done.
  10. Finish setting up your ad and click Publish.
How to create a partnership ad without an ad code

To create a partnership ad without an ad code:

  1. Go to Ads Manager and click + Create.
  2. Select your ad objective. Learn more about supported objectives and placements for partnership ads.
  3. Complete the rest of the details of your ad, including conversion location, budget, schedule and audience. Then click Next.
  4. At the ad level, turn on the Partnership ad toggle.
  5. Go to Identities, then click Edit.
  6. Choose which partner identities to display in your partnership ad header: both identities, first identity only, or dynamic identity. If you choose dynamic identity, the ad header format will be automatically selected by what is predicted to perform best.
    Note: Dynamic identity is turned on by default. However, both identities will be displayed for unsupported placements.
  7. Click Save.

Continue with the next steps if you’re using an existing post or uploading new creative:

If you’re boosting an existing post into a partnership ad:

If you’re uploading new creative for your partnership ad:

Once you’ve created your ad, it will be reviewed by Meta and you’ll be notified when it’s been approved.

Note: You won’t be able to manage or delete likes and comments that appear on the boosted post until your partnership ad is live.

In most regions, an Apple service fee of 30% of your total ad payment, before any taxes and local fees, may apply when you add available funds to your ad account in the Instagram iOS app. This fee is retained by Apple, not Instagram or Meta. Learn how to avoid the Apple service fee when boosting on Instagram.

You can pay for ads from the Instagram app by adding a payment method or by adding money to your ad account’s available funds. You can also pay by linking a Facebook Page to your Instagram professional account and using your ad account.

Note: When you boost content on the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to pay with available funds. Learn how to add money to your ad account’s available balance. Available funds added through the iOS app will be charged through the Apple App Store, which retains a service fee on your total ad payment before applicable taxes and local fees. Applicable taxes and fees are not kept by Meta. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

Before you begin
  • You need to have a professional account to run ads on Instagram. Learn how to set up a professional (business or creator) account.
  • To pay for ads using your ad account, you’ll need to connect your Facebook Page and professional Instagram account.
  • If you don’t already have an ad account set up, one will be created when you add a payment method on Instagram.
  • To pay for ads from the Instagram iOS app, you’ll need to use available funds. To save money and avoid the Apple service fee, use instagram.com instead of the Instagram iOS app.

Note: If you change the primary payment method on your ad account, the change will apply to both Facebook and Instagram.

Add a payment method for your Instagram ads

To add a payment method for your Instagram ads from the Instagram app:

  1. Go to your profile and tap Menu in the top right.
  2. Below For professionals, tap Ads payments.
  3. Tap Billing & payments.
  4. From here, you can select a payment method that is linked from Facebook, or add another payment method such as PayPal, credit card, or debit card.

Once you complete these steps, your selected payment method will be added to your Instagram ad account and available for ad payments.

To add a payment method for your Instagram ads from your computer:

  1. Go to the left menu and click Dashboard.
  2. Click Billing & payments on the right, below Other tools.
  3. A new window will open in Ads Manager. You can select a payment method linked from Facebook, or add another payment method like PayPal, a credit card, or debit card.

Improve my AI responses

Add facts to my AI

Avoid certain topics

My AI isn’t responding

I have a different question

This feature is being gradually introduced and may not be available to you yet.

This feature is only available on the Instagram mobile app.

When you turn on AI auto replies for Instagram, you can choose which Instagram and Threads content your AI uses as a knowledge base for responses, add new facts and links for your AI to be able to share in messages, plus add topics you’d like your AI to try to avoid.

Note: Content and information you provide to help improve your AI must follow our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use.

Improving your creator AI through AI settings

You can help improve auto replies generated by your AI in your AI settings in a few ways:

Summary

Create a summary that may be used to inform how your AI responds. Your summary can be a brief description about yourself. Note: Only you can see this summary.

Instagram content

You can select the types of content you’d like to use to help your AI sound more like you. This includes content you’ve created in the past, and any content you create in the future, including:

  • Posts
  • Reels
  • Comments
  • Stories and highlights
  • Archived stories
  • Broadcast channels
  • Threads posts

Your information

  • Facts: You can add or edit facts about yourself that you want your AI to know, so it can more accurately respond to fans as you would.
  • Questions: You can quickly answer some questions to help your AI learn facts about you and how you might respond to help inform its own responses.

Topics to avoid

Adding topics to avoid allows you to specify topics, like keywords and phrases, that you don’t want your AI to engage with. Note: Your AI will do its best to avoid these topics, but it’s not guaranteed.

When adding your topic, you can also select your AI’s response style to a specific topic when you make any of these selections:

  • Redirect conversation: Have your AI gently change the subject.
  • Refuse to answer: Have your AI firmly hold the boundary and not engage with the topic.
  • No response: Your AI won’t respond.

Shareable links

You can add any links to content or products that you’d like your AI to be able to share in message replies. To add a shareable link, go to Your AI Settings and tap Shareable links. Tap Add to fill in the link details, including a more detailed description to help your AI share the link in the right context. Once you’re done, tap Save.

Improving your creator AI through chat

By chatting with your own AI, you can test how your AI responds and give feedback on individual responses. You can access your AI by going to your messages and choosing your Primary inbox. Tap on “AI · your name” to chat with your AI to see how it responds.

You can tap the thumbs up or thumbs down icon on any AI response to give feedback on individual responses. If you tap the thumbs down icon, you can choose to:

  • Have your AI avoid this topic: This option allows you to add a new topic for your AI to avoid in the future.
  • Make a correction: This option allows you to edit a response in a way that will help inform future responses.
  • Give feedback to Meta: This option allows you to send freeform feedback to the team at Meta. Adding feedback here won’t immediately influence your AI’s future responses in the way the first two options can.
Creator AI insights

You can access Your AI insights in your Professional dashboard by tapping Your AI. From here, you’ll be able to view these insights:

  • Accounts engaged: The number of Instagram accounts engaged by your AI.
  • AI messages sent: The number of AI messages sent.
  • Content shared by AI: The amount of content shared by AI (reels, posts, comments, stories, and threads you created which your AI shared in message replies).

You may also see the frequent topics or what people are talking about in your messages, including messages between your AI and your audience, and in comments on reels and posts.

Download Instagram insights report

What do report columns mean?

Understand product engagement

My report is missing data

I have a different question

In the Insights tab of Commerce Manager, you can download a detailed spreadsheet with insights for your shoppable Instagram posts and stories. This report can be used to understand how people are interacting and engaging with your products on Instagram. It shares the following information on posts and stories that you and your creators have shared.

CSV report columns

These are the definitions of each column that you may find in this report:

  • Account name: The account that posted the post or story.
  • Total impressions: The number of times a post or story was on screen.
  • Impressions from Feed: The number of impressions a post received when it was displayed on feed. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Impressions from Explore: The number of impressions a post received from Explore. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Impressions from profile: The number of impressions a post received from the profile of the account that posted it. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Impressions from hashtag: The number of impressions a post received from accounts that found the post or story through hashtags. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Impressions from location tags: The number of impressions a post received from accounts that found the post or story through a location tag. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Impressions from other sources: The number of impressions a post received from accounts that found the post or story through sources other than feed, Explore, profile, hashtags or location tags. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Reach: The number of unique accounts that have seen this post or story at least once. Reach is different from impressions, which can include multiple views by the same accounts. The reach metric is estimated.
  • Reach from non-followers: The number of unique accounts that have seen this post or story at least once and do not follow the account it was posted from. Reach is different from impressions, which can include multiple views by the same accounts. The reach metric is estimated.
  • Likes: The number of likes on a post. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Comments: The number of comments on a post. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Shares: The number of shares a post or story received.
  • Saves: The number of saves a post received. This metric is only available for posts.
  • Profile visits: The number of times your profile was viewed by someone who also viewed your post or story. This metric is only available for accounts you own, not accounts that you partner with.
  • Follows: The number of accounts that followed you after viewing your post or story. This metric is only available for accounts you own, not accounts that you partner with.
  • Forward taps: The number of times someone tapped forward to the next story. This metric is only available for stories.
  • Back taps: The number of times someone tapped back to the previous story. This metric is only available for stories.
  • Next story swipes: The number of times someone swiped to the next story in their feed. This metric is only available for stories.
  • Exit story taps: The number of times someone exited a story. This metric is only available for stories.
  • Product page views: The number of views your product detail pages received from all the product tags on a post or story.
  • Sticker taps: The number of taps on the location, hashtag, mention or product stickers on a photo or video. This metric is only available for stories.
  • Product page views per product tag: The number of views of a product detail page for each product tagged in a post or story.
  • Merchant tagged: The account tagged in a post or story.
  • Product tagged: The products tagged in a post or story.
  • Product group retailer ID for product tags: The product group retailer ID of the product tagged in a post or story.
  • Retailer ID for product tags: The retailer ID or SKU of the product tagged in a post or story.
